human.name: Humans
human.homelands: Everywhere; most of every realm except the elven, dwarven, orc and giant lands
human.life: life expectancy at birth about 36; those who reach 20 usually live to 55–65; the oldest reach 90–100
human.fert: about 4 births per woman on average (most 2–6); 2 or 3 survive to adulthood

elf.name: Elves
elf.homelands: The Evenwood (Sylvaran) and the Elder Coast (Eldergrove); small quarters in western human cities
elf.fert: 2–3 births per woman over 200 fertile years (about 2.5 on average)

dwarf.name: Dwarves
dwarf.homelands: Stonehold and Emberdeep (Worldspine), Irondeep (Iron Mountains); smith quarters in many human cities

orc.name: Orcs
orc.homelands: The Grass Sea (Horde of Gorath) and the Eastern Steppe (Tusk Clans); mercenaries everywhere
orc.fert: about 3 births per woman; twins in about 1 birth in 3, so about 4 children on average

giant.name: Giants
giant.homelands: Frostholm and the White Coast (Hrimfell); a few hundred scattered
giant.fert: 2–4 births per woman (about 3 on average); one every 6–8 years

halfelf.name: Half-elves
halfelf.homelands: Mostly Eldergrove, the western Sunlands and Ashmere
halfelf.adult: 20 by human law, 40 by elven law
halfelf.fert: fertile with humans and elves; low fertility, 1–2 children on average

halforc.name: Half-orcs
halforc.homelands: The steppe borders, the Sunlands' ports, mercenary companies

CUL-01.name: Solenfolk
CUL-01.note: Heirs of the Solen Empire; Old Solen is their church and law language.

CUL-02.name: Northfolk
CUL-02.home: The northern plains, the west coast, the Crown Highlands, the Rift Coast
CUL-02.note: Farmers and knights of the north; many local dialects of one tongue.

CUL-03.name: Wind Riders
CUL-03.note: Horse and camel herders; nine tribes.

CUL-04.name: Qadiri
CUL-04.note: Coastal gardeners and sailors of the Southland's north shore.

CUL-05.name: Sandfolk
CUL-05.note: Camel nomads who guide caravans and trade salt.

CUL-06.name: Tamari
CUL-06.note: River farmers of the Monuti valley and delta.

CUL-07.name: Sabrans
CUL-07.note: Merchants and divers of the lower Bahesh and the gulf.

CUL-08.name: Zanari
CUL-08.note: Farmers, herders and gold traders of the savanna.

CUL-11.name: Eastfolk
CUL-11.home: The Velgrad Uplands and the Lakeland
CUL-11.note: Forest farmers, river traders and fur hunters of the north-east.

CUL-12.name: Skyfolk
CUL-12.note: Herders and monks adapted to the thin air.

CUL-13.name: Ranpuri
CUL-13.note: Rice farmers of the monsoon plains.

CUL-14.name: Amberfolk
CUL-14.note: Island spice growers, pearl divers and sailors.

CUL-15.name: Corsairs
CUL-15.note: A mixed people of every coast; pirates and smugglers.

CUL-16.name: Leaf People
CUL-16.note: Small forest hunters (men about 145 cm); they avoid outsiders.

CUL-17.name: Cloudfolk
CUL-17.note: Hill tribes of Great Amber's interior.

CUL-18.name: Marchfolk
CUL-18.note: Settlers, runaways and outlaws from every nearby people.

CUL-22.name: Horde clans
CUL-22.note: The clans united under the line of Gorath.

POL-01.name: Empire of Aldmark
POL-01.title: Emperor
POL-01.taxes: hearth tax of 1 mark a household a year;a tenth on goods landed at Kingsmere;scutage from knights who will not serve;the gods' tenth of war spoils (to the halls)
POL-01.debts: 24000 hold-marks (120000 suns) to Irondeep;100000 suns to the Hold Bank of Stonehold
POL-01.exports: wheat and rye;horses;amber;furs;flax and linen;pine timber and tar
POL-01.imports: iron and steel from Irondeep;tin from Frostholm by way of Northreach;ship oak from Greyhaven;wine and oil;salt;fine…
POL-01.deadline: Tue 21 Jun: Prince Harald weds Princess Rowena of Ashmere at Kingsmere

fleet.field: About 40,000, as two hosts of 20,000

primer.intro: The iron-ringed empire of the northern plains: black-earth wheat, Millrun horses, Kingsmere amber and the heaviest cavalry in the Westland.
primer.ruler: Emperor Aldwin Ironside, crowned on Return Day 1081 as his father's son; the lords swear to him on the iron ring every New Year's Day. Capital Kingsmere.
primer.people and land: 9,500,000 people on 1,056,400 km², nearly all human, with 114,000 half-orcs in the southern march and 66,500 dwarves. State faith: the Seven Halls, headed by the Emperor since 1002.
primer.strength: 110,000 standing, 460,000 at full levy; built around stake lines, crossbows and iron-mailed lances. Fleet: 24 galleys and 16 cogs at Cold Bay.
primer.three people to know: Aldwin Ironside, the Emperor whose bones sink like stone. Ysolde Ravenscar, the spymaster who had a king poisoned without his leave. Garrick Harrow, the marcher lord who wants his war first.
primer.ties: Allied to Greyhaven and, from June, Ashmere; hostile to the Horde; tense peace with Northreach, cold peace with Sylvaran, rivalry with Varenna and the Highland League; depends on Irondeep's iron.

POL-02.name: Holy See of Solenne
POL-02.title: High Luminary
POL-02.taxes: tithe of a tenth of every harvest;rent from Temple tenants;5 suns from each pilgrim at Solenne;salt tax;rents from Temple estates in Varenna, Ostra and Morhaven
POL-02.exports: olive oil;wine;sea salt;fine clay pottery;holy candles and sun badges;copied books and letters
POL-02.imports: Tamari wheat through Lucerna;timber;iron;rag paper from Qadir;beeswax;gold leaf
POL-02.faith: REL-01 Temple of the Returning Sun
POL-02.deadline: March: Marius Quill's envoy rides north with 10,000 suns to buy or steal Serra's proof from Queen Saelith

fleet.field: About 18,000 for 30 days

primer.intro: The Temple of the Returning Sun's own state around the old sun-city, which crowns kings across the Sunlands and keeps the calendar at the Shadow Needle.
primer.ruler: High Luminary Severin III, elected by the Luminaries in August 1088 on a promise to back Queen Livia; ill since 1103, and the votes for his chair are already being counted. Capital Solenne.
primer.people and land: 6,100,000 people on 282,650 km², almost all human, with 18,300 dwarves and 12,200 half-elves. State faith: the Temple of the Returning Sun; every high office is a priest's.
primer.strength: 68,000 standing, 300,000 at full levy; built around wall-keepers, pilgrim guards and the vowed Knights of the Sun, while crowned allies do the fighting. Fleet: 38 galleys and 12 armed cogs.
primer.three people to know: Severin III, the dying High Luminary. Marius Quill, the Needle-Keeper who guards the calendar's secret. Crispin Dorn, the Treasurer who needs cheap bread and four votes.
primer.ties: Allied to Varenna and Morhaven; backs Queen Livia; banks through Ostra's House Lunetti at 8 in 100; rivalry of faith with Velgrad and Drevna; Eldergrove holds Serra's proof over it; the Highland League never paid its tribute.

POL-03.name: Kingdom of Varenna
POL-03.title: King
POL-03.taxes: hearth tax;a penny in 20 on market sales;salt tax;tolls at the Crown Road passes
POL-03.debts: 1100000 suns to House Lunetti;unpaid crowning gifts to the Holy See
POL-03.imports: ship timber from Ashmere and the Highlands;copper;iron;horses from the Nine Winds;rag paper;spices;tin
POL-03.faith: REL-01 Temple of the Returning Sun
POL-03.deadline: May Fair to 21 Jun: the War Party's window to strike up the Palella at Crowbrook and Stagley before the wedding

fleet.field: About 46,000 by barge up the Palella; 24,000 over the passes

primer.intro: The largest realm and army in the Known World: the Lion crown, the Palella weaving towns and the spinning wheel nobody else has.
primer.ruler: King Roderic III Valdane, crowned by the Temple on Return Day 1088 as Queen Lucilla's son. He is 42, the age when Valdane hearts fail, and his collapsed in November 1104. Capital Varenna.
primer.people and land: 12,000,000 people on 1,084,900 km², nearly all human, with 48,000 dwarves, 48,000 half-orcs and 24,000 elves. State faith: the Temple of the Returning Sun.
primer.strength: 156,000 standing, 600,000 at full levy; built around crossbows behind terraces and stakes, with knights waiting for the moment to charge. Fleet: the Lion Fleet, 90 galleys and about 140 cogs.
primer.three people to know: Roderic III Valdane, the king with the Lion's heart. Dario Montaro, the general with the palace gates promised to him. Oria Vantes, the spymaster offering help in Lucerna.
primer.ties: Allied to Solenne, resenting the tithe, and to Morhaven, 4,000 men each; cold war with Blackreef since 1051; rivalry with Aldmark and Ashmere; public friendship with Lucerna, which secretly takes a fifth of the toll Varenna pays.

POL-04.name: Republic of Lucerna
POL-04.title: Doge
POL-04.taxes: Staple toll of one bushel in twenty;harbor dues;a fortieth on insured cargo;citizens' tax in gold crowns
POL-04.exports: re-shipped Tamari grain;sea salt;fine Lucernan wine;figs;ships;sea insurance and bills of exchange;trained food-tasters
POL-04.imports: Tamari wheat and barley;ship timber;iron and pitch;spices;fire-oil from Sabra (secret);wool and cloth
POL-04.faith: REL-01 Temple of the Returning Sun
POL-04.deadline: Fri 1 Apr: Admiral Castellan asks Lucerna for 20 galleys against Blackreef

fleet.field: About 3,000 landed from the fleet

primer.intro: A lagoon republic of 750,000 that feeds the Middle Sea: the Grain Staple, the most trusted gold coin, sea insurance, trained food-tasters and a secret fifth of the dragon toll.
primer.ruler: Doge Tiberio Doravelli, elected for life by the Great Council of about 300 families on 9 March 1096 and crowned by the High Luminary. Capital Lucerna.
primer.people and land: 750,000 people on 60,125 km², the smallest realm by land, nearly all human, with 7,500 half-orcs and 6,000 dwarves. State faith: the Temple of the Returning Sun.
primer.strength: 10,000 standing, 36,000 at full levy; built around citizen marines, hired swords, the Lagoon Chain and a secret oil cellar. Fleet: about 60 galleys, 20 manned, and 180 cogs.
primer.three people to know: Tiberio Doravelli, the Doge who knows where the fifth goes. Flavia Morello, who wants the ledger clean. Giulia Bassan, who holds a holy city's grain for a better price.
primer.ties: Secret partner of Blackreef and of Sabra, which sells it 400 jars of oil a year; partner of Ostra; public friend of Varenna; rival of Qadir; creditor of the Amber Isles and Greyhaven; buys Tamar's wheat under the Grain Staple.

POL-05.name: Kingdom of Ashmere
POL-05.title: King
POL-05.taxes: hearth tax;a fifth of copper dug;arrow tax of 24 arrows a hearth a year
POL-05.debts: 120000 suns to House Lunetti;9000 suns to Eldergrove for yew staves
POL-05.exports: wheat and barley from the ash soil;copper;sulfur and pumice;wool and cheese;obsidian
POL-05.deadline: Sun 20 Mar: Spring Equinox Moot at Ashmere; Rowena demands to read her marriage contract and its hidden clause

fleet.field: About 30,000 at home; 14,000 abroad for 40 days

primer.intro: The western kingdom of ash soil and the only longbow army: about 50,000 yeomen who can draw a war bow, with copper, sulfur and wool to pay for the arrows.
primer.ruler: King Edric Ashford, crowned on Return Day 1055 as his grandmother's heir, 71 years old after 49 years of peace, and now dosed with poppy syrup. Capital Ashmere.
primer.people and land: 5,500,000 people on 453,850 km², nearly all human, with 33,000 elves. Faith split: the court follows the Temple, the villages keep the Seven Halls in free halls; neither is state faith by law.
primer.strength: 60,000 standing, 260,000 at full levy; built around yeoman longbows behind stakes on a hillside. Fleet: 12 coastal galleys and nothing more.
primer.three people to know: Edric Ashford, the old king kept quiet. Rowena Ashford, the bride who wants to read the small print. Edmund Hale, the Chancellor who ordered the poppy.
primer.ties: Planned alliance with Aldmark; rivalry with Varenna since 1016; friendship with Eldergrove, which sells the yew; hires Highland crossbow companies; quarrels with Sylvaran over smuggled yew.

POL-06.name: Kingdom of Sylvaran
POL-06.title: Queen
POL-06.taxes: no coin tax;grove tithe of honey, wax and arrows;20 days of labor a year
POL-06.exports: honey and beeswax;furs of marten and beaver (few);medicinal herbs and dried mushrooms;carved bone and wood
POL-06.imports: salt;dwarven steel and mail;iron tools;wool cloth;Qadiri paper for the Chroniclers
POL-06.deadline: Leaf Fall (late September): the Moot of Leaves votes on the heir of the Evenwood

fleet.field: About 4,000 bowmen in one forest district; it does not march

primer.intro: The great forest of the Evenwood, oldest realm on the map, where the First Oak grows and no tree is cut without a Keeper's mark; honey, wax and the deadliest archers alive.
primer.ruler: Queen Ithrien the Oakborn, crowned at the Greening of 712 as her mother's heir; she is 586 and has no heir the law allows. Capital Evenglade.
primer.people and land: 780,000 people on 1,238,850 km², the second-largest land in the world: 744,900 elves, 27,300 humans, 7,800 half-elves. State faith: the Green Covenant, whose Keepers can veto any cutting.
primer.strength: 10,000 standing, 40,000 at full levy; built around rangers who are few, slow to replace and deadly from the trees. No fleet.
primer.three people to know: Ithrien the Oakborn, the last of her line. Arannel the Eldest Keeper, who tends the First Oak and has promised a sleeping crown. Calithil Lightfoot, who commands the rangers on the Edge.
primer.ties: Cold peace with Aldmark since the blood-price of 1080; cool toward Eldergrove since the Sea Covenant of 340; an old border with the Horde on the Tusk Hills; honey for iron with Irondeep, the oldest trade either keeps; a yew quarrel with Ashmere.

POL-07.name: Kingdom of Eldergrove
POL-07.title: Queen
POL-07.taxes: harbor fee of one part in twenty at Nimthil and Ithira;one voyage in ten for the queen;grove tithe of timber and food
POL-07.exports: yew staves for Ashmere;fir ship timber and masts;salmon and herring;seal oil;slate
POL-07.deadline: March: the Holy See's envoy comes to buy or steal Serra's proof from Queen Saelith

fleet.field: About 3,200

primer.intro: The sea-elves of the fir coast, who cut ship timber under the Sea Covenant: longships, yew staves for Ashmere's bows, and an archive that holds the Temple's worst secret.
primer.ruler: Saelith the Veiled Queen, of the Mistwalker line, queen since 1003 as her mother's heir; she rules with the Council of the Grey Veil, which decides in months, not decades. Capital Silverbough.
primer.people and land: 340,000 people on 372,925 km²: 306,000 elves, 20,400 humans, 13,600 half-elves. State faith: the Green Covenant in its sea-going form.
primer.strength: 5,000 standing, 18,000 at full levy; built around sea-archers on fir longships and night rangers who see in the dark. Fleet: about 40 longships and 70 cogs.
primer.three people to know: Saelith the Veiled Queen, who sells silence by the decade. Lirael the Archivist, who keeps the proof. Thalion Halfleaf, the half-elf heir who would rather not.
primer.ties: Friendship with Ashmere since 1012; cool toward Sylvaran; selling fir masts to Aldmark; a quiet war of paper with Solenne over Serra's proof; ivory and oil at Frostholm's summer fair.

POL-08.name: Kingdom of Northreach
POL-08.title: King
POL-08.gov: kingdom ruled with the Ring (council of jarls and the Lawspeaker)
POL-08.taxes: a tenth on all tin passing to Kingsmere;ship levy (a longship crew per district);fish tithes to the halls
POL-08.debts: 40000 highland silver to the Highland League
POL-08.exports: stockfish and herring;seal oil and furs;amber;walrus ivory and whale tusks;Frostholm tin (re-sold);pine timber and tar
POL-08.deadline: Late March: Jarl Halvard Stagg means to bring the Kingsmere-born cook to the Thing to name King Bjorn's poisoner

fleet.field: About 8,000 at home; 1,000–2,000 on skis in winter

primer.intro: The small kingdom of fog, forest, ice and longships that beat an empire in the Northreach Rising; stockfish, amber and Frostholm tin re-sold.
primer.ruler: King Eirik III Winterborn, crowned on Lantern Night 1090 after his father Bjorn died; he swore on the Oathfather's ring to keep the Free Halls. Capital Wolfhaven.
primer.people and land: 800,000 people on 159,550 km², almost all human. State faith: the Seven Halls, in the Free Hall form where villages choose their priests.
primer.strength: 10,000 standing, 40,000 at full levy; built around ice-walkers, the king's hird and longship raids on the ebb. Fleet: 48 longships and 15 cogs.
primer.three people to know: Eirik III Winterborn, who promised Aldmark ten years of silence. Halvard Stagg, the jarl bringing a cook to the Thing. Oddny Tinmark, the Tin Reeve whose balance has cheated the giants for years.
primer.ties: Tense peace with Aldmark since Coldhaven (1093); the Tin Compact with Frostholm; allied to the Highland League, which lent 40,000 silver due by 1111; secret trade in Hrimfell tusks sold as unicorn horn; secret bolts from Irondeep.

POL-09.name: Halls of Frostholm
POL-09.title: Chieftain
POL-09.gov: land of giant halls, each ruled by its eldest
POL-09.taxes: grain tribute to the halls each Harvest Home;all tin belongs to the halls
POL-09.exports: tin;walrus ivory;whale oil;mammoth ivory (sold as old bones dug from the ground);seal skins;wool
POL-09.faith: REL-12 The Mother Under the Ice

fleet.field: About 30 pairs and 300 tribute-folk for a few days

primer.intro: The giant halls of the far northern isle: 3,100 giants and the human tribute-folk who serve them, living on tin, walrus ivory, whale oil and mammoth wool.
primer.ruler: Chieftain Skarvi the Younger, chosen at the Thing of 1078 as his aunt's heir; each hall is ruled by its eldest, and the Skarfell chieftain speaks for all of them to humans. Capital Skarfell.
primer.people and land: 18,100 people on 122,525 km²: 3,100 giants and 15,000 humans. Faith: the Mother Under the Ice, who sends seals and whales to her children.
primer.strength: 300 standing (160 giants, 140 tribute-folk), 1,080 at full levy; built around giants fighting back to back in the winter dark with spearmen at their flanks. No fleet.
primer.three people to know: Skarvi the Younger, who sold tin he had sworn not to. Bergthor of Haugberg, the rival eldest who waits for 1106. Solvei of Torvik, the hunter with a harpoon head.
primer.ties: Tin for grain and ale with Northreach since 1002; kinship with Hrimfell, the other last giant people, last crossing 1019; Aldmark's wary interest in buying the tin direct; ivory and oil for Eldergrove's longships.

POL-10.name: Kingdom of Irondeep
POL-10.title: Queen
POL-10.gov: dwarven hold ruled by a queen with the Council of Masters
POL-10.taxes: metal tithe from every forge;no coin tax
POL-10.exports: iron bars;steel tools and pots;fine wire-drawn mail;plate pieces such as breastplates;crossbow bolts in small lots
POL-10.deadline: Tue 1 Mar: 400 Aldmark soldiers may stay at the lower Iron Road fort for 6,000 bushels of grain

fleet.field: About 2,000 at one gate

primer.intro: The dwarven hold beside Aldmark's plains: iron bars, steel tools, wire-drawn mail and the Deep Gate, which no human army has passed.
primer.ruler: Queen Brynja Deepeye, queen since 1032 as her father's daughter, confirmed by the Council of Masters and Law-Carver Orsa Flintmark; she has renewed the Iron Road Contract three times. Capital Irondeep.
primer.people and land: 100,000 people on 29,425 km²: 95,000 dwarves and 5,000 humans. State faith: the Deep Law, judged by Law-Carvers no ruler may overrule.
primer.strength: 1,800 standing, 6,000 at full levy within hours; built around breastplates and war-picks in the gate, with sappers under it. No fleet.
primer.three people to know: Brynja Deepeye, the queen who traded a fort for grain. Korrin Deepeye, the thane who wants his mother set aside. Orsa Flintmark, the Law-Carver already writing to Stonehold.
primer.ties: Trade dependence on Aldmark since 951, which wants to control the hold; bound to Stonehold and Emberdeep by the Judgment of 904; honey for iron with Sylvaran; secret iron to Greyhaven's shipwright and secret bolts to Northreach.

POL-11.name: Horde of Gorath
POL-11.title: War-Chief
POL-11.gov: horde of clans held together by the Line of Gorath
POL-11.taxes: no coin tax;one horse in twenty from each clan;a share of every raid
POL-11.exports: horses;sheep and goats;felt and wool;hides;salt from the Salt Sea edge
POL-11.faith: REL-11 The Storm and the Mare
POL-11.deadline: Tue 21 Jun: the Great Ride at the Drum Stones judges whether Tarn Halfblood is the rider of two peoples

fleet.field: About 36,000 riders for 30 days; 20,000 for a summer

primer.intro: The orc clans of the southern grass, held together by the Line of Gorath: horses, felt and relay riders who win in ten minutes or not at all.
primer.ruler: War-Chief Vrag, grandson of Gorath, chosen at 26 in 1098 to stop the clans splitting; shamans confirm a war-chief and the Grey Mothers can overrule him. He has a weak heart. Capital Urgol.
primer.people and land: 1,600,000 people on 1,345,050 km²: 1,312,000 orcs, 160,000 humans, 128,000 half-orcs. State faith: the Storm and the Mare, with a Drum Council of senior shamans.
primer.strength: 24,000 standing, 90,000 at full levy, women riding as well as men; built around relay charges by riders who tire in ten minutes. No fleet.
primer.three people to know: Vrag, the war-chief with the weak heart. Tarn Halfblood, who may be the rider of two peoples. Harkun the Drum-Master, who must judge him.
primer.ties: Hostile to Aldmark; enemies of the Nine Winds since the Salt Shore (1041); rivalry with the Highland League and the Tusk Clans; an old border with Sylvaran; its Nagoth clans sell wool and horses at Morhaven's and Ostra's market towns.

POL-12.name: Khanate of the Nine Winds
POL-12.title: Khan
POL-12.gov: confederacy of nine tribes under the Compact of 925
POL-12.taxes: one horse in thirty from each tribe;a tenth of every horse sold at the channel fairs;the oil money (to the khan alone)
POL-12.exports: horses (about 20,000 a year);camels;felt;caviar and dried sturgeon;salt;fire-oil (secret;to Queen Livia only)
POL-12.deadline: Tue 21 Jun: the Horse Feast; Yesun of the Red Wind needs the Well tribes' votes to block Serik

fleet.field: About 32,000 riders with 120,000 horses for 40 days

primer.intro: Nine horse tribes on the steppe by the Salt Sea, bound by the Compact of 925: 20,000 horses a year, the yam post, sturgeon and the only fire-oil north of Sabra.
primer.ruler: Khan Ozbek Kharsan, raised by the nine chiefs in 1079 as his uncle's heir and first among equals; their kurultai can force a khan out. He is nearly blind. Capital Kharsa.
primer.people and land: 1,400,000 people on 407,700 km²: 1,302,000 humans, 70,000 half-orcs, 28,000 orcs. Faith: the Eternal Blue; two tribes follow the Path of the Well.
primer.strength: 20,000 standing, 80,000 at full levy, every herder a rider and archer; built around horse archers who never close. Fleet: about 60 small boats on the Salt Sea.
primer.three people to know: Ozbek Kharsan, the blind khan who sells fire. Serik Kharsan, the heir who wants the oil stopped. Yesun of the Red Wind, who knows what lies in the Khatun's chest.
primer.ties: Enemies of the Horde; horses for grain and cloth with Greyhaven since 925; the Horse Road to Morhaven, which now carries the oil; a secret deal with Queen Livia; friendship with the Tusk Clans.

POL-13.name: Highland League
POL-13.title: First Speaker
POL-13.gov: league of mountain valleys under the Charter of Highcastle
POL-13.taxes: a tenth of every silver mine;a toll on every mule on the high roads;a fifth of every hire contract
POL-13.exports: silver;crossbowmen for hire;crossbows and bolts;cheese and wool;marble;iron and copper
POL-13.deadline: Sun 1 May: the Gordush crossbow contract; the vote at Highcastle decides whether 4,000 crossbowmen go to Aldmark

fleet.field: About 12,000 in the passes; 4,000 abroad under one contract

primer.intro: A league of mountain valleys under the Charter of Highcastle (336), where no one may be king: silver mines, cheese and the heavy crossbows every realm hires.
primer.ruler: First Speaker Helga Stonefoot, elected for life by the Council of Valleys in July 1099 by a single vote; she once saved a child from a Crown Eagle. Capital Highcastle.
primer.people and land: 1,400,000 people on 214,050 km², almost all human, with 8,400 dwarves. State faith: the Seven Halls, in the Free Hall form.
primer.strength: 18,000 standing, 4,000 of them abroad on contract until April, 72,000 at full levy; built around heavy crossbows for hire and gorges that eat armies. No fleet.
primer.three people to know: Helga Stonefoot, whose middle course may please no one. Ulric Greycloak, the Captain-General who took Aldmark's silver early. Tomas Redford, the Speaker whose vote was bought and who wants Helga's seat.
primer.ties: Wary peace with Aldmark, whose Edict of the Halls it refused; allied to Northreach, which owes it 40,000 silver; guards its glens against the Horde with no treaty ever signed; sells Ashmere bolts; Greycloaks have served Ostra since 968; never paid the Holy See's tribute.

POL-14.name: Kingdom of Greyhaven
POL-14.title: King
POL-14.taxes: channel toll (about 350,000 tides a year after Velgrad's half);hearth tax;harbor dues
POL-14.exports: ship oak and chestnut timber;iron;sulfur from Smokewell;fish;ships and ship repair;horses re-sold from the steppe
POL-14.imports: horses from the Nine Winds;wine and oil;spices;fine cloth;salt
POL-14.deadline: A July dusk: Velgrad looses eight fire rafts to fake the Black Dragon's rising and seize the channel tolls

fleet.field: About 20,000 on land

primer.intro: The channel kingdom: 58 galleys, half the Grey Channel tolls, ship oak for everyone's fleets, Tide Divers, and a deaf king who speaks with his hands.
primer.ruler: King Osric IV Tidewell, crowned in March 1084 as his father's son, already deaf from diving; his daughter Linnet reads his hand-signs aloud in council. Capital Greyhaven.
primer.people and land: 4,800,000 people on 430,650 km², nearly all human, with 28,800 half-orcs, 19,200 dwarves and 14,400 elves. State faith: the Seven Halls.
primer.strength: 60,000 standing, 230,000 at full levy; built around a galley navy that owns a kingdom, the tides first and the passes second. Fleet: 58 galleys and about 140 cogs.
primer.three people to know: Osric IV Tidewell, who hears nothing and misses little. Rolf Brightwater, the admiral waiting for the rafts. Linnet Tidewell, the daughter who is her father's voice.
primer.ties: Allied to Aldmark since 1076; rivalry with Velgrad over the channel tolls since 1010; horses for grain with the Nine Winds; marriage talks with Drevna; secret iron from Irondeep; older fleet debts to Lucerna.

POL-15.name: Kingdom of Morhaven
POL-15.title: King
POL-15.taxes: toll on every horse and camel on the Horse Road;harbor dues at Felano and Morhaven;land tax
POL-15.debts: 350000 suns to House Lunetti;unpaid crowning gifts to the Holy See
POL-15.exports: wheat;wine;timber;iron from the hills;horses resold west;salt fish
POL-15.imports: steppe horses and camels;felt;caviar;spices;cloth;rag paper;fire-oil passing through to Tessar (secret)
POL-15.faith: REL-01 Temple of the Returning Sun
POL-15.langs: Solen common speech;Old Solen;Wind Rider speech
POL-15.deadline: Late March: Silas Vane carries 40 jars of fire-oil to Coreria; if it burns, Morhaven's neutral trade turns

fleet.field: About 14,000 on the coast road; 9,000 onto the steppe

primer.intro: The watchful kingdom where the steppe meets the Sunlands: towers that see everything, deep walls, the Horse Road, and a king who sells to both sides.
primer.ruler: King Aurelio II Falcone, called the Bargainer, crowned by the Temple on Return Day 1079 as his father's son. Capital Morhaven.
primer.people and land: 2,600,000 people on 180,200 km², nearly all human, with 15,600 half-orcs and 10,400 dwarves. State faith: the Temple of the Returning Sun.
primer.strength: 38,000 standing, 136,000 at full levy; built around watch towers, deep walls and steppe riders. Fleet: 24 galleys and about 40 cogs at Felano.
primer.three people to know: Aurelio II Falcone, who bargains with everyone. Tancred Falcone, the prince who sent an unsigned warning north. Serena Falcone, whose cipher log could prove which road the jars came by.
primer.ties: Neutral trade with both Tessarian claimants; allied to Solenne (760) and Varenna (1090); enmity with Blackreef since 1011; sells oil, wine and grain to the Horde's Nagoth clans; the Horse Road with the Nine Winds.

POL-16.name: Free City of Ostra
POL-16.title: First Banker
POL-16.gov: city-state run by the Council of Twelve
POL-16.taxes: a penny in 50 on every exchange of coin;gate and harbor dues;wine tax;purple tax on dyed cloth
POL-16.debts: 600000 suns in city bonds to its own citizens
POL-16.exports: murex purple dye and purple cloth;Isle of Vines wine;olive oil;bills of exchange and loans;timber from the hills
POL-16.faith: REL-01 Temple of the Returning Sun
POL-16.deadline: Sun 1 May: the Ostran partition of the Neck must be signed before May Fair to stop Andros

fleet.field: About 9,000 for 30 days

primer.intro: The bankers' city of murex purple and bills of exchange, where House Lunetti holds about 4 million suns and lends to half the crowns of the world.
primer.ruler: First Banker Cosimo Lunetti, chosen by the Council of Twelve on 1 July 1091; banker of the Temple, Varenna, Morhaven and Queen Livia, and host of the secret Tessarian talks since 1102. Capital Ostra.
primer.people and land: 2,400,000 people on 187,600 km², nearly all human, with 19,200 half-orcs and 14,400 dwarves. State faith: the Temple of the Returning Sun.
primer.strength: 26,000 standing, 110,000 at full levy; built around hired walls paid on the first of the month, the Purple Company and Highland crossbows. Fleet: 30 galleys and about 70 armed merchantmen.
primer.three people to know: Cosimo Lunetti, who owns the debts of both claimants. Gerolt Marr, captain of the Purple Company, whose contract is pledged to a dwarven bank. Mora Purplehand, who leads 14,000 dockers and dyers.
primer.ties: Creditor of Tessaria since 1018; banking compact with Solenne; partner of Lucerna, which gets its fifth through an Ostran front house; rivalry with Stonehold, whose dwarf crowns undercut its bills, and with Velgrad; hires Greycloaks.

POL-17.name: Sultanate of Qadir
POL-17.title: Sultan
POL-17.taxes: water-tax of a tenth of every irrigated crop;a tenth on paper sent abroad;a twentieth on other cargo;2 silver qadr a head from non-believers
POL-17.debts: 180000 suns to the Water Endowment;90000 suns to the Gold Houses of Zanara
POL-17.exports: rag paper;dates;olive oil;copper and lead;salt fish;re-exported Zanari gold
POL-17.imports: linen rags from Tamar;wheat from Tamar;ship timber from the Holy Coast;iron;Zanari gold;horses
POL-17.faith: REL-07 The Path of the Well
POL-17.deadline: Fri 1 Apr: Grand Admiral Jalal sails on Sabra with 34 galleys

fleet.field: About 10,000 over the Sabun Pass; 15,000 on the coast

primer.intro: The sultanate of passes and galleys on the desert coast: rag paper, which only Qadir makes, dates, copper, and the House of Water where the Book of Wells is judged.
primer.ruler: Sultan Zahir IV Zahiri, Guardian of the Water, crowned on 21 April 1092 as eldest son; bedridden with kidney stones since November 1104. Capital Qadira.
primer.people and land: 2,100,000 people on 390,800 km², almost all human. State faith: the Path of the Well, whose Well-Keepers can declare a sultan's order against the Book.
primer.strength: 28,000 standing, 100,000 at full levy; built around holding the Sunwall and never crossing open desert without guides. Fleet: 34 galleys, 12 of them leaking, and about 120 merchant ships.
primer.three people to know: Zahir IV Zahiri, the sick Sultan. Jalal Zahiri, his brother, who built the fleet and wants to use it. Rafiq the Quiet, the spymaster hunting journeymen and jars.
primer.ties: Rivalry with Sabra since its breakaway in 1025 and with Lucerna, which paid for it; hostility with Blackreef, whose toll Qadiri ships refuse; a secret water-contract with the Sand Clans; the Delta Wells quarrel with Tamar; the Scale Pact with Zanara; fellow Well realm with the Amber Isles.

POL-18.name: Kingdom of Tamar
POL-18.title: King
POL-18.gov: god-king ruling through a vizier and nome governors
POL-18.taxes: grain tax set from the flood mark (a fifth in a fair year, a tenth in a lean one);a month of dyke work a year
POL-18.imports: timber;silver;iron;horses;olive oil and wine;paper;spices by the Monuti route
POL-18.deadline: August to October: the Monuti flood; a third lean flood would undo King Amenhar's right to rule

fleet.field: About 40,000 along the Monuti

primer.intro: The river kingdom of the Monuti, whose flood and wheat feed the Middle Sea: linen, papyrus, natron for the dead, and a god-king whose right rests on the height of the water.
primer.ruler: King Amenhar V Tamaren, son of the Flood Mother and a living god, crowned on 2 April 1089 as his father's son; his right rests on a flood mark re-cut that September. Capital Tamar.
primer.people and land: 4,200,000 people on 321,250 km², almost all human. State faith: the Flood Mother; about a sixth of the delta follows the Path of the Well.
primer.strength: 44,000 standing, 200,000 at full levy raised only from March to July; built around a river army that fights with the flood, fed on bread and short of horses. Fleet: 10 sea galleys, 16 river galleys and about 300 barges.
primer.three people to know: Amenhar V Tamaren, the god whose mark was re-cut. Rahotep Kadari, the general selling galleys for blood-price. Menna the Measurer, the flood-priest who ordered the 1089 roll burned.
primer.ties: Allied to Abara since 989, paying a river gift for the headwaters; old enmity with Tessaria over the Long Rift; sells wheat to Lucerna under the Grain Staple; quarrels with Qadir over the Delta Wells; natron and guides with the Sand Clans; Keshi spice passes up its river.

POL-19.name: Confederacy of the Sand Clans
POL-19.title: Speaker
POL-19.taxes: a fifth of every salt fee at Mirah;guide fee per camel;pilgrims' water fee
POL-19.debts: 40000 suns owed by the southern clans
POL-19.exports: rock salt;camels;guiding and escort;dates from the oases;copper
POL-19.imports: Zanari gold;millet and sorghum;cloth;iron blades;paper for contracts
POL-19.faith: REL-07 The Path of the Well
POL-19.deadline: Mon 14 Mar: Well Day; Tariq Bahar threatens to read Zahir's sealed water-contract unless Qadir pays 20,000 suns

fleet.field: About 20,000 in the Southern Hills; 5,000 at one well group

primer.intro: The largest realm on the map and nearly all of it Red Waste: 23 camel clans who hold the desert because nobody else can cross it, selling salt, guides and escort, and guarding the Well of Samar.
primer.ruler: Speaker Tariq Bahar, acclaimed for life by the clan chiefs at Zarak on 11 February 1087 as his uncle's heir; any clan may walk away from a decision it did not swear to. Capital Zarak.
primer.people and land: 1,300,000 people on 2,206,625 km², almost all human. State faith: the Path of the Well, in the Riders' form; the Keeper of the First Well guards the Well of Samar with them.
primer.strength: 18,000 standing, 72,000 at full levy, every grown man of the 23 clans; built around camel riders who never fight for ground and hold the desert by its wells. No fleet.
primer.three people to know: Tariq Bahar, the Speaker who sells silence to a Sultan. Harith Sayf, who would close the Salt Road. Salma Bahar, the Well-Mother asking about missing children.
primer.ties: An uneasy Treaty of the Salt Road with Zanara (1063); a secret water-contract with Qadir, which swore never to send soldiers to the Well; the Marad children quarrel with Sabra; natron, linen and grain across the Waste with Tamar.

POL-20.name: Empire of Zanara
POL-20.title: Emperor
POL-20.taxes: every gold nugget;a tenth of gold dust sold at market;salt tax at the city gates;vassal tribute in gold, cattle and captives
POL-20.deadline: May (the rains): Nia Tembo must cut the road to Atani before the rains end the war season

fleet.field: About 60,000 in the dry season

primer.intro: The gold of the Golden Plains, whose weights set the price of gold from Sabra to Qadira; ivory, iron, cattle and the second-largest army in the world.
primer.ruler: Emperor Mosi III Kanemba, chief voice of all the ancestors, emperor since 1094 as his father's son; his left hand went numb in November 1104. Capital Zanara.
primer.people and land: 11,000,000 people on 1,905,975 km², almost all human. State faith: the Thousand Ancestors; the High Rememberer can refuse to sing an emperor's line.
primer.strength: 140,000 standing, 560,000 at full levy; built around a great spear host run by runners and drums and paid in gold. Fleet: about 200 war canoes and barges on the rivers.
primer.three people to know: Mosi III Kanemba, the emperor with the numb hand. Juma Kanemba, the Marshal whose riders march by night. Nia Tembo, who must cut the road to Atani before the May rains.
primer.ties: An uneasy treaty with the Sand Clans; a dispute with Abara over the Road Promise; the Scale Pact with Qadir and the Gold Road to Sabra, both since 1071; rivalry with Kesh, which fears a road that bypasses its ports.

POL-21.name: League of the Spice Coast
POL-21.title: Prince
POL-21.gov: league of four towns run by a council of merchant houses
POL-21.taxes: a tenth of every spice cargo at the Pepper Hall scales;harbor fees at Kesh and Monuro;head tax of 1 kesh on foreign sailors
POL-21.exports: black pepper;cardamom;cinnamon-like bark;hardwoods;ivory;pearls;rare woods from the Leaf People
POL-21.deadline: Fri 1 Apr: Sultan Iskandar's fleet sails for the Isle of Pearls with Keshi ships

fleet.field: About 12,000 ashore; 4,000 overseas

primer.intro: Four merchant towns on the pepper coast run by a council of houses: black pepper, cinnamon bark, hardwoods, pearls, and a fleet that fights by night and with fire.
primer.ruler: Prince Amani Keshari, elected by the council in 1092 as his father's heir; he married Laila Maruang of the Amber Isles in 1101, borrowed 200,000 suns from Amber merchants and secretly pawned the harbor dues of 1105. Capital Kesh.
primer.people and land: 2,200,000 people on 253,750 km², almost all human. State faith: the Thousand Ancestors.
primer.strength: 22,000 standing, 100,000 at full levy, the hill levies for defense only; built around fighting at sea by night and with fire, and ashore from the forest. Fleet: about 45 fighting ships and 150 merchantmen.
primer.three people to know: Amani Keshari, the prince who pawned his harbor. Laila Maruang, the princess between her brother and her husband's house. Hamisi Monuri, the merchant who would sell the princedom.
primer.ties: Allied to the Amber Isles by the marriage of 1101; trade rivalry with Ranpur, whose pepper undercuts Kesh by the Nagora road; a quarrel with Zanara over the eastern road; spice up the Monundi to Abara and up the Monuti through Tamar.

POL-22.name: Kingdom of Abara
POL-22.title: King
POL-22.taxes: a tenth of grain and cattle to the reigning king;Tamar's river gift
POL-22.debts: 60000 suns (Yonas's court) to the Gold Houses of Zanara;cattle (Yared's court) to lords of the north
POL-22.exports: coffee beans;cattle and hides;iron;stream gold;honey and wax;highland horses
POL-22.deadline: Sat 1 Jan: King Yared's voiding of the Road Promise takes effect; 8,000 at Tamowa face Zanara's 12,000 at Atani

fleet.field: About 25,000 from one host; 60,000 if both kings agree

primer.intro: The highland kingdom that holds the source of the Monuti, and so Tamar's harvest: coffee, cattle, stream gold, pike-held terraces, and two crowned kings who swap the crown every New Year's Day.
primer.ruler: Twin kings since 1090 under the Compact of 1053: Yared Asfari reigns in odd years and holds the crown for 1105; Yonas Asfari reigns in even years. Each keeps his own court, guard and host. Capital Abara.
primer.people and land: 6,500,000 people on 737,900 km², almost all human. State faith: the Thousand Ancestors, with the royal ancestor houses at Abara.
primer.strength: 80,000 standing in two hosts that have not fought together since 1049, 320,000 at full levy; built around pike hedges on chosen ground. No fleet.
primer.three people to know: Yared Asfari, the king of 1105, who calls his twin's promise void. Gebre Tsega, the Marshal holding Tamowa, quietly paid by a Zanari merchant. Tekle Asfari, the exiled prince who wants to come home.
primer.ties: Allied to Tamar since 989, taking a river gift each year; a dispute with Zanara; pepper comes up the Monundi from Kesh, searched by Yared's new toll-men; pays Tessar to keep Tekle on the Neck.

POL-23.name: Kingdom of Hrimfell
POL-23.title: King
POL-23.gov: realm of giant halls under a king of the Jotunhall line
POL-23.taxes: a share of every catch in meat, fat and oil;30 days of hall work a year;a share of ivory from giants
POL-23.exports: walrus ivory;whale tusks sold south as 'unicorn horn';seal oil;whalebone;furs;soapstone
POL-23.faith: REL-12 The Mother Under the Ice
POL-23.deadline: Tue 21 Jun: the Midsummer Thing of Hrimfell chooses its next king

fleet.field: About 280 (120 giants, 160 hunters)

primer.intro: The giant kingdom of the frozen eastern coast: 2,600 giants and 9,100 human hunters, living on seals and walrus, and selling whale tusks south as unicorn horn.
primer.ruler: King Hraldr of Jotunhall, named alone by Mother Asta at the Thing of 1077 as his cousin's heir; he led the Hrimfell Raids from a sledge, made the Truce of Dobin in 1098, and is dying. Capital Jotunhall.
primer.people and land: 11,700 people on 619,225 km²: 2,600 giants and 9,100 humans. Faith: the Mother Under the Ice; Jotunhall is in the time of the 52nd Mother, and the sixtieth will be the last.
primer.strength: 200 standing (72 giants in pairs, 128 human harpooners and runners), 680 at full levy; built around giants fighting back to back, in the cold, and rarely. No fleet.
primer.three people to know: Hraldr of Jotunhall, the dying king on a sledge. Ulfar of Jotunhall, the halls' candidate. Torvald of Torholm, who leads the Walking Halls and wants a reason to break the truce.
primer.ties: The Truce of Dobin with Drevna over the whaling grounds; kinship with Frostholm, the other last giant people; secret tusk trade through Northreach; white bear and fox pelts sold to Velgrad at the Ostmir fairs.

POL-24.name: Emirate of Sabra
POL-24.title: Emir
POL-24.taxes: water-tax of a tenth;the best pearl of every boat each week and a tenth of the rest;1 dinar per 20 camels
POL-24.debts: 50000 suns to the Gold Houses of Zanara
POL-24.exports: pearls;dates;'lamp oil' (fire-oil;in secret);salt;dried fish;gold in transit
POL-24.faith: REL-07 The Path of the Well
POL-24.deadline: Fri 1 Apr: Jalal sails on Sabra; Tahir Sabrani plans to burn the fleet at Miruma first

fleet.field: About 8,000

primer.intro: The pearl emirate that broke from Qadir in 1025, rich on pearls, dates and the "lamp oil" boiled on its oil shore, which burns fleets and feeds Blackreef's dragon.
primer.ruler: Emir Karim Sabrani, Emir since 2 October 1086 as his father's son; the oil trade is run from his own treasury and never discussed in council, and his chest has doubled to about 800,000 suns. Capital Sabra.
primer.people and land: 1,200,000 people on 392,225 km², almost all human. State faith: the Path of the Well, in the Wells form.
primer.strength: 17,000 standing, 60,000 at full levy; built around never meeting a fleet head-on but burning it, and camel riders who fight at noon. Fleet: 14 galleys, 30 fire-boats and about 400 pearling boats as scouts.
primer.three people to know: Karim Sabrani, the Emir who never says the word oil in council. Tahir Sabrani, the son who wants to strike first. Qasim Nafari, the oil-master who counts every returned empty.
primer.ties: Secret oil supplier to Blackreef since 1051 and to Lucerna, whose loans paid for the revolt; rivalry with Qadir; the Marad children quarrel with the Sand Clans; the Gold Road caravan from Zanara reaches it each spring.

POL-25.name: Kingdom of Velgrad
POL-25.title: King
POL-25.taxes: half of the channel through-tolls;a tenth of every river cargo;hearth-tax in rye or pelts
POL-25.exports: sable and marten furs;iron and copper;sulfur from Redcrown;flax and linen;tar and pitch;wax and honey;silk re-sold from the east
POL-25.imports: wine and olive oil;salt;spices;fine cloth;Qadiri paper;dwarven steel
POL-25.deadline: A July dusk: Velgrad looses the eight fire rafts to seize the Grey Channel tolls

fleet.field: About 20,000 for one summer

primer.intro: The feudal kingdom of the Eastland, seat of the Patriarch of Dawn: sable furs, Redcrown sulfur, Sevany galleys, half the Grey Channel tolls, and a war fought by proxy in the Neck.
primer.ruler: King Stanislav Sevrin, crowned by the Patriarch on 2 July 1098 as his father's son, a head taller than other men; no king of Velgrad has ever ruled uncrowned. Capital Velgrad.
primer.people and land: 4,500,000 people on 730,050 km², nearly all human, with 27,000 half-orcs and 18,000 dwarves. State faith: the Dawn Church, whose Patriarch sits at Velgrad.
primer.strength: 50,000 standing, 220,000 at full levy; built around passes, galleys and proxies, with 4,400 men already in Prince Andros's camp. Fleet: 38 galleys and 22 armed cogs at Sevany.
primer.three people to know: Stanislav Sevrin, the tall king who plans a dragon. Radek Volan, the Channel-Master buying pitch and old hulls. Kirill the Lamp-Bearer, the Patriarch who could unlight Andros.
primer.ties: Backs Prince Andros, who married Vesna Sevrin in 1075; rivalry with Greyhaven since 1010, Drevna since the Lakeland War, Ostra and Solenne; buys Hrimfell pelts at Ostmir; pays the Tusk Clans' silk toll at Kraoth.

POL-26.name: Kingdom of Drevna
POL-26.title: Queen
POL-26.gov: kingdom ruled by the Dravic queen with a small council
POL-26.taxes: hearth-tax in furs or wax;river tolls on the Dromir;a tenth of every silk caravan at Lubany
POL-26.exports: furs;beeswax and honey;timber and tar;flax;rye;dried and salted fish;whale oil
POL-26.imports: salt;wine;iron tools and dwarven steel;fine cloth;horses from the steppe;Qadiri paper
POL-26.deadline: Sat 1 Jan: the Lake Council hears the case for the 2,000 bushels of withheld rye

fleet.field: About 24,000 in summer; 8,000 by sled in winter

primer.intro: The Lakeland: furs, beeswax, rye and the Dawn Church's oldest monasteries, ruled by a queen whose family cannot bear the sound of drums.
primer.ruler: Queen Milena Dravic, crowned in June 1085 as her father's daughter by Patriarch Kirill of Velgrad; the great lords meet as the Lake Council each New Year's Day. Capital Drevna.
primer.people and land: 5,800,000 people on 693,175 km², nearly all human, with 46,400 half-orcs, 23,200 orcs and 17,400 dwarves. State faith: the Dawn Church, under a lesser Patriarch at Drevna.
primer.strength: 64,000 standing, 280,000 at full levy; built around crossbows, ice and silence, an army that wins by waiting. No sea fleet; about 300 lake boats and 50 whaling boats.
primer.three people to know: Milena Dravic, who cannot command within sound of drums. Vadim Zorac, the Lord Marshal who holds the rye. Ludmila Dravic, the heir training with wax in her ears.
primer.ties: Hostile peace with the Tusk Clans under the Treaty of Thardush (1066); rivalry with Velgrad; the Truce of Dobin with Hrimfell; rivalry of faith with Solenne; salt from Skyhold; marriage talks with Greyhaven.

POL-27.name: Abbey of Skyhold
POL-27.title: Abbot
POL-27.taxes: one child from every family to a monastery;tithe of butter and wool;pilgrim gifts of silver or butter
POL-27.exports: salt and borax from the dry lakes;sky wool from yaks and goats;gold dust;medicinal herbs;yak tails and hides
POL-27.imports: barley and rice;iron tools and dwarven metalwork;cotton cloth;Qadiri paper for scripture;dried fruit
POL-27.faith: REL-06 The Way of the Open Sky
POL-27.deadline: May or June: Brother Pema's search diary is carried to the dying Abbot Tashen

fleet.field: About 5,000 on the Roof

primer.intro: The monastery-state on the Roof of the World: the White Stair, sky burials, salt and borax from the dry lakes, yak wool, and guards who have sworn never to kill.
primer.ruler: Abbot Tashen, 13th Abbot of the White Stair, found as a child and named in September 1061 as the reborn abbot; the search is disputed. He coughs blood, and Steward Sonam runs the daily rule. Capital Skyhold.
primer.people and land: 350,000 people on 402,425 km², almost all human. State faith: the Way of the Open Sky; the Red Stair sect of the High Wastes rejects the 13th Abbot.
primer.strength: 3,600 standing (2,400 Stair Guard with staves and slings, 300 Snowborn Guides), 16,000 at full levy; built around thin air, which is the wall, and guards who do not kill. No fleet.
primer.three people to know: Tashen, the dying Abbot with a sealed letter for his rival. Norbu of the Red Stair, who says the search found the wrong child. Sonam of Skyhold, the Steward buying steel.
primer.ties: Salt trade with Drevna under the Salt Letters of Eaglespire; free passage for its salt through Stonehold's tolls since 650; a quarrel with Emberdeep over the dragon of Kardeep; the salt trail to Ranpur, run since 521.

POL-28.name: Kingdom of Stonehold
POL-28.title: King
POL-28.taxes: metal tithe from every forge and mine;Zardeep Pass toll of one part in ten;1 in 20 of Ranpur's Nagora tolls
POL-28.exports: gold and silver;rubies and sapphires;crucible-steel blades;mail and breastplates;copper and tin;rock salt
POL-28.imports: barley;rice and wheat;beer malt;wool and cotton cloth;timber;lamp oil
POL-28.deadline: April to May: the Old Toll marches on the Nagora Gate unless Crown Prince Hrodgar bargains first

fleet.field: About 5,000, into a pass or gorge only

primer.intro: The greatest dwarven hold and seat of the First Hall where the Deep Law was carved: gold, rubies, crucible-steel blades, the Hold Bank, and a pass it lost to Ranpur in 1085.
primer.ruler: King Harvald Bardun, king since 1011 as his father's son, now 215; he has not left the First Hall since 1098 and signs whatever the banker Orrin Goldvein reads him. Capital Stonehold.
primer.people and land: 300,000 people on 310,025 km²: 260,100 dwarves and 39,900 humans. State faith: the Deep Law; the Eldest Carver sits here.
primer.strength: 6,000 standing, 18,000 at full levy, every adult trained with pike, axe and crossbow; built around pikes in the gate, crossbows on the wall and sappers under the floor. No fleet.
primer.three people to know: Harvald Bardun, the king who signs what he is read. Kettil Ironbrow, leader of the Old Toll, who would feed an Ostran expedition to a dragon. Thora Grimstone, the Eldest Carver calling Emberdeep to trial.
primer.ties: Cold peace with Ranpur since the Nagora Pass; creditor and rival of Tessaria over the Tirana gold since 1004; bound to Irondeep and Emberdeep by the Judgment of the First Hall; rivalry with Ostra's banks; free salt passage for Skyhold.

POL-29.name: Kingdom of Emberdeep
POL-29.title: Forge-Queen
POL-29.taxes: metal tithe from every forge;gate fee at Tharmund on all human trade
POL-29.debts: 40000 lotus (about 308000 suns) to the temple banks of Ranpur at 12% a year
POL-29.deadline: February: the heat tallies go to the Forge-Queen before the spring cutting

fleet.field: About 3,000

primer.intro: The dwarven hold inside a hot mountain, its forges heated by springs the dwarves call the Smith-Father's breath: crucible steel, gold, gems, and a Dragon Watch with crossbows aimed at the sky.
primer.ruler: Forge-Queen Hilde Hammerhand, who took the Forge Crown at 106 in 1050 after the steam burst; she keeps the true heat readings secret. Capital Emberdeep.
primer.people and land: 220,000 people on 140,175 km²: 190,080 dwarves and 29,920 humans. State faith: the Deep Law.
primer.strength: 4,400 standing, 13,200 at full levy; built around one road, hot tunnels and crossbows aimed at the sky. No fleet.
primer.three people to know: Hilde Hammerhand, the Forge-Queen digging a way out. Hakon Steamwright, who keeps the true tally. Inga Crag, captain of the Dragon Watch, who killed a sky-king.
primer.ties: Trade partnership with Ranpur since 950, and the Chanari steel secret they share; bound to Irondeep and Stonehold by the Judgment of 904; a quarrel with Skyhold over the dragon of Kardeep.

POL-30.name: Kingdom of Ranpur
POL-30.title: Raja
POL-30.taxes: a sixth of every rice harvest;the Nagora tolls;market tax in the ports
POL-30.debts: 20000 dwarf crowns to the Hold Bank of Stonehold;a debt to the temple banks for the Nagora road
POL-30.imports: iron and timber from the Free Marches;gold;horses;salt;silver
POL-30.deadline: April to May: Stonehold's Old Toll marches on the Nagora Gate

fleet.field: About 50,000 with 200 elephants on the Chanpur plain

primer.intro: The monsoon kingdom of rice, cotton, sugar and war elephants, with the only human crucible steel at Chanari and the richest temples in the world.
primer.ruler: Raja Indrajit Ranavir, called Victor of Nagora, crowned in September 1090 as his father's son after winning the Nagora Pass as prince; the temples hold the courts and the gold. Capital Ranpur.
primer.people and land: 7,000,000 people on 270,800 km², almost all human. State faith: the Thousand Names; the One Face movement grows among merchants.
primer.strength: 84,000 standing, 350,000 at full levy called after the rice harvest and never in the monsoon; built around elephants, crucible steel and miners, fighting only in the dry season. Fleet: about 50 galleys and 120 armed merchantmen.
primer.three people to know: Indrajit Ranavir, the Raja who won a pass. Rohan Nagar, the general who keeps two toll books. Kiran Ranavir, the kinsman who wants the Steel Guard and the temples.
primer.ties: Cold peace with Stonehold since 1085; the steel partnership with Emberdeep since 950; trade rivalry with Kesh over pepper and with the Amber Isles over cotton and spice ships; the salt trail to Skyhold.

POL-31.name: Kingdom of Tessaria
POL-31.title: Queen / Prince (two claimants)
POL-31.gov: kingdom split in civil war since 1061
POL-31.taxes: road taxes (both claimants);forced loans on towns;grain taken for the armies

primer.intro: The Neck, the only land road between the Southland and the Eastland, torn by civil war since 1061: copper, cedar, road tolls, and two crowned claimants who deny each other exists.
primer.ruler: Two. Queen Livia Tessaran, crowned by the Temple at Tessar on 12 April 1061 on her father's disputed deathbed words. Prince Andros Tessaran, her cousin, proclaimed at Calossa the same day and crowned by the Dawn Church in 1062. Capital Tessar; Andros winters at Coreria.
primer.people and land: 1,900,000 people on 182,575 km², almost all human. Faith split about half each between the Temple in the south and the Dawn Church in the north.
primer.strength: 35,000 standing (Livia 18,000, Andros 17,000), 90,000 at full levy; built around a queen behind walls and engines with hired swords, and a prince in a winter camp who buys towns. Fleet: Livia's 12 galleys.
primer.three people to know: Livia Tessaran, the queen with the fire. Andros Tessaran, the prince who buys garrisons. Corvin Asterio, her Lord Marshal, who has sold copper to the enemy's mint since 1101.
primer.ties: Solenne backs Livia and Velgrad backs Andros; Ostra and Stonehold are creditors; Morhaven trades with both; Blackreef hires Livia 800 crossbowmen and the Nine Winds sell her oil; old enmity with Tamar; Abara pays to keep its exiled prince here.

POL-32.name: Sultanate of the Amber Isles
POL-32.title: Sultan
POL-32.taxes: harbor fee on every ship;a fifth of all spice;water-tax
POL-32.faith: REL-07 The Path of the Well
POL-32.deadline: Fri 1 Apr: Sultan Iskandar's fleet of about 6,200 men sails for the Isle of Pearls

fleet.field: About 10,000 at home; 6,000 overseas

primer.intro: The spice islands of the eastern gulf: cloves, nutmeg, amber-gum, pearls, about 55 galleys steered by a secret needle, and a royal line that aches before storms.
primer.ruler: Sultan Iskandar Maruang, Guardian of the Water, crowned in October 1099 as his father's son; he passed the Storm Watch at 12. Capital Amberport.
primer.people and land: 1,500,000 people on 170,750 km², all human. State faith: the Path of the Well for the sultans and Well-Keepers; the commoners follow the Thousand Names.
primer.strength: 18,000 standing, 72,000 at full levy; built around a galley sultanate steered by a secret needle and marines who land on beaches. Fleet: about 55 galleys and 140 armed spice ships.
primer.three people to know: Iskandar Maruang, the Sultan who plans to betray his ally. Jaya Rawang, the admiral who promised too much. Rahim Sulong, the Grand Vizier who buys toll farms and Keshi princes.
primer.ties: Allied to Kesh by the marriage of 1101; in debt to Lucerna's House Doravelli against the clove harvests; rivalry with Ranpur for the eastern cotton and spice ships; fellow Well realm with Qadir, through which its pilgrims sail.

POL-33.exports: stolen and resold cargo;salt fish from the Bone Coast;goats and hides;hired crossbowmen;safe-passage tokens
POL-33.deadline: Fri 1 Apr: Lark Shoalwise sells the stamped Sabran fire-oil jar to Qadir

fleet.field: About 1,800 landed for a few days

primer.intro: The pirate haven in the shoals of the Strait of Hael, which takes 1 in 40 from every ship that passes, about 45,000 marks a year, behind a dragon that is really Sabran oil.
primer.ruler: Captain-General Nell Brine, elected by the Captains' Table in November 1094 as her father's heir; every captain with a share-book sits at the Table, and it can vote her out. Capital Blackreef.
primer.people and land: 180,000 people on 101,275 km²: 167,400 humans, 9,000 half-orcs and a few hundred of every other people. Faith: the luck-gods of the Corsairs, with dice thrown before a raid.
primer.strength: 3,400 standing, 800 of them hired to Queen Livia, 10,000 at full levy; built around fear: fire-rafts in the shoals, a staged dragon and crossbows for hire. Fleet: 22 light galleys, 12 captured cogs and about 60 fire-rafts.
primer.three people to know: Nell Brine, who runs piracy as a toll company. Ima Redsail, who wants the old ways and Nell's seat. Brann Hollow, captain of the 800 Reef Crossbows at Tessar.
primer.ties: Cold war with Varenna, which pays the toll; secret partner of Lucerna and secret buyer of Sabra's oil; enmity with Morhaven since the sack of 1011; hired swords to Queen Livia; hostility with Qadir, whose ships refuse the toll.

POL-34.name: League of the Tusk Clans

POL-34.taxes: Toll of Kraoth on every Silk Road caravan (one part in ten since 1103);one horse in twenty-five from each clan

POL-34.faith: REL-11 The Storm and the Mare
POL-34.deadline: Tue 21 Jun: the Tusk Great Ride at Grakmar

fleet.field: About 18,000 riders for a month; 10,000 for a summer

primer.intro: The 31 orc clans of the eastern steppe who would not follow Gorath and call no living chief holy: horses, felt, turquoise, and the silk-road toll at Kraoth.
primer.ruler: War-Mother Urza Ironhide, chosen at 14 in 1080 as Grakka's hearth daughter; the council of clan-mothers ruled for her until 1082 and can still overrule her on grazing and law. Capital Grakmar.
primer.people and land: 700,000 people on 644,850 km²: 602,000 orcs, 49,000 humans, 49,000 half-orcs. State faith: the Storm and the Mare, which here rejects any living chief as holy.
primer.strength: 10,000 standing, 40,000 at full levy from 31 sworn clans; built around drums, relays and silk-road silver. No fleet.
primer.three people to know: Urza Ironhide, the War-Mother who must not faint in the sun. Hrok Whitehorn, whose riders burned the Sevmir farms. Gurz the Toll-Keeper, who holds the Silk Road's purse.
primer.ties: Hostile peace with Drevna since the Tusk War ended in 1066; rivalry with the Horde, which sent no help in that war; Velgrad pays its silk toll at Kraoth; friendship with the Nine Winds, whose Khan fought Gorath and sends horses.

FAM-702.title: none (extinct)
FAM-702.local: Former ruling house of the Emirate of Qadir
FAM-702.notes: Extinct in its own name since 803; it lives on through House Zahiri. A house of the fallen Emirate of Qadir.

BLD-01.name: House Corvane
BLD-01.trait: Sunborn eyes: many women of the line see about 100 times more shades of color than others; half the sons are red-green color-blind
BLD-01.how: A changed color-cell gene on the X chromosome makes a red-sensing cone whose peak is shifted. A woman who carries it on one X and a normal gene on the other grows four kinds of color cells instead of three and can tell apart shades that look identical to everyone else (tetrachromacy).
BLD-01.inherit: Carried on the X chromosome. A carrier mother passes it to half her sons, who are color-blind, and half her daughters, who may have the Sunborn eyes. A color-blind father passes it to all of his daughters and none of his sons.
BLD-01.cost: About half of all Corvane sons are red-green color-blind and barred by old custom from reading battle banners, signals or heraldry, so the house cannot lead troops. The Stone Rule narrows its marriages and keeps it poor. The women's gift makes them valuable to the Temple and dependent on it.
BLD-01.exclusive: The Stone Rule, kept since Aurelia: a Corvane daughter marries only a man who takes the Corvane name, and her children are Corvanes.
BLD-01.ancestor: Aurelia the Far-Seeing, daughter of Corvan the Sunbringer
BLD-01.story: The first carrier was Aurelia the Far-Seeing, born in 12 AR, the daughter of Corvan the Sunbringer and Seraphine of Lorina. Neither parent had the gift; it was a new change in the X she got from her father. As a small girl in the palace at Solenne she sorted the potters' glazes by shades the potters could not see and called the ash-grey winter sky 'nine colors'. At 14 she caught a Lorina cloth merchant selling cheap brown-red cloth as true madder red for the royal banners, and her father began to use her as a judge of dyes.
BLD-01.significance: In 1105 the Sunborn eyes are the reason House Corvane still matters. They are the living proof, to believers, that Corvan's blood is touched by the Light, and they give the only lay member of the High Luminary's council her office as Warden of the Crowning Stone and judge of the Temple's gold and…

BLD-02.name: House Valdane
BLD-02.trait: Lionblood: very tall with long arms and fingers; reach a hand beyond other men of the same height
BLD-02.how: A change in the gene for a connective-tissue protein (fibrillin, as in Earth's Marfan syndrome) lets the long bones grow longer and makes the tissue that holds the joints, the lenses of the eyes, the heart valves and the wall of the main artery looser and weaker.
BLD-02.inherit: Dominant: one copy is enough, and each child of a carrier has an even chance of getting it. It shows in about half of each carrier's children.
BLD-02.cost: Weak heart valves and a weak main artery: many carriers die suddenly in their 40s, and hard riding or war can burst the artery. The lenses of the eyes slip, so most carriers are short-sighted young and half-blind in later life. Loose joints dislocate.
BLD-02.exclusive: The Rule of the Long Blood of 891: a Valdane daughter who shows the reach marries a Valdane cousin or takes the sun-sisters' vows, and never carries it into another house.
BLD-02.ancestor: King Roderic Valdane the Lionheart, first carrier
BLD-02.story: The first carrier was Roderic Valdane, born at Varenna in March 835 to King Lothar II the Grey, then 56, and his third wife, Queen Adria of Norossa. Neither parent was tall, and no Valdane before him had the reach; the change arose new in his father's seed, which happens more often with old fathers. The boy grew long and thin. At ten he stood a head over the sons of the palace guard, his fingers could span an octave of a lute and then some, and he stooped to hear people. The court physicians noted that he could bend his thumb flat to his wrist and that he read with the page at his nose.
BLD-02.significance: In 1105 the Lionblood decides whether Varenna has a king. Roderic III's failing heart could stop any day, and his heir is a boy of 12 with the same blood and weak eyes.

BLD-03.name: House Ironside
BLD-03.trait: Iron bones: bones two to three times denser than normal, rarely broken
BLD-03.how: A change in one gene that controls how bone is laid down and taken away. The body keeps adding bone and hardly removes any, so the skeleton is two to three times denser than normal and very hard to break, but far heavier.
BLD-03.inherit: Dominant: one copy is enough. About half the children of a carrier have it, and a child without it cannot pass it on.
BLD-03.cost: Too heavy to float: they sink in water with armor or without it, and two of the line have drowned. The thickened skull presses on the nerves of the ear and brings deafness and headaches after 50. Heavy bodies tire their horses faster, and every Ironside must be kept away from fords and thin ice.
BLD-03.exclusive: The change arose in Brand alone in 890, so only his descendants can carry it; his brother's line at Dunfield does not. Every carrier since has been of the imperial line.
BLD-03.ancestor: Emperor Harald Ironside, founder of the Empire of Aldmark
BLD-03.story: The iron bones began with Brand, born in 890 at Dunfield on the Millrun, the second son of the horse-breeder Ivo of Dunfield. No one before him in the family had them; the change was born with him. His mother said he was the heaviest baby the Dunfield midwife had ever lifted. At eight he fell 9 m from a hayloft onto packed earth and walked away with bruises. At 15 he went through the Millrun ice while leading a mare across and sank like an anvil, straight down, while his brother Wulf, who went through beside him, floated. Wulf dragged him out by the hair.
BLD-03.significance: The whole Ironside dynasty now rests on one carrier of the iron bones, Prince Harald, who cannot swim and wants to ride with Lord Harrow across the Gordush after May Fair. There is no cadet branch with the blood.

BLD-04.name: House Winterborn
BLD-04.trait: Frost blood: can sleep in snow and work bare-handed in hard frost without frostbite
BLD-04.how: A changed gene for the enzyme that lets cells burn fat for heat, carried in two copies, together with unusually large stores of heat-making brown fat around the neck and spine.
BLD-04.inherit: Recessive: it shows only when a child gets a copy from both parents, about 1 in 4 children of two carriers. Carriers with one copy show nothing. The house marries cousins to keep it.
BLD-04.cost: About one baby in ten dies of fits before two if it goes even a day without food, so the house keeps a milk watch over every royal child. Adults with the blood must eat often and grow weak quickly when starved. The cousin marriages also bring other weaknesses into the nursery.
BLD-04.exclusive: The blood shows only in children of two carriers, and only the Winterborn house marries carrier to carrier: the royal line weds the Stagflow branch, and Winterborn daughters marry inside the house.
BLD-04.ancestor: Eirik Winterborn, who led his men over the sea ice to Wolfhaven in 812
BLD-04.story: The frost blood first showed in Eirik, born in January 784 in a sealers' camp on the sea ice off the Amber Capes. His parents, Thane Ulfar and his wife Ragnhild, were cousins of the Capes thane-kin, and each carried one copy without knowing it. The night Eirik was born a blizzard blew the camp's tents away. Ragnhild dug a snow-hole and lay in it with the newborn until morning, and when the men dug them out the baby's hands were warm. The camp called him the winter-born child.
BLD-04.significance: The frost blood is part of the Winterborn claim to rule: the founder crossed the ice with it, and every winter campaign of the Northreach Rising was led by frost-blooded men. Eirik III is the only frost-blooded Winterborn of the main line alive.

BLD-05.name: House Ashford
BLD-05.trait: The Wakeful: fully rested on 4 hours of sleep
BLD-05.how: A change in one gene of the body's inner clock shortens the sleep the brain needs, so carriers wake fully rested after four hours. The same change seems to push the mind's highs higher: carriers swing between bouts of wild confidence and black moods.
BLD-05.inherit: Dominant: one copy is enough, and about half the children of a carrier have it. A child without it cannot pass it on.
BLD-05.cost: Bouts of wild confidence followed by black moods lasting weeks. Two Ashford kings made ruinous decisions in bold fits: Cedric's pass tax of 975 and Edric's clause of 1104. Queen Elsbeth and Crown Prince Aldred died after black moods.
BLD-05.exclusive: Every carrier descends from Aldred I. The royal line and the Embermere branch, which descends from a younger son of Godric II, are the only families with it.
BLD-05.story: The trait first showed in Aldred Ashford, born 738, son of the lord of the Ashmere valley. His nurse told his mother that the boy never slept more than four hours and woke laughing. As a young lord he worked the day at the valley's courts and rode the night between the halls of his rivals. In the winter of 771 to 772 he rode to the Hawkmarch, Crowbrook and Swanburg in six nights, a ride of about 400 km, and came back with three lords bought with copper shares. His rivals slept; he did not.
BLD-05.significance: The Wakeful blood sits at the center of the wedding that will decide the west in 1105. The hidden clause was signed in a bold fit, and the king who signed it is now sunk in the black mood that followed. If Edric dies or breaks before June, Rowena becomes queen and can tear up the treaty;

BLD-06.name: Stonefoot kin
BLD-06.trait: Perfect balance: can run along a wall top or stand on one foot in a storm
BLD-06.how: The balance organs of the inner ear are unusually sensitive, and the brain trusts them more than the eyes. On still ground a Stonefoot feels the smallest tilt and corrects it at once. On a moving floor the ears and eyes disagree, and the same sharp sense brings violent sickness.
BLD-06.inherit: Dominant: one copy is enough, and about half the children of a carrier have it.
BLD-06.cost: Violent seasickness: most Stonefoots collapse on a boat or a ferry and faint on swaying bridges. They cannot serve abroad by sea or cross lakes.
BLD-06.exclusive: Every carrier descends from Orm Stonefoot. The kin marry inside the Highcastle valley clans, and husbands or wives from other clans take the Stonefoot name, as Bard Cairnhold did in 1073;
BLD-06.ancestor: Hild Stonefoot, first to climb Mount Roktar
BLD-06.story: The balance first showed in Orm, born about 652 to a herding family of Highcastle. As a boy he walked the top rail of the sheep pens and the ridge of the Council hall roof, and he never fell. He became a cragsman, gathering eagle eggs and wild honey from cliffs the other herders would not try, and the herders said his feet were stone on the rock. When he took his children down to the Sunland fairs to sell cheese, the ones who had his feet were sick on the Lake Calia ferry until they could not stand, and one fainted halfway across the rope bridge over the Greycloak Gorge.
BLD-06.significance: The balance is why the Stonefoot kin hold the League's highest seat and why they alone can guard the last Snow Drakes of the Crown Range. Ada Stonefoot's Cliff Runners keep hunters out of the high valleys, and only the kin can climb to the nesting clefts.

BLD-07.name: House Tidewell
BLD-07.trait: Deep lungs: can hold breath for 5–6 minutes and dive to 40 m
BLD-07.how: A changed gene makes the spleen about half again as large as other people's. On a dive the spleen squeezes a store of red blood into the body, and a strong diving reflex slows the heart, so the body wastes little breath;
BLD-07.inherit: Dominant: about half of the children of one carrier have it, sons and daughters alike. It only shows in children who are trained to dive from early childhood.
BLD-07.cost: Burst eardrums and deafness by about 40 for those who dive, often much earlier; lung fevers after cold dives, which killed Osric III; a Tidewell who does not dive gains nothing, and the Ring Law can bar an heir who fails the dive.
BLD-07.exclusive: The deep lungs are born only to Tidewells. Other Northfolk divers, even the best of the Tide Divers, cannot stay down past two or three minutes.
BLD-07.ancestor: King Osric Tidewell the Diver of Greyhaven, who cut the harbor chain of an enemy fleet underwater
BLD-07.story: Wenna Tidewell was born in 688, the daughter of a Northfolk net-maker who mended nets for the Solen fleet station at Greyhaven. As a girl she dived for tools the sailors dropped in the harbor, and the older divers noticed that she stayed down far longer than they could and came up without gasping. The station's chain-master took her on at 14. In 719 the great harbor chain broke its winch, sank and fouled on an old wreck in 30 m of water, and the galleys could not leave. The Solen divers tried and failed. Wenna went down eleven times in one day and freed it link by link.
BLD-07.significance: In 1105 the diving blood decides who may rule the richest toll in the north, and the heir's claim rests on a dive that was faked, which three people can prove.

BLD-08.name: House Falcone
BLD-08.trait: Falcon eyes: can read a banner at 3 km and spot sails at 30 km
BLD-08.how: A dominant variant packs the cone cells in the center of the eye far tighter than normal, so the eye resolves about twice the fine detail of an ordinary eye. The same variant thins the dark pigment layer at the back of the eye, so bright light scatters inside it and brings on blinding headaches.
BLD-08.inherit: Dominant: each child of a carrier has an even chance to inherit it, and about half of Falcone children show it. It shows by about age six, when a child reads a pennant that grown men cannot.
BLD-08.cost: Bright light brings on blinding headaches; most carriers wear green glass shades or gauze veils at noon and are dazzled when they look toward a low sun, as Prince Leone was in 1079. Some go half blind in old age.
BLD-08.exclusive: The trait began as a single new change in Piero Falcone in 921, so only his descendants can carry it; about 30 people have had it in five generations.
BLD-08.ancestor: Captain Aurelio Falcone the Far-Eyed, who spotted a corsair fleet at 30 km and saved Morhaven
BLD-08.story: The first carrier was Piero, a charcoal-burner's son born in the Castina hills in 921. Nobody in his family before him had unusual eyes; the trait began with him. In 898 Tancred the Steadfast had ordered a stone tower every 10 km along the coast and the steppe edge, and the towers needed boys who could see. Piero climbed the Castina tower at 14 in 935. He read the signal flags of the next tower at 3 km when the older lookouts saw only a smudge, and he counted riders on the steppe edge an hour before anyone else.
BLD-08.significance: The Falcone eyes are why this house holds Morhaven: the crown of 1012 was a reward for one morning's sight, and the Tower Watch they lead is the kingdom's whole defense doctrine. In 1105 the eyes matter three ways.

BLD-09.name: House Lunetti
BLD-09.trait: Perfect memory: remembers every number, face and date they have seen
BLD-09.how: A rare variant changes how the brain stores what the eyes and ears take in, so a carrier keeps a page of figures, a face or a spoken price after one exposure and can call it back years later.
BLD-09.inherit: Dominant but weak-showing: each child of a carrier has about two chances in five to carry the variant, and only about half of those show the full memory, so about 1 in 5 children of the line has it.
BLD-09.cost: They cannot forget: sleeplessness, black moods and obsessions with numbers and old wrongs. Nora Lunetti drowned herself in 934 and Ugo Lunetti in 1071; Cosimo walked into the harbor in 1102 and was pulled out.
BLD-09.exclusive: Only descendants of Ilaria Lunetti carry the memory. Her Ledger Contract of 911 binds every marriage of the house: men who marry Lunetti heiresses take the Lunetti name, and Lunetti daughters who…
BLD-09.ancestor: Ilaria Lunetti the Ledger, who could recite every debt owed to Ostra
BLD-09.story: The first carrier was Ilaria, daughter of the money-changer Benedetto Lunetti, born at Ostra in 842. Nobody before her in the family had shown anything more than a good head for sums. At seven she sat under her father's table on the harbor steps and recited back the day's rates for 30 coins after hearing the brokers call them once. Benedetto tested her with the price lists of the previous month and she gave them back line by line. When he took a bench in the new Exchange Hall in 849, he kept no tablet: the girl was his book. At 12 she kept the bench alone.
BLD-09.significance: The Lunetti memory is Ostra's hidden vault. The bank's true books exist in two heads as well as on paper, so Lunetti accounts cannot be forged, stolen or burned away, and every king who owes the house knows it. Cosimo remembers every debt and every word of the Ostran talks;

BLD-10.name: House Doravelli
BLD-10.trait: The Taster's tongue: can taste bitter poisons at one-hundredth the dose others need
BLD-10.how: Carriers have about three times the usual number of taste buds on the tongue and a highly sensitive form of the bitter-taste receptors, with a sharp sense of smell (supertasters).
BLD-10.inherit: Dominant: about half the children of a carrier have it. It is tested at seven with a drop of wolfsbane in water.
BLD-10.cost: Cannot bear strong food, spice or wine; many are thin and sickly, and strong smells make them vomit. A taster who is offered a bribe to let poison pass carries the whole house's name.
BLD-10.exclusive: The Rule of the Cup of 971: every child of Doravelli blood, born in Lucerna or abroad, in marriage or not, is tested at seven with a drop of wolfsbane in water.
BLD-10.ancestor: Doge Silvio Doravelli the Taster, who detected poison in the council's wine
BLD-10.story: The first known carrier was Nicola Doravelli, born about 680, a sampler at the Grain Staple whose work was to chew a mouthful from every cargo and spit it out. In the autumn of 709 a cargo of Tamari grain came in that looked and weighed right, and that every weigher passed. Nicola said it was bitter and would not certify it. The shipmaster laughed, paid the toll and sold the grain at Ostra, where it caused the fire-sickness of spoiled grain, burning limbs and madness, and killed about 300 people. The Staple made Nicola its taster.
BLD-10.significance: In 1105 the Taster's tongue sits at the most dangerous table in the Known World. Nerio Doravelli is Queen Livia's only defense against poison, and the only man who could let poison pass: Prince Andros's chancellor has offered him 5,000 crowns to do it, and he has not answered.

BLD-11.name: House Tessaran
BLD-11.trait: Six-fingered: a full, working sixth finger on each hand, giving a stronger grip on reins and hilts
BLD-11.how: One changed gene alters how the hand bud splits in the womb and adds a sixth finger on the little-finger side, with its own bones, joints and tendons, so it bends and grips like the others. The same gene helps close the wall between the heart's chambers;
BLD-11.inherit: Dominant: a carrier father or mother passes it to about half of their children. It never skips a generation, so a five-fingered child of the house cannot pass it on.
BLD-11.cost: Weak hearts: about one carrier child in eight is born with a hole between the heart's chambers and dies young or at a sudden strain, as Leo II, Anselm's two sons and Anselm himself did. Commoners call the hand a curse, and each claimant says the other's hand is the cursed one.
