giants of Hrimfell vs Drevna's northern settlers over whaling grounds.

secrets.title: The six missing years
secrets.pub: Mount Hael's ash hid the sun for seven years. At noon on 21 June 1 AR, as Corvan was crowned, the sun shone clear again. The Common Reckoning counts from that day of Return.
secrets.truth: The failed summers ran six years, 12 BR to 7 BR. The first good summer was 6 BR. Corvan won his crown in the Famine Wars (6–1 BR), fought over grain under a clear sky. The priest Tavian and the sun priests folded the war years into the Dimming so the sun seemed to return for Corvan. In 316 Elira Starling found the gap in Brother Odo's Dim Chronicle;
secrets.who: The High Luminary; three to five senior Needle-Keepers who hold the archive keys; the Eldest Keeper and the chroniclers of Sylvaran, who have always known and…
secrets.proof: 1) Odo's original Dim Chronicle, sealed in the Temple archive under the Needle court at Solenne, with Starling's own margin note of 316.
secrets.ifr: The Book of Ash warns that the Light will fail again when the count of the Needle and the count of the trees agree, so many would fear a second Dimming. The Holy See's claim that the Light returned the sun through Corvan would crack.

secrets.title: The fire at Mirona
secrets.pub: In November 3 BR Brennus of Lorina had the granary at Mirona burned with about 300 people inside, to starve Corvan's allies.
secrets.truth: Unpaid hired spearmen of Corvan's own army set the fire while looting. Corvan hanged 22 of them in secret and let Lorina take the blame. Tavian wrote the story everyone now tells.
secrets.who: Perhaps two Temple archivists who have read Tavian's letters. Nobody else alive.
secrets.proof: Tavian's letter to Corvan of December 3 BR, asking him to 'let Lorina carry the fire', in the Temple archive at Solenne.
secrets.ifr: The saintly image of the Sunbringer would be stained, House Corvane shamed, and the town of Lorina given an old grievance against Solenne.

secrets.title: Aurelia's borrowed sight
secrets.pub: The Light showed Aurelia the Far-Seeing the eclipse of 33 AR in a vision. The seers of House Corvane have holy sight.
secrets.truth: Aurelia's extra color sight is a real inherited eye trait, but it did not show her the eclipse. She found it in 11 old Tamari clay star-lists and a copper plate from Hael, brought north by refugees, which showed that eclipses repeat every 18 years.
secrets.who: The Needle-Keepers who keep the eclipse tables. The flood-priests of Tamar, who keep older star-lists of their own and suspect where the Temple got its cycle.
secrets.proof: The Copper Plate of Hael and 11 Tamari clay tablets, with notes in Aurelia's own hand, in the Needle-Keepers' archive at Solenne.
secrets.ifr: The Temple's seers would lose their holy aura. Tamar's flood-priests could claim the Temple's greatest wonder was stolen Tamari learning.

secrets.title: The exiled smith
secrets.pub: Humans learned to smelt iron by copying dwarven blades bought in trade. Dwarves have never taught an outsider.
secrets.truth: About 1000 BR an Iron Mountain smith, Hodd Ashbeard, was exiled for selling a furnace to humans. He lived 40 years at Felano and taught the bloomery to its smiths.
secrets.who: The Law-Carvers of Stonehold and Irondeep, who keep the exile rolls. The smiths' guild of Felano keeps a garbled tale of 'the Short Master'.
secrets.proof: Hodd's name and crime carved in the exile rolls of the First Hall of Stonehold. A small stone anvil cut with dwarven marks in the old smiths' hall at Felano.
secrets.ifr: The dwarves' boast that they never teach would fall. Human smiths and kings would press the holds harder for their secrets, saying they were shared once already.

secrets.title: Hael was warned
secrets.pub: The Devourer came without warning and swallowed the sun at Mount Hael in one day. Hael was simply cursed.
secrets.truth: The mountain warned for three years: quakes, hot sour springs, dead birds in its hollows. King Haldor of Hael closed the roads to keep his copper mines working, and about 70,000 people who could have fled were buried. The few Hael priests who escaped blamed the king and kept a secret mountain faith; the cult of the Ashen descends from them.
secrets.who: The hidden Ash-priests of the Ashen, for whom it is core teaching. A few Temple archivists.
secrets.proof: Four letters from Hael copper merchants to Solen traders, dated 16 to 14 BR, in the Temple archive at Solenne.
secrets.ifr: The Temple's teaching of a sudden, unearned stroke of the Devourer would weaken, the Ashen would gain sympathy for having been right, and Ashmere would ask what Mount Cinder and Mount Brand are saying.

secrets.title: The Year of Ash Trees
secrets.pub: In the Old Edge Wars the orcs set the Evenwood's southern edge on fire to drive out the elves.
secrets.truth: In August 1410 BR elven Keepers set the fire themselves, burning about 9,000 km² of oak as a belt to keep orc raiders out of the deep forest. The shame is why elves forbid open fire in the deep forest.
secrets.who: The Eldest Keeper and the senior Keepers who may read the Keepers' chronicle; the Moot's Chronicler has never been allowed to read the entry.
secrets.proof: The Keepers' chronicle at Evenglade, entry for the Year of Ash Trees. A layer of charcoal under the plough soil around Dunwatch and Thornstone.
secrets.ifr: Elves would lose the high ground in every quarrel over human burning and cutting. The Horde would gain an old grievance, and Aldmark a weapon in any dispute over the Oak Line.

secrets.title: The road gift
secrets.pub: In 118 the beaten orcs begged for peace, and the Crown Range border was won by the sword.
secrets.truth: The First Orc War was a draw. For 40 years (118–158) the Solen crown paid the clans a yearly road gift of 3,000 bushels of wheat and 400 iron blades, hidden in the royal accounts as road upkeep at Albora.
secrets.who: Almost no one. The Grey Mothers' law-songs remember 'the forty winters of Sunland bread'.
secrets.proof: Royal account rolls for 118–158 in the Holy See archive at Solenne, with lines reading 'road upkeep, Albora'. Winter-count hides of the western clans showing a grain wagon each winter.
secrets.ifr: Sunland pride would be hurt, and the Horde of Gorath could claim the Sunland lords once paid it tribute and demand it again.

secrets.title: The flood-priest's gate
secrets.pub: In April 210 King Khaset of Tamar walked into the Monuti and gave himself to the Mother, and his grieving city yielded to Aldric II.
secrets.truth: The High Flood-Priest opened Tamar's river gate to the Solen in return for a promise that temple lands would never be touched. Khaset was killed by Solen soldiers in his palace. The bargain is why temple estates still own a third of the valley.
secrets.who: The High Flood-Priest of Tamar and a few temple archivists, passed down in secret.
secrets.proof: A bronze plate of the pact, sealed by Aldric II and the High Flood-Priest, in the temple archive under the Flood Stairs at Tamar.
secrets.ifr: The flood-priests, who can declare that the Mother has abandoned a king, would be shown to have sold the last native king. King Amenhar V could use it to seize temple estates, which would start a crisis in Tamar.

secrets.title: The emperor's arrow
secrets.pub: Maximian the Great died of marsh fever at Castella in March 302, after a victorious campaign against the elves.
secrets.truth: An elven arrow struck Maximian in the thigh on 19 August 301 during the Burning of the Edge. The wound festered for seven months and killed him. The court hid it because the war was lost.
secrets.who: The elves of Sylvaran, whose chronicle names the archer. Anyone who has read the court physician's case book.
secrets.proof: The Solen court physician's case book in the Holy See archive at Solenne. The Sylvaran chronicle at Evenglade, which records the shot and the day.
secrets.ifr: The legend of Maximian the Great, and the Solen story that the Oak Line was a gift, would fall. It would please the elves and change little else.

secrets.title: The seventh clause
secrets.pub: The Treaty of the Oak Line (302) only fixes the forest's southern and eastern border, the southern half marked by 212 stones. The empire granted it out of generosity.
secrets.truth: A seventh clause, never read in public, lets the elves kill anyone who fells a tree north of the line, with no blood-price owed. Emperor Maximian II accepted it because the elves would sign nothing else.
secrets.who: The Moot of Leaves. The Holy See's archivists, heirs to the Solen state papers. The elves may have shown it to Aldmark's envoys in the Sylvaran–Aldmark Border…
secrets.proof: The elven copy on vellum, sealed with Maximian II's sun seal, at Evenglade. The Solen copy in the Holy See archive at Solenne.
secrets.ifr: Lords and loggers along the Oak Line in Varenna and Aldmark would be outraged that a dead empire signed away their right to justice. Varenna might disown the clause, and the elves might start to use it openly.

secrets.title: The Wolfsbane Cup
secrets.pub: Emperor Cassian II died of marsh fever in 379 AR.
secrets.truth: A cupbearer named Tullo, paid from General Severan's household, put wolfsbane in the emperor's wine. Severan was crowned a month later.
secrets.who: Nobody alive has read the proof. Senior Needle-Keepers of the Holy See could find it if they looked.
secrets.proof: Tullo's confession, taken by a dawnkeeper before he was hanged for theft in 380, is sealed in the Needle-Keepers' archive at Solenne. A household ledger of Severan's lists 'for the cup, 50 crowns'.
secrets.ifr: It would show that the Temple crowned a murderer and kept quiet for 700 years. Heirs of Solen law in Tessaria and Varenna would lose a hero, and the Holy See would look like a keeper of crimes.

secrets.title: The Burning of Calossa
secrets.pub: In 393 AR the people of Calossa set fire to their own town rather than surrender to the empire.
secrets.truth: Solen soldiers killed about 3,000 townsfolk and burned the town on Severan's written order, to frighten the last March lords into surrender.
secrets.who: Marchfolk song-keepers have always said it. A few court historians of Tessar know it for certain.
secrets.proof: Severan's order is copied in a legion day-book kept in the royal archive at Tessar. A layer of burned bone lies about 1 m under Calossa's market square.
secrets.ifr: Marchfolk settlers would turn hard against anyone who claims Solen's heritage, including both Tessarian claimants. The Free Marches would be even harder to rule.

secrets.title: Fire on the Water at Kyzai
secrets.pub: Lightning from a dry storm burned the Solen barge fleet at Kyzai in 425 AR.
secrets.truth: The Wind Riders threw pots of fire-oil from the Salt Sea's eastern seeps. Fire-oil has been a Rider weapon since at least 425 AR, and Solen's generals hid it because they had no answer.
secrets.who: The khans and chief shamans of the Nine Winds. A few Holy See archivists.
secrets.proof: The report of the Solen engineer Rufus Cato, which describes 'fire that floats and cannot be drowned', is in the Holy See archive at Solenne.
secrets.ifr: Every realm would learn how old the fire-oil secret is and where it began. That would raise the value of the eastern Salt Sea shore and the Nine Winds' danger.

secrets.title: The Mast-Oak Sale
secrets.pub: In 340 AR Nimrael the Grey Veil and her followers left Sylvaran in a peaceful parting of faith, the Sea Covenant.
secrets.truth: The parting was peaceful, but a secret set it off. Nimrael's kin had sold 300 mast-oaks to the Solen fleet in 334–336, cut without a Keeper's mark. The Moot asked her to leave rather than stand judgment.
secrets.who: The Eldest Keeper at Evenglade and, by tradition, the rulers of Eldergrove.
secrets.proof: A Solen fleet ledger in the Holy See archive reads '300 mast-oaks from the western elves, 18,000 silver crowns'. The Moot's sealed Leaf Record of 340 is kept at Evenglade.
secrets.ifr: Eldergrove's founding story would change from faith to trade. Sylvaran's purists would use it against every Eldergrove envoy.

secrets.title: The Exiles of Emberdeep
secrets.pub: Around 400 AR Dagna Hammerhand was called east by the Smith-Father's breath, the hot springs, and founded Emberdeep.
secrets.truth: In 398 AR Dagna killed the king of Stonehold's nephew, a rival mine-master, in a forge quarrel. The Law-Carvers exiled her and her whole clan, and Emberdeep was founded by outlaws.
secrets.who: The Eldest Carver of Stonehold, and the ruling Hammerhands of Emberdeep.
secrets.proof: In the First Hall of Stonehold an exile-stone carved with Dagna's name stands with its face turned to the wall. Emberdeep's founding chant has a verse that is never sung.
secrets.ifr: Under the Deep Law, Stonehold could call Emberdeep's founding unlawful and demand blood-price. Relations between the two holds would sour.

secrets.title: The Knife at the Drum Stones
secrets.pub: Emperor Octavian killed Urzag Redhand with his own lance at the Battle of the Drum Stones in 476 AR.
secrets.truth: Urzag's sister's son Gorza stabbed him in the back during the fighting. Gorza had taken 400 pounds of Solen silver to do it.
secrets.who: The Grey Mothers of the Horde of Gorath, who keep the old winter-counts.
secrets.proof: The Redhand clan's own winter-count hide, painted by Gorza's mother Gashna, shows 'the summer the chief was knifed by his sister's son' as a small knife in the corner.
secrets.ifr: Clans that claim descent from Gorza would be shamed. Solen and Aldmark tales of honest victory over the orcs would be proven false.

secrets.title: The Bones in the Wall
secrets.pub: The Crown Wall was built by the legions and paid masons (474–489 AR).
secrets.truth: About 30,000 orc captives from the Old Horde did most of the heavy work. About 11,000 died of cold, hunger and beatings, and many were buried in the fort foundations.
secrets.who: The Grey Mothers' spoken epics tell it. Few humans believe them.
secrets.proof: Bone pits lie under the forts at Dunwatch and Thornstone. Building accounts in the Holy See archive list 'bread for 30,000 captives'.
secrets.ifr: The Horde of Gorath would have a blood grievance and a claim against the forts that Aldmark garrisons. That could start a war on the Crown Range line.

secrets.title: The Old Stones of the Well
secrets.pub: On 14 March 541 AR Samar struck the rock and water leapt out by the Giver's will.
secrets.truth: Samar found the water by reading the desert's signs and digging for 11 days. Below 9 m he found the cut-stone lining of a far older well, marked by Old Tamari masons, that had silted up long ago.
secrets.who: The Keeper of the First Well, who alone goes down the shaft to clean it.
secrets.proof: Stones about 14 m down the shaft carry Old Tamari masons' marks. The oldest copy of the Book of Wells, kept at Zarak, holds a saying left out of later copies: 'I did not make the water;
secrets.ifr: Riders and Wells would argue over whether the Well is a miracle, and Tamar's flood-priests could claim the holiest site of the Path.

secrets.title: The November Order
secrets.pub: Admiral Gaius Merel sailed late against orders in 602 AR and lost the fleet sent to relieve Qadira. He was beheaded for it.
secrets.truth: Justinian IV ordered the fleet to sail on 9 November, after Sea Closing and against every admiral's advice. The written order was hidden and Merel was killed to protect the emperor's name.
secrets.who: Nobody alive knows it. The order sits unread in the Holy See archive.
secrets.proof: Justinian IV's order, in his own hand and under his seal, is in the imperial letter-chests of the Holy See archive at Solenne.
secrets.ifr: Merel's descendants could claim their family's lost lands on the Holy Coast. It would add to the case that the Holy See hides imperial crimes.

secrets.title: The Eggs on the Gundgard Road
secrets.pub: In 612 AR a Great Ash Dragon attacked a dwarven pack-train without warning on the Gundgard road. Durek Hammerhand, heir of Emberdeep, died fighting it with his axe.
secrets.truth: Durek's party had taken two dragon eggs from a nest in hot-spring ground, to sell or to show off. The dragon was defending its young. Most of the 41 dead drowned when panicked mules dragged them off the ledge.
secrets.who: The Forge-Queen of Emberdeep and its Law-Carvers.
secrets.proof: Two Great Ash Dragon eggshells lie in Emberdeep's treasury vault. The sole survivor's account is carved in the Hammerhand clan hall and covered with a hanging.
secrets.ifr: The Red Stair monks, who call dragons sky-kings, would curse Emberdeep. Clan Hammerhand's honor would be stained.

secrets.title: The Pretender was the true son
secrets.pub: Aurelian the Pretender was a palace nobody who lied that he was Justinian IV's son.
secrets.truth: Justinian IV secretly married Lady Serena of House Brennus, lords of Lorina in 584, and Aurelian was their son, born 585. After 625 Valerian II paid the Needle-Keepers to hide the marriage record.
secrets.who: The Needle-Keepers' archivists of the Holy See; no living ruler.
secrets.proof: The signed marriage record, sealed with Justinian's ring, lies in a locked chest of the Temple archive at Solenne, filed under the wrong year (591).
secrets.ifr: Every ruler who claims descent from Valerian II would be shown as a usurper's heir, and the Temple as a paid liar.

secrets.title: Who killed Octavian
secrets.pub: Octavian the Stern died of camp fever at Calora in 621.
secrets.truth: Two of his officers poisoned his wine with yew seed. Valerian's agents paid them 30,000 silver suns.
secrets.who: Nobody alive knows it; it survives only in writing.
secrets.proof: A payment line 'for the eastern matter, 30,000' in Valerian's war ledger in the Holy See archive, and one officer's deathbed confession kept in the Sun Temple at Calora.
secrets.ifr: Valerian II, the hero of the Solen restoration, would be shown as a poisoner who bought his throne.

secrets.title: Lucerna paid for Tamar's freedom
secrets.pub: Queen Nefira freed Tamar with delta courage alone after the Mother abandoned the Solen governors.
secrets.truth: Lucerna's grain merchants lent Nefira 40,000 silver suns and 2,000 crossbows in 639, in return for the right to buy Tamar's wheat. The grain contract of 645 was the repayment.
secrets.who: The Doge's council of Lucerna keeps the old ledgers; the High Flood-Priest of Tamar suspects.
secrets.proof: Harbor ledgers of 639–645 in Lucerna's Hall of Records, with Nefira's seal on the loan.
secrets.ifr: Tamar's founding story would become a merchant deal, shaming the royal house of Tamar and angering the flood-priests.

secrets.title: Maximus lived
secrets.pub: Maximus the Fair died at the Battle of Felano in 667 and lies under a plain stone there.
secrets.truth: The body was a guardsman in Maximus's cloak. Maximus fled by boat to the Free Marches and lived as a ferryman on the Tirana until 694. He had two sons.
secrets.who: A few Marchfolk families who say they descend from 'the ferryman'.
secrets.proof: The grave at Felano holds a man too short to be Maximus; a Marchland saints' shrine on the lower Tirana holds his ring with the imperial sun.
secrets.ifr: Some Marchfolk house could claim the blood of Valerian II, and any Solen revival would have a pretender ready.

secrets.title: The Snow Drakes survive
secrets.pub: The last Snow Drake was shot by a Stonefoot hunter in 704 and its kind died out.
secrets.truth: A small group survives in two Crown Range valleys above 3,000 m, about 15 in 1105. The Stonefoot herders protect them and call the white shapes in the clouds eagles.
secrets.who: A few Stonefoot herders and their elders.
secrets.proof: Nesting clefts with eggshell in the two valleys above Highcastle on the Crown Range.
secrets.ifr: Hunters and collectors would pour into the Highland League, and the Stonefoots' word would be doubted.

secrets.title: Dwarven silver behind the Neck
secrets.pub: The lords of the Neck rose in 702 on their own to defend old freedoms.
secrets.truth: Stonehold paid Leo Tessaran in silver and dwarven mail and fed Tessar by mule train during the siege of 708–709. The price was a toll-free Neck road for dwarven goods, kept secret for two centuries.
secrets.who: The Law-Carvers of Stonehold; the kings of Tessaria were told on crowning until the empire fell in 1047.
secrets.proof: A carved contract with both names poured in metal, in the vaults of the First Hall of Stonehold; a copy in the Tessaran treasury at Tessar.
secrets.ifr: Tessaria's founding legend would become a dwarven purchase, and the old toll-free right could be claimed again in the Tessarian Civil War.

secrets.title: The Patriarch and the general
secrets.pub: The Dawn Schism of 734 was a pure quarrel of faith about the sun, the High Luminary and the people's tongue.
secrets.truth: Bogumil and General Borislav Sevrin agreed in 733 to break from Solenne together: the church would free the soldiers from their oaths, and the general would guard the church and keep the eastern tithes.
secrets.who: The Patriarch of Dawn and his closest monks.
secrets.proof: Eleven letters between Bogumil and Borislav in the library of the Dawn Cathedral at Velgrad.
secrets.ifr: The Dawn Church's founding would look like a tax revolt, and the Temple would use it in the Tessarian Civil War.

secrets.title: Where the Schism Tax went
secrets.pub: The Schism Tax of 738 paid the loyal armies after the east broke away.
secrets.truth: Temple officials used their half and part of the army's half to buy farmland in Varenna, Ostra and on the Morhaven Coast. This is how the Temple came to own about a sixth of that land.
secrets.who: The Holy See's treasurers; some Varennan landowners suspect.
secrets.proof: Land deeds dated 738–748 in the Holy See treasury at Solenne, paid in coin marked for the army.
secrets.ifr: Varenna, Ostra and Morhaven could claim the land back, cutting deep into the Temple's income.

secrets.title: The price of the Lantern Gate
secrets.pub: General Marcus Vell opened the Lantern Gate on Ash Night 759 out of pity for the starving city.
secrets.truth: High Luminary Benedict promised Vell a pardon and estates at Lavino to open it. Benedict also held back Temple grain so the city would turn to him.
secrets.who: The High Luminary's inner council; the Vell family.
secrets.proof: A deed of gift to Vell for Lavino in the Holy See archive, and a letter from Vell to his daughter, kept by the family.
secrets.ifr: The Holy See's founding would be shown as bought treachery, weakening its claim to rule Solenne.

secrets.title: The emperor's real killers
secrets.pub: Constantine IX died fighting Varennan soldiers on the palace stairs.
secrets.truth: Two Knights of the Sun, the Temple's own military order, killed him in his bedchamber before any Varennan reached the palace. Benedict never gave the order in writing.
secrets.who: The Grand Master of the Knights of the Sun.
secrets.proof: Constantine's signet ring is kept in the Knights of the Sun's chapter house in Solenne; a palace servant's account survives in a Varennan monastery.
secrets.ifr: The Temple would be known as the killer of the last emperor, and Varenna would have a reason to deny the Holy See's rule.

secrets.title: The Diver's Ferry
secrets.pub: Osric the Diver burned the Khan's boats at Yarbek in 882 and kept the riders off the Grey Channel.
secrets.truth: A secret clause of the Treaty of the Narrows (883) made Greyhaven ferry the Wind armies into the Free Marches: about 22,000 riders and 70,000 horses in 884 and more later, for 20,000 silver a year and a tenth of the Marches loot.
secrets.who: Each Tidewell king tells his heir; a few Nine Winds tale-tellers who still sing of 'the grey boats'.
secrets.proof: A copy of the ferry accounts for 884–890 in a sealed chest of the Greyhaven harbor archive; silver bars stamped with the Khan's horse mark in the Tidewell vault.
secrets.ifr: House Tidewell's hero legend breaks; the March towns and Velgrad would call Greyhaven the Khan's partner, and the Nine Winds could claim old treaty rights of passage over the channel.

secrets.title: The Forty Silent Days
secrets.pub: Khan Ulagan died in peace at Kharsa on 6 March 912.
secrets.truth: He died on 26 January 912. Khatun Saran hid the body in ice for 40 days, sent the news by yam only to the hearth tribes, and put her younger son Berek in Kharsa with the treasury before Temur heard.
secrets.who: The Kharsan khans, father to heir; the keepers of the Kharsa yam station passed down the story.
secrets.proof: The Kharsa yam tally cords for January to March 912, showing mourning riders sent out 39 days before the announcement, kept in the khan's tent-chest at Kharsa.
secrets.ifr: The four western tribes that backed Temur could claim the Kharsan khanship was stolen from the start and refuse the khan of 1105.

secrets.title: The Price of Temur's Head
secrets.pub: Temur Kharsan fell fighting in a raid in January 920, and Berek mourned him with a khan's funeral.
secrets.truth: Berek's agents paid Temur's guard captain 3,000 silver and a herd to kill him in his tent at Torkul. Berek then had the captain killed.
secrets.who: No one living is sure; a song of the western tribes, 'The Captain's Herd', hints at it.
secrets.proof: The captain was buried with a silver travel tablet bearing Berek's seal, in a small grave mound near Torkul.
secrets.ifr: The founder of the ruling Kharsan line would be known as a brother-killer, and the western tribes of the Nine Winds could use it to break the Compact.

secrets.title: Where the Black Cough Began
secrets.pub: The Black Cough was the Eternal Blue's punishment for the brothers' war, and it came from Temur's camps.
secrets.truth: The first cases were marmot hunters and fur dealers at Kyzai in Berek's own lands, in April 915, and the yam riders carried it along every road. Berek's scribes knew and blamed Temur. The true cause is still unknown to anyone in 1105.
secrets.who: Nobody knows it whole. Old Kharsan court scribes knew where it started.
secrets.proof: The yam tally cords of Kyzai and Kharsa for 915, and a fur-dealer's list of marmot bales at the first sick camps, in the khan's tent-chest at Kharsa.
secrets.ifr: The yams, pride of the Nine Winds, would be feared as plague roads, and the marmot fur trade could be banned in a panic.

secrets.title: The Ledger's Two Books
secrets.pub: Ilaria Lunetti the Ledger lent Morhaven the silver that saved it from the Khan.
secrets.truth: She lent Morhaven 60,000 silver at 12 percent a year, and at the same time her agents at Erkent bought furs and captives taken in the Free Marches from the Khan's governors. In 909 she called in the governors' loans first and seized their herds.
secrets.who: The heads of House Lunetti, who read the private books.
secrets.proof: Ilaria's private ledgers, in her own hand, in the House Lunetti vault at Ostra.
secrets.ifr: House Lunetti would be shamed for trading in captives; Morhaven could demand back the interest it paid; Temple courts could fine the house.

secrets.title: Sethril's Fall
secrets.pub: Sethril the Unwounded died peacefully in his sleep at about 417, unwounded to the end.
secrets.truth: Torchlight at his last bout brought on a seizure, the hidden cost of the Quickened blood. He fell against a stone stair and died five days later of the blow.
secrets.who: The Grove Keepers of Evenglade and the masters of Sylvaran's sword schools.
secrets.proof: The Grove Keepers' death record at Evenglade, and the school rule against bouts by torchlight.
secrets.ifr: Rivals would learn that the Quickened duelists of Sylvaran can be beaten by flickering light, a real weakness in any fight at night.

secrets.title: Zahir's Rider Guide
secrets.pub: The Giver of Water led Sultan Zahir across the Burning Waste to hidden water.
secrets.truth: A Sand Clan guide, a Rider and so a rival of the Wells, sold Zahir the route and three secret cisterns. In return Zahir swore never to send soldiers to the Well of Samar.
secrets.who: Clan Bahar of the Sand Clans; the Keeper of the House of Water in Qadira.
secrets.proof: The water-contract sealed with Zahir's ring, kept by Clan Bahar at Zarak; a copy in the House of Water at Qadira.
secrets.ifr: Qadir's story that God guided its founder would crack, and the Sand Clans could claim Qadir owes them its throne.

secrets.title: Irondeep's Arrowheads
secrets.pub: The Open Forge dispute was about Irondeep selling pots and tools too cheaply to humans.
secrets.truth: From about 896 to 911 Irondeep sold about 14,000 sets of lamellar plates and a great many arrowheads to the Wind Empire, through dealers in Kingsmere. The Judgment of 904 left the sales before it unpunished. Sales went on in secret for seven years after the Judgment of 904, until the Khan's wars ran down; those later sales broke the Judgment itself.
secrets.who: The Deepeye rulers of Irondeep and the Eldest Carver of Stonehold.
secrets.proof: Irondeep's sale tallies in the Deepeye vault; Wind lamellar plates with Irondeep maker's marks in old Kharsan graves near Kharsa.
secrets.ifr: Stonehold's Law-Carvers could reopen the case against Irondeep under the Deep Law, and Aldmark would be shamed that its merchants armed the steppe.

secrets.title: The Miracle of Morhaven
secrets.pub: In 897 the Sun struck the Khan's army with fever and saved Morhaven.
secrets.truth: King Tancred paid men to throw dead horses and cattle into the stream above the Khan's camp. The drought and the fouled water did the rest.
secrets.who: The Morhaven chancery clerks; a few Temple archivists.
secrets.proof: The garrison pay roll of 897 in the Morhaven chancery, which pays 'carrion carriers'; a Temple inquiry letter in the Holy See archive at Solenne.
secrets.ifr: The Temple's miracle would be exposed as a trick of war, embarrassing the Holy See and the crown of Morhaven.

secrets.title: Kingsmere's Tribute
secrets.pub: The Kingdom of Kingsmere never bowed to the Wind Empire; it only sent gifts of friendship.
secrets.truth: Kingsmere paid the Khan 6,000 silver and 500 horses every year from 881 to 912, as tribute, to keep the riders south of the Millrun.
secrets.who: Aldmark's treasury keepers; the Kharsan khans.
secrets.proof: Kingsmere treasury rolls for 881–912 listing 'gifts to the east', in the Oath Hall at Kingsmere; matching tribute tallies at Kharsa.
secrets.ifr: Aldmark's pride that the north never bowed would be broken, and the Nine Winds could mock the empire in any quarrel.

secrets.title: The lead gold of Tessar
secrets.pub: The Tessarian treasury kept sending gold to Ostra until the bankers turned greedy in 1044.
secrets.truth: From 1043 the Tirana camps were empty. Grand Treasurer Olivar Mentis sent 46 bars stamped with the imperial gold mark that were lead with a thin gold skin, to buy time.
secrets.who: House Lunetti's heads; Isabetta Lunetti found it in 1044; First Banker Cosimo Lunetti in 1105; the Tessarian mint-master's family.
secrets.proof: The cut-open bars lie in the Lunetti strong-room at Ostra, still in their sealed chests with Olivar's letters.
secrets.ifr: It would prove the Tessarian crown cheated its lenders, giving Ostra a legal claim to seize Tessarian goods and ruining both claimants' credit.

secrets.title: Who paid the corsairs of 1011
secrets.pub: Blackreef pirates attacked Morhaven in 1011 for loot, and Aurelio Falcone saved the city.
secrets.truth: Agents of Emperor Nikandros paid the Blackreef captains 30,000 new Leontines to sack Morhaven, Tessaria's rival port for March and channel trade. The contract also promised 30,000 more Leontines on success, which were never paid. That unpaid debt is why Blackreef kept the contract, and why it can still be sold.
secrets.who: The Brine line of Blackreef; a few old Tessarian court families; nobody in Morhaven.
secrets.proof: The hiring contract, sealed with a Tessarian treasury seal, is in the Brotherhood's chest at Blackreef.
secrets.ifr: Morhaven would demand payment from whichever Tessarian claimant wins, and could back the other.

secrets.title: The staged poisonings of Vikram
secrets.pub: Raja Vikram the Unpoisoned survived seven poisonings because the gods favored him.
secrets.truth: The first poisoning in 1001 was real, and Vikram survived because of his inborn liver trait. Three of the later six were staged by his own ministers to make his reign look blessed.
secrets.who: The high priests of two Ranpur temple families, one of them Govind the Elder of House Bhaskar, High Priest of the Great Temple.
secrets.proof: A temple ledger in Ranpur records payments to 'tasters who fell ill' in 1009, 1015 and 1026.
secrets.ifr: It would shame House Ranavir and weaken the temples that back Raja Indrajit.

secrets.title: Harald's broken truce
secrets.pub: Jarl Ulf Greymane broke a truce sworn on the iron ring at the Glenwash in 945, and Harald Ironside punished him.
secrets.truth: Harald broke the truce. Ulf's sister Sigrun told him where Ulf camped, and her price was marriage. By the faith of the Seven Halls, an oath-breaker drowns forever.
secrets.who: The Free Hall keepers of Wolfhaven; the Emperor of Aldmark's High Hall-Keeper.
secrets.proof: The Oath Hall record was taken by Emperor Hakon in 1002. A copy made in 946 is kept by the Free Halls at the Sea King's stones in Wolfhaven.
secrets.ifr: It would call the founder of Aldmark an oath-breaker and shake the Emperor's claim to head the faith.

secrets.title: The order for Kadah
secrets.pub: Rebels burned Kadah in 985 and killed 2,000 townsfolk for paying taxes to Tessaria.
secrets.truth: Tessarian hired soldiers did it on a written order sealed by Emperor Nikandros.
secrets.who: The flood-priests of Tamar; the King of Tamar.
secrets.proof: The captured order, in its seal-bag, is kept in the temple archive at Talim.
secrets.ifr: Tamar could use it to demand payment from Tessaria or to shame the Temple-backed claimant, Nikandros's heir.

secrets.title: The tenth of the gold
secrets.pub: The Treaty of the Tirana Heads (1004) split the upper Tirana gold fairly between Tessaria and Stonehold.
secrets.truth: A secret clause gives Stonehold a tenth of all gold Tessaria ever takes from the Free Marches, forever.
secrets.who: King Harvald Bardun and the Law-Carvers of Stonehold. The Tessarian copy burned in 1047.
secrets.proof: The clause is carved in the First Hall of Stonehold.
secrets.ifr: Stonehold would claim a share of any future Tirana gold, and would oppose any new expedition that ignores it.

secrets.title: The poisoned cattle of 1042
secrets.pub: The Red Widow simply grew fiercer with age.
secrets.truth: In 1042 Olivar Mentis paid herders to leave 30 cattle laced with wolfsbane and arsenic near the Widow's Crag. She ate some, fell sick for weeks and came back angrier. Her attacks of 1043 finished the gold camps.
secrets.who: Nobody alive for certain. One herder's son in the Marches tells the story.
secrets.proof: A page in Olivar Mentis's second ledger records 'thirty head, for the Crag, 1,100 Leontines'.
secrets.ifr: It would show the empire caused its own ruin and warn anyone planning a new move against the dragon.

secrets.title: Olivar's second ledger
secrets.pub: A mob hanged Grand Treasurer Olivar Mentis in 1047 because he had stolen the treasury's money.
secrets.truth: Emperor Anselm had the prison door left open. Olivar kept a second ledger showing that a fifth of all loans since 1027 went to Anselm's own household, palaces and gifts.
secrets.who: The lesser Patriarch of Dawn at Tessar; possibly Prince Andros Tessaran.
secrets.proof: The ledger is sewn into the binding of a Dawn Church prayer book in the lesser Patriarch's library at Tessar.
secrets.ifr: It would blacken Anselm's name and weaken his daughter Queen Livia's claim, helping Prince Andros.

secrets.title: Amenhar's birth
secrets.pub: Amenhar I, who freed Tamar, was the grandson of the exiled King Kheti III.
secrets.truth: Amenhar was the son of a Talim flood-priest. The male line of Kheti III had died out in exile; the priests forged Amenhar's birth roll and married him to Kheti's last granddaughter, Neferu (966–1031), so that his heirs would carry the royal blood.
secrets.who: The chief flood-priests of Talim, one generation at a time.
secrets.proof: The true birth roll, on papyrus in a sealed jar, is in the temple vault at Talim.
secrets.ifr: It would break the divine claim of the royal house of Tamar and hand power to the flood-priests.

secrets.title: The Thunder Horse
secrets.pub: In 1024 Gorath rode the Storm-Father's Thunder Horse at the Drum Stones.
secrets.truth: Gorath's kin drove a herd of wild horses past the stones in a thunderstorm. The shaman in the eagle-owl mask was paid in 200 horses.
secrets.who: The Grey Mothers of Gorath's clan. Harkun the Drum-Master, told by Oruk Owl-Mask in 1079.
secrets.proof: The winter-count hide of Gorath's clan, kept by the Grey Mothers at Urgol, shows the drive in a small picture for 1024.
secrets.ifr: It would strip the Line of Gorath of its holy claim and please the Tusk Clans.

secrets.title: Why two tribes held back
secrets.pub: The Nine Winds lost the Battle of the Salt Shore (1041) to the Horde's strength.
secrets.truth: Two of the nine tribes held back their riders because Gorath had promised them the winter grazing north of Kultau. He kept the promise.
secrets.who: The khans of those two tribes and the Horde's war-chief. Mother Shura, Keeper of the Grass, who takes a grass price of about 150 horses a year from…
secrets.proof: A knotted treaty cord is held by the shaman of one of the tribes at Kultau.
secrets.ifr: It would split the Nine Winds and could start a feud against the two tribes.

secrets.title: Lucerna's oil
secrets.pub: Sabra freed itself from Qadir by its own courage (1020–1025).
secrets.truth: Lucerna's bankers paid for Sabra's revolt. Sabra has sold Lucerna 400 jars of fire-oil a year ever since, in secret.
secrets.who: The Emir of Sabra; three members of Lucerna's council.
secrets.proof: Lucerna's arsenal books, kept in the arsenal at Lucerna, list the jars as 'lamp oil from the south'.
secrets.ifr: Qadir would treat it as an act of war by Lucerna. Every navy would want fire-oil too.

secrets.title: The Deathbed Words
secrets.pub: Anselm Six-Fingers named his daughter Livia heir on his deathbed in 1061, before the Luminary of Tessar and six witnesses.
secrets.truth: Anselm could no longer speak when the witnesses came in. All six were Temple men. The royal physician wrote on his wax tablets that the king died 'without a word or a sign'.
secrets.who: Queen Livia; High Luminary Severin III; the Needle-Keepers' archivist who holds the tablets; no witness is still alive.
secrets.proof: The physician's wax tablets, sealed in a lead box in the Temple archive at Solenne, shelf of Tessarian royal papers.
secrets.ifr: Livia's claim loses its only legal ground. Temple-faith lords could desert her, and the Temple would be shown to have made a queen with a lie.

secrets.title: Lucerna's share of the dragon toll
secrets.pub: Lucerna fought Blackreef in the Corsair War and still condemns the pirates and their dragon toll.
secrets.truth: A secret clause of the Peace of Ratrock (1056) gives Lucerna's council families one fifth of every dragon toll. The money passes through a front house in Ostra. About 9,000 marks a year.
secrets.who: Doge Tiberio Doravelli; four council families of Lucerna; First Banker Cosimo Lunetti; Captain-General Nell Brine.
secrets.proof: The Lucernan copy of the clause in the Doge's strongroom at Lucerna; the Ostran front house's ledgers in the Lunetti vault at Ostra;
secrets.ifr: Varenna, which paid for half the war, would feel betrayed. Merchants would refuse the toll. Lucerna's council could fall.

secrets.title: Sabra's oil behind the dragon
secrets.pub: A great fire-dragon guards the Corsair Isles.
secrets.truth: The 'dragon' is fire-oil from Sabra's seeps on the Gulf of Sands, sold to Blackreef since 1051 by three emirs in turn. Sabra takes payment in silver and in safe passage for its own ships.
secrets.who: Emir Karim Sabrani; his oil-master; Captain-General Nell Brine and about 40 pirates.
secrets.proof: The oil-master's tally sticks and shipping notes in the emir's treasury at Sabra; oil jars stamped with Sabra's well-mark in the store caves at Ratrock.
secrets.ifr: Lucerna, Varenna and Qadir would have cause for war on Sabra. The dragon toll would collapse, and Blackreef with it.

secrets.title: How Conrad Ironside died
secrets.pub: Emperor Conrad died of a winter fever at Kingsmere in 1081.
secrets.truth: Conrad drowned when the Fairrush ice broke under his horse. His dense Ironside bones took him straight down. The court hid it because of the whispered prophecy 'An Ironside will fall into the water and the empire with him'.
secrets.who: Emperor Aldwin; Lady Ysolde Ravenscar; two surviving huntsmen, pensioned on a farm near Swanvale.
secrets.proof: The two huntsmen at Swanvale; the body's river-soaked furs, burned, but the burning was noted in the palace wardrobe book at Kingsmere.
secrets.ifr: The prophecy would seem half-fulfilled. Oath-sworn lords might wait for the empire to fall and stop paying Aldwin.

secrets.title: The poison at the winter court
secrets.pub: Northreach says Aldmark poisoned King Bjorn in 1090. Aldmark says his belly burst.
secrets.truth: Bjorn was poisoned by a cook in the pay of Lady Ysolde Ravenscar, Aldmark's spymaster. She acted without Emperor Aldwin's order, to break Northreach's will. Aldwin does not know.
secrets.who: Lady Ysolde Ravenscar; the cook, who lives in Ostra under another name.
secrets.proof: The cook, in the dyers' quarter of Ostra; a payment line in Ravenscar's cipher ledger at Kingsmere.
secrets.ifr: Northreach would go to war again. Aldwin would have to punish or protect his spymaster, and either choice costs him.

secrets.title: Serra's proof
secrets.pub: The Needle-Keeper Ottavio Serra confessed in 1068 that his count was a lie of the Devourer.
secrets.truth: Serra proved the Common Reckoning is six years short. His notebook sets the Needle's count and the tree-ring count side by side, and they agree. The Book of Ash says the Light will fail again when those two counts agree.
secrets.who: High Luminary Severin III; the three senior Needle-Keepers; Queen Saelith of Eldergrove, who was sent a copy by Serra in 1067;
secrets.proof: Serra's notebook in the Needle-Keepers' vault under the Shadow Needle at Solenne; a copy in the archive at Silverbough.
secrets.ifr: Panic that the Light will fail. The Temple's authority over the calendar breaks. The Ashen would claim the prophecy is theirs.

secrets.title: The re-cut flood mark
secrets.pub: The Monuti flood of 1089 was fair, and the Flood Mother came back to King Amenhar V.
secrets.truth: The 1089 flood was low for the third year running. The flood-priests plastered over the old mark on the Flood Stairs and cut a new one. They cut the grain tax by a third to hide the poor harvest. By the faith's own law the king lost his right to rule.
secrets.who: King Amenhar V; High Flood-Priest Menna the Measurer; four stair-masons, two still alive.
secrets.proof: The old mark under the plaster of the Flood Stairs at Tamar; the temple tax roll for 1089 in the Flood Temple archive.
secrets.ifr: Amenhar V's right to rule would be void. The Delta Wells and rival temple families would move against him.

secrets.title: The switched boy
secrets.pub: The search monks found Tashen by the signs, and the old abbot's soul 'walked ahead' into him.
secrets.truth: The searchers first chose Norbu, a boy born in 1060 after the 12th Abbot's death. The abbey steward's faction swapped in Tashen, the son of the steward's cousin. The Red Stair's claimant is the boy who was found first.
secrets.who: Brother Pema, the last living search monk; Norbu of the Red Stair; Abbot Tashen, who learned it in 1090.
secrets.proof: The search diary of 1061, hidden by Brother Pema at Moonstair monastery.
secrets.ifr: The White Stair's abbot would be a fraud in the eyes of the faithful. Norbu could take Skyhold when Tashen dies.

secrets.title: The firstborn twin
secrets.pub: The Rememberers could not tell which of the twins Kaleb and Kiros was born first, so they split the crown.
secrets.truth: The Rememberers' knotted birth-cord record shows Kiros was born first. By old custom his line, now only his son Tekle, holds the better claim to the whole crown.
secrets.who: Rememberer Selam the Knot-Keeper; Prince Tekle Asfari suspects it.
secrets.proof: The birth-cord record of 1029 in the Rememberers' hall at Abara, in the chest of House Asfari.
secrets.ifr: Tekle could claim all of Abara. The twin kings would face civil war, and the Compact of 1053 would break.

secrets.title: Emberdeep's rising heat
secrets.pub: Emberdeep's hot springs are a gift of the Smith-Father, and the lower halls were sealed after an accident in 1050.
secrets.truth: Hilde's secret readings show the rock in the lowest galleries is 9 °C hotter than in 1050, and new steam vents opened in 1102. She is quietly cutting an escape road to Balmund.
secrets.who: Forge-Queen Hilde Hammerhand; the Law-Carvers of Emberdeep; 12 surveyors sworn to silence.
secrets.proof: The heat-tally stones in the sealed lower gallery of Emberdeep; the new tunnel works toward Balmund.
secrets.ifr: Panic in the hold. The prophecy 'the mountain will open' would seem to be coming true. Traders and smiths might flee.

secrets.title: The survivor's map
secrets.pub: No army can kill the Red Widow, and the gold of the upper Tirana is lost for good.
secrets.truth: Jory Flint, a survivor of 1097, saw a crossbow bolt tear her right wing. She turns slowly to the left and has not bred in 20 years. He drew a map of the gold streams and her dawn patrol route and sold it to Cosimo Lunetti.
secrets.who: Jory Flint; First Banker Cosimo Lunetti; Doge Tiberio Doravelli.
secrets.proof: The map in the Lunetti vault at Ostra; Jory Flint himself, drinking in Madara.
secrets.ifr: A new expedition would be raced by every power near the Marches. Queen Livia would pledge anything for the gold.

secrets.title: Fire-oil for Queen Livia
secrets.pub: The Nine Winds sell their fire-oil to nobody.
secrets.truth: Since 1103 Khan Ozbek has sold Queen Livia 30 jars of fire-oil a year. It goes by camel to Morhaven and by ship to Tessar. King Aurelio II takes a cut for letting it pass. Livia plans to burn Andros's winter camp at Coreria.
secrets.who: Khan Ozbek Kharsan; Queen Livia; King Aurelio II Falcone; Livia's master of engines.
secrets.proof: Bills of lading for 'lamp oil' in a merchant's warehouse at Felano; the jars in the queen's cellars at Tessar.
secrets.ifr: The Dawn Church and Velgrad would call it an atrocity. Morhaven would be dragged into the Tessarian war.

secrets.title: Vrag's heart
secrets.pub: War-Chief Vrag is strong and fearless, the true blood of Gorath.
secrets.truth: Vrag carries the Line of Gorath's weak heart. He has fainted twice after the blood-fury, in 1102 and 1103. The Grey Mothers expect him to die young, as his father and grandfather did.
secrets.who: Mother Ugra of the Grey Mothers; two of Vrag's bodyguards.
secrets.proof: Mother Ugra's healing-hide, painted with the winter each fainting happened, in her tent at Urgol.
secrets.ifr: Clans would begin choosing Vrag's successor now. Tarn Halfblood's followers would claim the prophecy points to Tarn instead.

secrets.title: Tarn's father
secrets.pub: Tarn Halfblood is the son of a nameless orc raider and a Hazelhollow farm girl.
secrets.truth: Tarn's father was Durgash Blood-Fist, son of Gorath, who took his mother, Maren of Hazelhollow, into his camp during the raids of 1072. Tarn is Vrag's half-brother and carries Gorath's blood.
secrets.who: Maren of Hazelhollow; Mother Ugra of the Grey Mothers; Tarn himself learned it in 1102.
secrets.proof: Maren's own word; Durgash's copper arm-ring given to Maren, which Tarn now wears; the Grey Mothers' winter-count hide for 1073.
secrets.ifr: Tarn would have the best claim to be the 'rider born of two peoples'. The Horde could split between the half-brothers. Aldmark would face a half-orc rising with a royal orc at its head.

secrets.title: The Ostran talks
secrets.pub: Queen Livia and Prince Andros will never speak to each other.
secrets.truth: Since 1102 their envoys have met secretly at Ostra, under Cosimo Lunetti's roof, to split the Neck for good: Livia keeps Tessar and the south, Andros the north, and the Neck road tolls are shared. Both churches would lose their say.
secrets.who: Queen Livia; Prince Andros; First Banker Cosimo Lunetti; one envoy of each.
secrets.proof: Two draft treaties in Cosimo Lunetti's study at Ostra.
secrets.ifr: High Luminary Severin and the Patriarch of Dawn would both unlight their own claimant. Velgrad would lose the Neck tolls it holds as security.

secrets.title: The false calf
secrets.pub: Moon-Pearl, the white elephant, is 58 and has no calf, and the dream will end when she dies without one.
secrets.truth: In 1101 the keepers of the white stable secretly bought a pale young elephant from Amber hunters. They hide it at a temple estate near Nagita and plan to show it as Moon-Pearl's calf, born 'in secret', when she dies.
secrets.who: Keeper Anand of the White Stable; three temple families; Raja Indrajit does not know.
secrets.proof: The young elephant at a temple estate near Nagita; the purchase record in Amberport's market roll.
secrets.ifr: A temple fraud at the heart of the kingdom. If exposed after Moon-Pearl's death, Ranpur would believe the dream has ended.

secrets.title: The staged rising
secrets.pub: The Black Dragon of Greyhaven will rise from the channel in 1105, 34 years after 1071.
secrets.truth: Channel-Master Radek Volan of Velgrad is buying pitch, sulfur and old hulls at Sevany. King Stanislav plans to fake the dragon's rising with fire rafts in 1105, panic Greyhaven and seize the channel tolls in the confusion.
secrets.who: King Stanislav Sevrin; Channel-Master Radek Volan; about 60 Velgradan sailors.
secrets.proof: Purchase ledgers at Sevany; the hulls, bought at Sevany and sailed south, moored in a creek that runs from the Dobava foothills down to the channel, almost opposite Greyhaven.
secrets.ifr: Greyhaven and Aldmark would go to war with Velgrad. Andros would lose his Velgradan ally in Tessaria.

secrets.title: The Ashmere clause
secrets.pub: The betrothal of Prince Harald and Princess Rowena is a friendly match between equals.
secrets.truth: King Edric signed a hidden clause: if Rowena has no son, Ashmere passes to the Emperor of Aldmark. He signed during one of his bold fits and has since sunk into a black mood.
secrets.who: King Edric Ashford; Emperor Aldwin; Lady Ysolde Ravenscar; Sir Owain Cinderwell, captain of Edric's guard, who witnessed it.
secrets.proof: Aldmark's copy in the imperial treaty chest at Kingsmere; Edric's copy in the royal chapel at Ashmere.
secrets.ifr: Ashmere's lords and Princess Rowena would refuse the match. Varenna would see Aldmark reaching for the western coast and could go to war.

secrets.title: The pale thrall's son
secrets.pub: Orrak the Walker (961–1011), founder of the Longwind line, was a Gashmar orc born to a Gashmar mother. Calling the Longwinds half human is only an old insult.
secrets.truth: Orrak's mother was Hilde, a Northfolk farm girl taken in the Gashmar raid over the Glenwash in August 954. She served seven winters as a herd-thrall, was adopted into a Gashmar kin in 961 and married the rider Varg Crow-Eye. Orrak, born that year, was half human, so every Longwind carries human blood.
secrets.who: The Grey Mothers of the Horde, who keep the hide; Brak Longwind, head of the line.
secrets.proof: The Grey Mothers' winter-count hide for 961, kept at Urgol, shows 'the winter the pale thrall bore a son'. Aldmark's own chronicles count the 140 captives of 954.
secrets.ifr: The Longwinds have been mocked as half human for 140 years. Proof would shame Brak on the war-chief's council, where he carries Vrag's most private words, and would cheer Tarn Halfblood's half-orcs, who could say the Horde's best runners were always of two…

creatures.name: Great Ash Dragon
creatures.habitat: High mountains with updrafts and hot springs
creatures.size: Wingspan 12–14 m; body 5 m nose to tail tip; 220–280 kg
creatures.behavior: Solitary, fiercely territorial over 5,000–12,000 km²; uses flame to stampede herds off cliffs and to drive rivals away, not to cook prey
creatures.weak: Thin wing membranes tear under arrows or crossbow bolts, and a torn wing grounds it; cannot take off quickly from flat ground;
creatures.belief: Worshipped by the Red Stair monks, who call them sky-kings; lowlanders believe they breathe fire for minutes and hoard gold

creatures.name: The Red Widow
creatures.habitat: The southern Free Marches and the northern Worldspine foothills around the Widow's Crag
creatures.size: Wingspan 14.2 m; about 275 kg; the largest Great Ash Dragon on record
creatures.behavior: Holds 12,000 km², patrols at dawn and dusk, returns to the Widow's Crag; kills anyone who nears her nest
creatures.weak: Old wing damage slows her turns to the left; she has not bred in 20 years and may be weakening
creatures.belief: Marchfolk say she is a punishment for the fall of the old empire; the Red Stair monks call her holy

creatures.name: Sunwall Wyvern
creatures.habitat: Cliffs and gorges of the Sunwall
creatures.behavior: Nests in colonies of 10–30 on sheer cliffs; mobs intruders
creatures.weak: Spray is short range and runs out after 4–5 bursts; it cannot fly in dead calm and struggles in heat of the day
creatures.belief: Qadiri children are told wyverns breathe fire and steal babies; herders believe their eggs cure blindness (they do not)

creatures.name: Sea Drake
creatures.habitat: Open sea and sea cliffs of the Western Ocean
creatures.behavior: Follows ships for scraps; harmless to people unless its nest is threatened
creatures.weak: Cannot take off from calm water; clumsy on land
creatures.belief: Sailors believe killing one brings a storm; Corsairs paint them on sails

creatures.name: Amber Wyrm
creatures.habitat: Rainforest and scrub of the Amber Isles and the Isle of Pearls
creatures.behavior: Ambush hunter; can run 20 km/h in short bursts and swims between islands
creatures.weak: Cold mornings make it slow; large spears to the neck
creatures.belief: Islanders call it the true dragon and say it breathes invisible fire (the venom)

creatures.name: Snow Drake
creatures.habitat: High valleys of the Crown Range
creatures.weak: Few left; a hard winter could end them
creatures.belief: Believed extinct since the last one was killed in 704 AR; highlanders' tales of white shapes in the cloud are dismissed as eagles

creatures.name: The Dragon of Blackreef
creatures.habitat: Waters around the Corsair Isles
creatures.belief: Merchants of the Middle Sea believe a great fire-dragon guards the Corsair Isles and pay 'dragon tolls' to Blackreef

creatures.name: The Black Dragon of Greyhaven
creatures.habitat: The Grey Channel near Smokewell
creatures.size: Said to be black and as large as a hill
creatures.belief: The people of Greyhaven believe a black dragon lives under the channel and rises every 34 years

creatures.name: Grey Leviathan
creatures.habitat: Deep water of the Western Ocean
creatures.behavior: Mostly solitary; ignores ships unless a ship crosses a hunt
creatures.weak: Must surface to breathe; harpoons from several boats can bleed it; it avoids shallow water
creatures.belief: Sailors believe the leviathans are the souls of drowned kings

creatures.name: Kraken
creatures.habitat: The deep ocean
creatures.size: Up to 18 m with tentacles; mantle 3 m; 400–600 kg
creatures.behavior: Never seen alive near the surface except when dying
creatures.weak: Loses buoyancy and dies in warm surface water
creatures.belief: Believed to drag ships under and to be as big as an island

creatures.name: Middle Sea Serpent
creatures.habitat: Deep water of the Middle Sea
creatures.weak: None needed
creatures.belief: Believed to be a sea serpent that eats sailors and whose appearance foretells earthquakes
creatures.truth: Real, harmless; the earthquake link is folk belief

creatures.name: Isle-Turtle
creatures.habitat: Warm seas of the Eastern Gulf
creatures.behavior: Floats at the surface to warm itself, sometimes for hours
creatures.weak: Slow on land; easy prey when nesting
creatures.belief: Sailors tell of landing on an island that sank beneath them
creatures.truth: Real; the sinking-island tale is exaggeration

creatures.name: Old Whiskers
creatures.habitat: The Salt Sea
creatures.behavior: Harmless, but can overturn a small boat when hooked
creatures.weak: Must enter rivers to spawn, where it is netted
creatures.belief: The Salt Sea monster that swallows horses; its eggs are said to give long life

creatures.name: The Black Maw
creatures.habitat: The deep Southern Ocean and Eastern Gulf
creatures.weak: Needs large prey; its numbers have fallen as whales were hunted
creatures.belief: Believed extinct: its fossil teeth ('stone tongues') are dug up and sold as charms

creatures.name: Giant Spider Crab
creatures.habitat: Cold deep water off the Corsair Isles
creatures.weak: Easily caught in pots
creatures.belief: Believed to drown fishermen by dragging them down

creatures.name: Sea Maidens
creatures.habitat: Warm coasts of the Middle Sea
creatures.weak: Easily hunted; their numbers are falling
creatures.belief: Sailors believe singing sea-maidens lure ships onto rocks

creatures.name: Unicorn horn
creatures.habitat: The White Coast and Whale Sound
creatures.belief: Southern courts believe unicorn horn cups sweat when poison is near; a horn sells for more than its weight in gold

creatures.name: Wolves of the Sea
creatures.habitat: Cold seas of the north and west
creatures.behavior: Pods of 5–30; curious about boats; do not attack people
creatures.belief: Northreach sailors believe they are the dead of the Sea King's hall and must not be harmed

creatures.name: The Grey Stag
creatures.habitat: Deep old-growth of the Evenwood
creatures.size: 2.1 m at the shoulder; antlers up to 3.6 m across; 600–700 kg
creatures.weak: Hunted out of every human land
creatures.belief: Humans believe it extinct and its antlers are sold as 'giant bones'

creatures.name: Aurochs
creatures.habitat: The Evenwood and the Elder Coast
creatures.size: 1.8 m at the shoulder; up to 1,000 kg
creatures.behavior: Bulls are aggressive; herds charge intruders
creatures.weak: Bulls can be trapped in pits
creatures.belief: Humans believe the last were killed in the north around 700 AR
creatures.truth: Believed extinct but alive (in elven lands)

creatures.name: The Evenwood Wolf
creatures.habitat: The Evenwood, the Pinewild
creatures.behavior: Avoids people; kills livestock at forest edges
creatures.weak: Poison and pit traps
creatures.belief: Northfolk tales of wolves the size of ponies

creatures.name: Wolf-men of the Pinewild
creatures.habitat: The Pinewild
creatures.belief: Trappers believe men who eat wolf meat turn into wolves

creatures.name: Hell Boar
creatures.habitat: Broadleaf forest and scrub of the Sunlands' hills
creatures.weak: Heavy boar spears; it charges in a straight line
creatures.belief: Morhaven farmers call it the Devourer's pig

creatures.name: Old Man of the Trees
creatures.habitat: Rainforest of the Deep Green
creatures.size: Up to 3.5 m tall standing; 1–2 tonnes
creatures.weak: Slow; hunted by spear
creatures.belief: Keshi tales of forest giants who walk like men

creatures.name: Cave Bear
creatures.habitat: Caves and forests of the Iron Mountains
creatures.size: 1.3 m at the shoulder on all fours; 3.5 m standing; 400–600 kg
creatures.weak: Sleeps deeply in winter
creatures.belief: Dwarves of Irondeep believe cave bears guard the ancestors' vaults
creatures.truth: Real (believed extinct everywhere except by the dwarves)

creatures.name: White Wyrm
creatures.habitat: Flooded caves under the Worldspine and Iron Mountains
creatures.weak: Slow on land
creatures.belief: Dwarves say it is a dragon's larva

creatures.name: Deepweaver
creatures.habitat: Caves of the Worldspine
creatures.weak: Needs cave humidity; dies in dry air
creatures.belief: Believed by miners to be the size of dogs

creatures.name: Knockers
creatures.habitat: Deep mines everywhere
creatures.belief: Dwarves and human miners believe small spirits knock to warn of danger (or to lure miners to death)

creatures.name: Crown Eagle
creatures.habitat: The Crown Range, the Ash Range, the Worldspine
creatures.weak: Nests can be robbed
creatures.belief: Believed to carry off children and lambs
creatures.truth: Real; child-snatching is rare but has happened

creatures.name: Griffin bones
creatures.habitat: The Burning Waste
creatures.belief: Salt miners believe griffins guard the gold of the desert and that the bones are of griffins killed by dragons

creatures.name: Snow Ape
creatures.habitat: Forests and snowfields of the eastern Worldspine
creatures.weak: Few and slow-breeding
creatures.belief: Ranpuri and dwarves call it the wild giant or snow-man, and some believe it is a giant cursed to walk alone

creatures.name: Bone-breaker
creatures.habitat: The Roof, the Worldspine, the Crown Range
creatures.belief: Skyfolk honor it at sky burials; lowlanders believe it drops tortoises and rocks on men

creatures.name: The Thunder Mammoth
creatures.habitat: Frostholm
creatures.behavior: Kept in loose herds by the giants
creatures.belief: Humans believe mammoths died out long ago; their frozen bodies found in the Frostfells are called dragon-kin

creatures.name: Woolly Rhino
creatures.habitat: The Eastern Steppe's northern edge
creatures.weak: Poor eyesight; can be pitted
creatures.belief: Humans believe the 'horned wool-beast' is extinct; the Tusk Clans do not

creatures.name: Cave Hyena
creatures.habitat: The Grass Sea and the Salt Steppe
creatures.weak: Fire and dogs
creatures.belief: Orcs believe hyenas carry the souls of the unburied

creatures.name: Horned Hare
creatures.habitat: The Grass Sea, the northern plains
creatures.belief: Believed to be a rare horned beast whose horn brings luck

creatures.name: The Thunder Horse
creatures.habitat: The Grass Sea
creatures.belief: Orcs believe the Storm-Father rides a horse the size of a hill across the sky

creatures.name: Basilisk
creatures.habitat: Rocky desert and scrub of the Red Waste and the Qadiri Coast
creatures.weak: Rinse the eyes at once; a shield or veil blocks the spray
creatures.belief: Believed to kill with a look
creatures.truth: Real (with a bite that can kill)

creatures.name: Sand Death-worm
creatures.habitat: The Red Waste
creatures.size: Said to be 2 m long and red, spitting acid
creatures.belief: Caravan men believe it spits acid and kills with lightning

creatures.name: Deathstalker
creatures.habitat: The Red Waste, the Burning Waste, the Gulf of Sands
creatures.behavior: Hides under stones; stings when stepped on
creatures.weak: Shake out boots and bedding; its venom is rarely fatal to healthy adults
creatures.belief: Believed to grow as big as horses in the deep desert

creatures.name: White Oryx
creatures.habitat: The Red Waste and the Thornveld
creatures.belief: Seen from the side the two horns look like one: the Sand Clans' 'unicorns'
creatures.truth: Real; the one-horn legend is an optical illusion

creatures.name: Fire Salamander
creatures.habitat: Everywhere wood is burned
creatures.belief: Believed to be born in fire and to be unharmed by it

creatures.name: Sand Dragon
creatures.habitat: The Red Waste's rocky margins and the Burning Waste
creatures.belief: Children believe it is a baby dragon

creatures.name: Great Crocodile
creatures.habitat: The Monuti delta, Lake Nubako and the Long Rift
creatures.weak: Cannot open its jaws against pressure: a bound snout is harmless
creatures.belief: Tamari believe crocodiles are the Flood Mother's guards and must not be killed during the flood

creatures.name: River Horse
creatures.habitat: The Monuti, the Long Rift lakes, the Golden Plains rivers
creatures.weak: Slow out of water only in short runs
creatures.belief: Tamari believe they are the Flood Mother's cattle

creatures.name: Hydra of the Greenmire
creatures.habitat: The Greenmire bogs
creatures.belief: Aldmark tales of a many-headed serpent that grows two heads for each one cut off

creatures.name: Green Anaconda
creatures.habitat: Swamps of the Deep Green and the Spice Coast
creatures.weak: Out of water it is slow
creatures.belief: Keshi believe the rivers are held in its coils

creatures.name: Wisplights
creatures.habitat: All bogs
creatures.belief: Believed to be spirits of the drowned leading travelers into the bog

creatures.name: Tiger of Ranpur
creatures.habitat: The Monsoon Coast and Worldspine foothills
creatures.weak: Hunted by beaters and elephants
creatures.belief: Ranpuri believe man-eaters carry the souls of murderers

creatures.name: White Elephant
creatures.habitat: Ranpur's royal stables and the Pearl Herd's grounds near Nagita
creatures.weak: Sunburn; poor eyesight
creatures.belief: Sacred to the Thousand Names; while it lives, the kingdom is blessed

creatures.name: World Python
creatures.habitat: The Deep Green, the Amber Isles, the Monsoon Coast
creatures.weak: Slow after a meal
creatures.belief: Believed to be the root of the world

creatures.name: Thunderbird of Great Amber
creatures.habitat: Rainforest of Great Amber
creatures.belief: Believed to be a god's messenger

creatures.name: The Roc
creatures.habitat: The interior of the Isle of Pearls
creatures.size: 3 m tall; 400–500 kg; eggs 30 cm long
creatures.weak: Easy to hunt; its eggs are stolen
creatures.belief: Sailors say the roc carries off elephants and that its eggs are as big as houses
creatures.truth: Real; the flight and elephant tales are false

creatures.name: Phoenix feathers
creatures.habitat: The Amber Wilds
creatures.belief: Believed to be the feathers of a bird that dies in flames and rises again

creatures.name: Forest Men
creatures.habitat: The Deep Green
creatures.behavior: Peaceful; males display and charge when threatened
creatures.belief: The Keshi believe they are people who fled into the forest to avoid work

creatures.name: Hael Hounds
creatures.habitat: The Ashlands
creatures.behavior: Wary of people but bold in packs at night
creatures.belief: Believed to be the ghosts of the Dimming's dead, guarding the cursed mountain
creatures.truth: Real; the ghost belief is folk faith

creatures.name: Cyclops skulls
creatures.habitat: The Isle of Vines and the Isle of Bells
creatures.belief: Believed to be skulls of one-eyed giants who ruled the isles before men

creatures.name: Mermen of Tamar
creatures.habitat: The Monuti delta
creatures.belief: Sailors believe the delta holds a race of fish-men

creatures.name: Steppe Eagle Owls
creatures.habitat: The Grass Sea, the Pinewild
creatures.belief: Orcs believe the owl carries a shaman's spirit on night flights

creatures.name: Lake Silara Serpent
creatures.habitat: Lake Silara in the Evenwood
creatures.belief: Human visitors report a lake serpent; elves find this funny

creatures.name: Frost Leviathan
creatures.habitat: Whale Sound and the whole Northern Ocean coast, west to Frostholm's capes
creatures.behavior: Slow and peaceful; like Earth's bowhead it ranges widely along the ice edge, so a whale struck in Whale Sound may turn up years later off Frostholm
creatures.weak: Slow, and floats when killed
creatures.belief: The giants of Hrimfell believe each one carries an ancestor's soul

creatures.name: Sky Serpent of the Roof
creatures.habitat: The Roof
creatures.belief: Skyfolk believe a serpent of light coils around the sun to guard it

creatures.name: Salt Sea Seals
creatures.habitat: The Salt Sea
creatures.belief: Nine Winds children believe they are drowned horsemen

creatures.name: Moon Moths
creatures.habitat: The Evenwood
creatures.belief: Elves believe the moths carry the souls of the newly dead up to the canopy

ladders.title: Soldier
ladders.holds: Himself or herself; stands in a mess of ten and a file of twenty
ladders.address: by name; 'you there' to a stranger

ladders.title: File-Leader
ladders.holds: A file of twenty: two messes of ten who eat, march and sleep together. He leads one mess himself and the senior soldier of the other answers to him

ladders.title: Sergeant
ladders.holds: A section of two files (forty), the squad's left or right hand

ladders.title: Sergeant-Major
ladders.holds: No command of his own: the company's senior non-commissioned man, who keeps the roll, the drill and the discipline for a company or a whole regiment

ladders.title: Squad Captain
ladders.holds: A squad of a hundred: his own file and two sections under their sergeants (20 + 40 + 40).

ladders.title: Captain
ladders.holds: A company of two hundred (two squads) with its sergeant-major, standard-bearer and horn

ladders.title: Senior Captain
ladders.holds: A wing of four companies, or an elite corps of that size; the first rung that commands other captains
ladders.address: 'Captain' to his face, 'Senior Captain' on the roll; 'Captain of Captains' in the Sunlands

ladders.title: Commander
ladders.holds: A regiment of four wings: the first rung that commands more than one kind of troop, and the first trusted with a mixed order of battle

ladders.title: General
ladders.holds: A battle of four regiments (van, main or rear, or a wing of the line), or an independent march or fortress command

ladders.title: High General
ladders.holds: A field army of four battles, or a whole theatre; in the Sunlands often styled 'Captain-General', on a border 'Warden of the March'

ladders.title: Marshal
ladders.holds: The whole field strength of a crown: every army, every theatre, every fleet that the sovereign does not lead in person.
ladders.size: 200,000 and up (or all of a small realm's host)

ladders.title: Supreme Commander
ladders.holds: The sovereign, who commands every soldier in law and some in fact. Not a rank to be earned: it comes with the crown, the khan's tablet, the…

ladders.title: Emperor
ladders.holds: A crown that holds other crowns: vassal kings or a league of lordships sworn on one oath

ladders.title: King
ladders.holds: A crowned head of one realm, answerable to no earthly lord

ladders.title: Sovereign Prince
ladders.holds: The elected or hereditary head of a small independent state that no king calls his vassal

ladders.title: Head of State
ladders.holds: A head of state who holds office by vote, lot, sign or acclaim and not by crown

ladders.title: Vassal King
ladders.holds: A crowned king who swears fealty to an emperor and keeps his own court, law and levy
ladders.address: Your Majesty (in his own land); Your Grace (at the imperial court)

ladders.title: Consort
ladders.holds: The sovereign's spouse. Crowned Consort (Queen, Empress) where law and the faith allow; otherwise 'Prince-Consort' or 'Khatun'

ladders.title: Heir
ladders.holds: The named or lawful successor: Crown Prince, Heir of the Veil, Forge-Princess, Heir of the Khan

ladders.title: Prince of the Realm
ladders.holds: A child of a sovereign who is not heir

ladders.title: Prince of the Blood
ladders.holds: A grandchild, sibling, nephew or niece of a sovereign, within three degrees of a crown

ladders.title: Duke
ladders.holds: A duchy: a province that was once a realm. Holds high justice, may raise his own host and mint small coin

ladders.title: Marquis
ladders.holds: A march: a border province held against a named enemy. Keeps a standing garrison, may build forts without leave and may treat with the enemy across…

ladders.title: Count
ladders.holds: A county: a walled city and its country; Earl in the north, Jarl in Northreach, Emir in the Sultanates, Chief in the clans
ladders.address: My Lord Count; My Lady Countess

ladders.title: Viscount
ladders.holds: The count's deputy or the lord of a great town inside a county; Reeve-Lord or Sheriff in the north

ladders.title: Baron
ladders.holds: A barony: a castle and 5 to 30 villages; Thane in Northreach and the dwarven holds; Lord of a place elsewhere

ladders.title: Banneret
ladders.holds: A knight with a banner: land for five to twenty lances, and leave to lead them under his own flag

ladders.title: Knight
ladders.holds: A manor or a stipend: one lance of the knight and 3-5 followers

ladders.title: Squire
ladders.holds: A knight's household youth or a landless man of arms in service

ladders.title: Franklin
ladders.holds: A free landholder with no title: yeoman, freeholder, soldier-farmer of 20-30 acres

ladders.title: Clerk
ladders.holds: Writes, counts, seals; lives on fees

ladders.title: Reeve
ladders.holds: Steward of a manor, a toll or a shire's rents; Bailiff in the south, Headman in the clans

ladders.title: Warden
ladders.holds: Keeper of a castle, a town, a gate or a toll road; Castellan, Provost, Harbor-Master

ladders.title: Master
ladders.holds: Head of an office or a guild: Master of Horse, Master of the Arsenal, Master of Doors, Master of Pilots

ladders.title: Great Officer
ladders.holds: One of the crown's five or six: Lord Chancellor, Lord Treasurer, Chief Justice, Master of the Household, Admiral, Marshal

ladders.title: First Minister
ladders.holds: The one who rules in the sovereign's name: Vizier, Grand Vizier, Chief Minister, Steward, Prince-Consort at Drevna

ladders.title: Novice
ladders.holds: Lay brother or sister, acolyte, apprentice shaman

ladders.title: Keeper
ladders.holds: A priest or priestess of one hall, shrine, grove, well or stair: Hall-Keeper, Needle-Keeper, Well-Keeper, Grove Keeper, Rememberer, shaman,…

ladders.title: Prior
ladders.holds: Head of a monastery, a great shrine or a valley's keepers: Abbess, Prior, Eldest Keeper of a grove, Master of the Search

ladders.title: Bishop
ladders.holds: Head of a faith inside one realm or one great province: Luminary, High Hall-Keeper, Chief Well-Keeper, Lesser Patriarch, Eldest Carver, Grey Mother,…

ladders.title: Patriarch
ladders.holds: Head of a faith across realms: High Luminary of the Temple, Patriarch of Dawn, the Abbot of the White Stair in Skyhold, the Eldest Grey Mother

tactics.name: Shield Wall
tactics.desc: Two to four ranks stand shoulder to shoulder, 0.6–0.8 m of front a man, shields overlapped, spears and swords working over and under the rims. It stops arrows and frontal charges as long as nobody runs; the front rank changes on a horn call every one to two minutes.
tactics.users: Ashmere, Northreach, Irondeep, Emberdeep, Stonehold, Velgrad, Drevna, Abara, Tessaria.

tactics.name: Shield Roof
tactics.desc: The front rank kneels behind its shields while the ranks behind hold theirs flat overhead, roofing a column against plunging arrows and stones. A column of 200 moves at a slow walk, about 1 km in 20 minutes, under walls or along forest roads.
tactics.users: Tamar (Sons of the Mother, with tall shields), Solenne, Varenna, Qadir, the dwarven holds.

tactics.name: Spear Wall
tactics.desc: A shield wall with 2.5–3 m spears in the first three ranks; the second and third ranks thrust past the first, so an attacker meets three points before he reaches a shield. Best in narrow places.
tactics.users: Irondeep, Stonehold, Zanara, Abara, Highland, Tamar.

tactics.name: Set Spear Line
tactics.desc: Spearmen kneel and set the butts of long spears in the ground, points at a horse's chest or a giant's knee and belly. The charger spits itself on its own weight. It needs nerve more than skill.
tactics.users: Drevna, Hrimfell's human harpooners, Northreach, Aldmark, Tessaria.

tactics.name: Pike Hedge
tactics.desc: A block of 4–6 m pikes five to eight ranks deep, with the points of the first five ranks out in front; an eight-rank hedge of 600 men holds a front of about 75 m. No horse breaks it from the front and elephants stop on it. It moves slowly and turns badly.
tactics.users: Abara, Stonehold, Irondeep, Highland (the Flightfolk eight-rank hedge).

tactics.name: Hidden Spear Line
tactics.desc: Spearmen lie flat in tall grass, a sunken road or behind a crest while horse or light troops draw the enemy on; at a horn call they rise 30–50 m in front of the pursuers and set spears.
tactics.users: Varenna, Morhaven, Abara, Ashmere.

tactics.name: Boar Spear Stand
tactics.desc: A file braces cross-barred boar spears against a charging beast or rider; the bar stops the point a hand deep so the spear is not lost and the next man can strike. A hunters' habit drilled for forest edges, where riders and beasts come singly.
tactics.users: Drevna, Velgrad, Aldmark's forest marches, the Tusk Clans' foot (Rhino Spear Lodge at Krarog).

tactics.name: Wyrm Spear Stand
tactics.desc: Three men with heavy cross-barred spears face an Amber Wyrm (7–9 m, bursts of 20 km/h) or a rush in thick forest: one takes the charge, two drive for the neck. In war the Wyrm Spears use it as a picket against rushes from the wet forest.
tactics.users: the Amber Isles (the Wyrm Spears, paid by the head since the bounty of 1022).

tactics.name: Bull's Horns Attack
tactics.desc: The Zanari attack: the chest (the center) closes with the enemy and holds him; two horns of young runners race around both flanks to meet behind him; the loins (the reserve) wait behind the chest. The horns close in 10–20 minutes, steered by drums.
tactics.users: Zanara; Abara copies it.

tactics.name: Hilltop Stand
tactics.desc: Taking the top of a hill and making the enemy climb: a man climbing a steep slope in mail is spent twice as fast, and arrows and stones carry farther downhill. If surrounded, the shields form a ring around the crest.
tactics.users: Abara, Ashmere, Highland, Varenna.

tactics.name: Gate Holding
tactics.desc: A few heavy men fill a gateway, stair or breach 2–4 m wide so that only two or three enemies can strike at once, with reserves rotating the front every two minutes.
tactics.users: Irondeep (Deep Gate Wardens), Stonehold, Emberdeep (Tharmund Gate Shields), Ashmere (Cinderwell Shield Guard).

tactics.name: Pass Holding
tactics.desc: A small force holds a pass or a neck of land: a barricade at the narrowest point, missile men on both slopes, a second line 1–2 km back. A thousand supplied men can stop ten thousand for weeks.
tactics.users: Highland, Qadir (Wardens of the Sabun), Greyhaven (Rift Watch), Velgrad, Ranpur (Nagora Road Wardens).

tactics.name: Ford Holding
tactics.desc: The enemy wades waist-deep at about 1 km an hour in a column 20–50 m wide; crossbows shoot into the crowd and spears meet the first men out of the water.
tactics.users: Aldmark, the Horde, Drevna, Abara (Monundi fords).

tactics.name: Road Station Hold
tactics.desc: Turning a walled caravan station (a stone court, a well, a tower and an inn) into a strongpoint of 50–200 men with crossbows. It closes the road and its tolls even when the enemy army marches past.
tactics.users: Tessaria (both claimants), Velgrad (the three pledged stations on the northern Neck road), the Nine Winds (yams).

tactics.name: Terrace Wall Defense
tactics.desc: Fighting among the dry-stone terraces of olive groves and vineyards: walls 1–1.5 m high every 20–40 m stop horsemen from wheeling, crossbowmen shoot from behind them, and knights wait for the moment.
tactics.users: Varenna, Morhaven, Abara (highland terraces).

tactics.name: Tunnel Holding
tactics.desc: Dwarven defense of a gallery about 2 m wide and high: a shield-file of three blocks it while war-picks and short spears strike past; doors, drop-stones and pits every 50 m; air shafts can be closed or fired to smoke the attacker.
tactics.users: Emberdeep, Irondeep, Stonehold.

tactics.name: Stake Line
