tactics.desc: Each man carries a 1.5–2 m stake sharpened at both ends; driven in at 45° in two or three staggered rows a pace apart in front of bows or crossbows, it takes about ten minutes to plant. Horses refuse it and orc relays break on it.
tactics.users: Aldmark (Gordush Stake-Men; also called the Stake Wall), Ashmere, Highland, Varenna, Drevna.

tactics.name: Ditch and Stakes
tactics.desc: A ditch 2 m deep and 2–3 m wide with the spoil thrown up as a bank and stakes on top; 1,000 men dig about 500 m in a day. It turns a field into a fort.
tactics.users: Varenna, Aldmark, Solenne, Ranpur.

tactics.name: Caltrop Field
tactics.desc: Four-pointed iron caltrops (one point always up, 4–6 cm long, about 50 g each) scattered two or three to a square meter in front of a line. Ten thousand weigh half a tonne. Horses and elephants go lame.
tactics.users: Stonehold, Emberdeep, Irondeep, Aldmark.

tactics.name: Pit Traps
tactics.desc: Pits 1–1.5 m deep with stakes in the bottom, covered with brushwood and turf; a line takes a night to dig. A 4-tonne elephant or a galloping horse breaks a leg.
tactics.users: Stonehold, Kesh hill folk (poisoned bamboo stakes), the Amber hill tribes, Sylvaran.

tactics.name: Felled-Tree Barricade
tactics.desc: Trees felled across a forest road with their branches toward the enemy; twenty axemen block 100 m in an hour, and archers shoot anyone who tries to clear it.
tactics.users: Sylvaran, Eldergrove, Highland forest clans, Northreach, Drevna.

tactics.name: Wagon Fort
tactics.desc: Wagons chained wheel to wheel in a ring or square, gaps closed with pavises or stakes; crossbowmen shoot from inside and between the wheels. A field army of 15,000 needs 600–1,000 wagons and deploys in about an hour.
tactics.users: Aldmark, Drevna, Highland companies, Tessaria.

tactics.name: Pass Wall
tactics.desc: A dry-stone or timber wall built across a pass in days or weeks, with a gate and a fighting platform.
tactics.users: Velgrad, Stonehold, Highland, Skyhold, Qadir.

tactics.name: Couched Lance Charge
tactics.desc: Heavy horse knee to knee, lances couched under the arm: walk, trot, canter, and only the last 50–100 m at the gallop. Horse and rider, about 700 kg at 30 km an hour, drive into one point. It breaks foot that wavers and does nothing against foot that holds.
tactics.users: Aldmark, Varenna, Morhaven, Solenne, Velgrad, Tessaria, Greyhaven.

tactics.name: Noon Charge
tactics.desc: A charge at midday in the desert summer, sun high behind the riders. Men bred to the heat ride fresh while the enemy, in mail at 40 °C, is half spent and dazzled.
tactics.users: the Sand Clans (Noon Lances of Bahar), Sabra, Solenne (the Knights of the Sun keep the name and the drill).

tactics.name: Flanking Charge
tactics.desc: Cavalry held on a wing until the enemy's line is fully engaged, then sent around into its side or rear, where only the end files can face it. Timing matters more than speed.
tactics.users: every army with horse, especially Aldmark, Varenna, Morhaven, Abara, Zanara (Golden Horse), the Horde and the Nine Winds.

tactics.name: Coast Road Charge
tactics.desc: Knights wait behind terrace walls or in a sunken coast road while enemy riders, checked by the walls and shot by crossbows, bunch up; then they charge down the road in a column four to six wide and spread into the crowd.
tactics.users: Varenna, Morhaven (Coast Road Knights).

tactics.name: Cavalry Sweep
tactics.desc: When a sally fails or a line breaks, horsemen sweep the open ground to catch men before they reach a gate, a camp or a wood. It kills more than the fight before it.
tactics.users: the Nine Winds, the Horde, Morhaven, Zanara, Aldmark, Abara.

tactics.name: Feigned Retreat
tactics.desc: A force pretends to break and runs, drawing pursuers out of order; on a signal it turns, while hidden reserves or flanking horse strike. Steppe riders feign for hours; the Wind riders once feigned for nine days. A feint can become a real rout if the men stop believing it.
tactics.users: the Nine Winds, the Horde, the Tusk Clans, Ashmere, Morhaven, Aldmark.

tactics.name: Elephant Charge
tactics.desc: Ten to sixty elephants advance 30–40 m apart, archers shooting from the howdahs, foot guards running at their legs; at 25 km an hour a 4–5 tonne beast scatters foot, and horses never trained with elephants bolt.
tactics.users: Ranpur, Zanara.

tactics.name: Elephant Screen
tactics.desc: Elephants stand in a line or at intervals in front of foot, a camp or a river crossing. Horses will not close with them, and the howdah archers shoot over the foot.
tactics.users: Ranpur, Zanara.

tactics.name: Camel Charge
tactics.desc: Camel lancers ride at enemy horse: horses that have never smelled camels shy away. Camels stand 2 m at the hump but start and turn slowly.
tactics.users: the Sand Clans, Sabra (Camel Guard), Qadir (hired clans).

tactics.name: Camel Screen
tactics.desc: Camels kneel in a ring or line with riders shooting from behind them: a wall against horse and a store of water at once. In the field, screens of camel riders close crossings and watch the wells.
tactics.users: the Sand Clans, Sabra, Qadir.

tactics.name: Chariot Charge
tactics.desc: Two-horse chariots with a driver and an archer or javelin man charge, shoot and wheel away; a dead horse stops the whole car. No realm fields chariots in 1105.
tactics.users: none in 1105.

tactics.name: Herd Screen
tactics.desc: Loose horses or cattle are driven ahead of the attacking riders to hide their numbers in the dust and break the enemy's front with their weight; the riders follow 200–300 m behind.
tactics.users: the Horde (its herd clans supply about 1,500 remounts a year), the Tusk Clans, the Nine Winds.

tactics.name: Yak Stampede
tactics.desc: Herders drive a herd of 100–300 yaks down a narrow valley or along a ledge into an enemy column: each beast weighs about 500 kg and the herd sweeps the path clear. It scatters an enemy without much killing, which suits Skyhold's rule.
tactics.users: Skyhold, the Red Stair herders.

tactics.name: Ring Hunt Drill
tactics.desc: Thousands of riders form a ring tens of kilometers across and close it over days, keeping their places by flag and horn; it is a winter hunt and a war drill at once. In war the same ring closes on an army.
tactics.users: the Nine Winds (the Ring Hunt of Kyztai, led by Serik Kharsan, ), Zanara.

tactics.name: Tiger Beat Drive
tactics.desc: A tiger hunt turned into drill: lines of beaters with drums and gongs drive a quarry (an enemy patrol, raiders, a scattered force) through grass and forest toward elephants and archers waiting at the end.
tactics.users: Ranpur.

tactics.name: Horse Archery
tactics.desc: Riders shoot the composite bow from the gallop, six to ten arrows a minute at 30–80 m, then wheel away; each carries 60 arrows and leads three to five horses. They wear the enemy down and rarely close until he breaks.
tactics.users: the Nine Winds, the Horde, the Tusk Clans, Morhaven (Santora Riders).

tactics.name: Backward Shot
tactics.desc: Shooting back over the horse's rump at full gallop, so the pursuit rides into the arrows. The core of every steppe feigned flight.
tactics.users: the Nine Winds (the Kharsa Arrow Field), the Horde, the Tusk Clans.

tactics.name: Howdah Archery
tactics.desc: Two or three archers in a timber howdah 3–4 m up shoot down over shields and pick out officers.
tactics.users: Ranpur, Zanara.

tactics.name: Massed Archery
tactics.desc: Hundreds or thousands of bowmen shoot at a high arc on command, six to ten arrows a minute each: 2,000 archers put 15,000 arrows into the air in a minute. Few kill through mail, but they wound, kill horses and break nerve.
tactics.users: Tamar (Ibis Archers), Zanara, Ranpur, Abara, Kesh.

tactics.name: Longbow Volley
tactics.desc: Men who draw 70–100 kg yew bows shoot 10–12 aimed arrows a minute at 200 m from behind stakes or from a slope, loosing together on a horn; a heavy arrow pierces mail at 60–100 m. A few thousand bowmen empty a charge in two minutes. Among humans only Ashmere trains for it;
tactics.users: Ashmere (King's Bowmen and village rolls).

tactics.name: Crossbow Volley
tactics.desc: Crossbowmen in two or three ranks shoot in turn, one rank loosing while the others span: two bolts a minute each with a belt-hook bow, one with a steel bow. A farmhand learns crossbow in weeks.
tactics.users: Highland, Aldmark, Varenna, Solenne, Ostra, Drevna, Stonehold, Emberdeep, Tessaria, Blackreef.

tactics.name: Wall Crossbow Relay
tactics.desc: On a wall, each master shooter has two or three loaders who span and pass bows; one loophole keeps up four to six shots a minute.
tactics.users: Solenne (Dorata Crossbows on the Valerian Wall), Ostra, Morhaven, Emberdeep.

tactics.name: Crossbow Line behind a Stream
tactics.desc: Crossbowmen behind a stream, a flooded ditch or a marsh edge: attackers slowed to a wade are shot at 30–60 m and cannot answer.
tactics.users: Aldmark, Drevna, Varenna, Tessaria.

tactics.name: Javelin Volley
tactics.desc: Light foot throw two or three javelins each at 15–30 m just before contact, then close or run. A javelin stuck in a shield drags it down; a volley kills horses and chariot teams.
tactics.users: Zanara, Abara, Kesh, the Amber hill tribes, Tamar, Qadir.

tactics.name: Sling Volley
tactics.desc: Slingers hurl lead or baked-clay bullets of 30–60 g at 100–200 m; a bullet breaks bones through padding and can stun through a helmet. A sling costs a penny; the skill takes years.
tactics.users: Skyhold (Stair Guard), Highland, Qadiri and Sand Clan hill folk, Kesh and Amber hill folk.

tactics.name: Dusk Volley
tactics.desc: Elven archers shoot as the light fails, when elven eyes (about three times human night sight) still see and human eyes do not; Eldergrove's longships close at dusk, sweep the enemy deck at 150 m and pull away before boarding. Mistwalker carriers, half-blind at noon, fight best now.
tactics.users: Eldergrove, Sylvaran.

tactics.name: Reed-Bank Archery
tactics.desc: Bowmen hide in reed beds and small boats along rivers and canals and shoot barge crews and marching columns at 30–80 m, then vanish into channels a stranger cannot follow.
tactics.users: Tamar (Ibis Archers), Sand Clan marsh folk of Wadiyah.

tactics.name: Silent Archery
tactics.desc: Rangers shoot from cover with no horn, no shout and no sign; men fall and nobody sees from where. Each ranger shoots, moves 20–30 m, and shoots again, by hand signal only.
tactics.users: Sylvaran, Eldergrove (Night Rangers of the Veil).

tactics.name: Starlight Shooting
tactics.desc: Elven archers shoot by starlight or a thin moon at 50–100 m, where a human sees nothing beyond 20 m.
tactics.users: Sylvaran, Eldergrove.

tactics.name: Skirmish Screen
tactics.desc: Light troops in loose order, 2–5 m apart, 100–300 m ahead of the line: they shoot, hide the deployment, fight the enemy's skirmishers and fall back through gaps when the lines close.
tactics.users: Varenna, Zanara, Abara, Tamar, Kesh, Ashmere, Morhaven.

tactics.name: Hit and Run
tactics.desc: A small mounted band strikes a camp, a column's tail or a watering place, kills and burns for 10–20 minutes, and is gone before formed troops arrive.
tactics.users: the Sand Clans, Sabra, the Horde, the Tusk Clans, the Nine Winds.

tactics.name: Cavalry Raid
tactics.desc: 500–3,000 riders go deep into enemy land for days, burning and driving off herds and avoiding battle; or a wing rides round in battle to loot the enemy camp.
tactics.users: Abara (Horsemen of the Monundi), the Horde, the Nine Winds, Zanara, Morhaven, Aldmark (Ravenscar Night Riders).

tactics.name: Camel Raid
tactics.desc: Camel riders cross waterless ground no horse can (a camel goes five to seven days without water in summer heat), strike caravans and water trains, and vanish.
tactics.users: the Sand Clans, Sabra, Qadir's hired clans.

tactics.name: Herd Raiding
tactics.desc: Driving off the enemy's horses and sheep to starve his riders and pay your own. A band of 500 riders can take 20,000 sheep in a season.
tactics.users: the Horde, the Tusk Clans, the Nine Winds (Red Wind raiders), the Sand Clans.

tactics.name: Night Raid
tactics.desc: A picked force of 50–1,000 strikes by night: it burns stores, ships or tents, kills sentries, takes prisoners and is gone before dawn. It needs guides, silence and the right moon.
tactics.users: Kesh, the Amber Isles, Northreach, Eldergrove, Sylvaran, Drevna, the Horde.

tactics.name: Night Fire Raid
tactics.desc: A night raid whose only aim is fire: riders or boats carry fire-oil pots or pitch torches to barges, wagons, haystacks or tents, throw and leave. One raid can burn a summer's grain.
tactics.users: the Nine Winds (Keepers of the Seeps), Kesh (Night Swimmers), Blackreef, the Horde (fire arrows).

tactics.name: Dawn Attack
tactics.desc: An army marches by night and strikes at first light, when the enemy is asleep, cold and unarmed; the first fifteen minutes decide it.
tactics.users: Ashmere, Aldmark, Northreach, Velgrad.

tactics.name: Supply Raid
tactics.desc: Striking the enemy's wagons, mule trains, barges and foragers instead of his army; an army without bread breaks within a week.
tactics.users: the Sand Clans, Drevna, Sylvaran, Highland, Northreach, Kesh.

tactics.name: Convoy Ambush
tactics.desc: Waiting for a guarded convoy where it must string out (a gorge, a ford, a forest track) and striking its head and tail at once.
tactics.users: Stonehold, Highland, the Sand Clans, Kesh, Sylvaran.

tactics.name: Forest Ambush
tactics.desc: A column on a forest track, often 1–2 km long and two or three abreast, is struck from both sides at close range where it cannot form.
tactics.users: Sylvaran, Eldergrove, Northreach, Drevna, Kesh, the Amber hill tribes, Highland forest clans.

tactics.name: Hill Ambush
tactics.desc: Troops hidden behind a crest or in side valleys strike an enemy drawn past them, often after a feigned retreat, charging downhill.
tactics.users: Ashmere, Abara, Highland, Varenna.

tactics.name: Pass Ambush
tactics.desc: A column strung out in a pass (8,000 men over 6 km at Albora) is struck from the heights at its head, its tail and its baggage.
tactics.users: Highland, Qadir, Sabra, Skyhold, Velgrad.

tactics.name: Fog Ambush
tactics.desc: Men who know the ground strike a column in river or sea fog at 20–50 m, when it cannot see its own flanks or signals.
tactics.users: Northreach, Eldergrove, Greyhaven.

tactics.name: Ice Edge Ambush
tactics.desc: Giants and their harpooners wait where boats or sledges must land at the edge of sea ice or shore ice, and break them with stones and clubs as they come in.
tactics.users: Hrimfell, Frostholm.

tactics.name: Tree Stand Ambush
tactics.desc: Rangers on hidden platforms 6–15 m up in trees beside roads shoot down over shields and cross from tree to tree by branch and rope.
tactics.users: Sylvaran (stands overlook every road across the Oak Line), Eldergrove.

tactics.name: Rockfall Ambush
tactics.desc: Boulders stacked above a gorge road behind timber props are released by pulling a pin; one fall closes the road and kills dozens.
tactics.users: Highland, Stonehold, Skyhold, Qadir, the Hrimfell giants.

tactics.name: Ski Raid
tactics.desc: Raiders on skis cover 40–60 km a day over snow where horses founder, burn stores and are gone.
tactics.users: Northreach (the Ice Walkers and the Ski Yard of Saltbridge).

tactics.name: Winter Sled Raid
tactics.desc: Horse-drawn sledges carry raiders and loot over frozen rivers and lakes at 40–60 km a day; from December to March the Lakeland is one great road.
tactics.users: Velgrad, Drevna (Sled Riders).

tactics.name: Ridge Running Raid
tactics.desc: Runners move along ridge crests and wall tops where no rider can follow, 30–40 km a day across mountains, to scout a camp, strike it from above and run.
tactics.users: Highland (Stonefoot Cliff Runners).

tactics.name: Night March
tactics.desc: Moving an army by night, without lights or talk, to arrive at dawn or to slip away: 15–25 km in a night with guides. Columns get lost easily.
tactics.users: Ashmere, Zanara, Aldmark, Northreach.

tactics.name: Desert Night March
tactics.desc: In the deserts the army moves from dusk to dawn and lies up in shade through the day; a man walking by night needs about half the water. Guides steer by the stars from well to well.
tactics.users: the Sand Clans, Sabra, Qadir.

tactics.name: Winter Campaign
tactics.desc: Fighting in the season nobody fights: frozen rivers carry armies and hay stores can be burned, but men freeze and horses starve.
tactics.users: Northreach, Drevna, the giants of Frostholm and Hrimfell (who fight only in the cold), the Tusk Clans' Ironhide band, Velgrad (reluctantly).

tactics.name: Ice Crossing
tactics.desc: Crossing river, lake or sea ice: about 10 cm of sound ice holds men walking in file 5 m apart, 20 cm a horse, 30 cm a loaded sledge. Men carry poles, test the ice with axes and never bunch.
tactics.users: Northreach, Drevna, Velgrad.

tactics.name: River Crossing
tactics.desc: Forcing a river by boats, rafts, a bridge of boats or a ford found at night; archers cover the far bank and the first troops over hold a bridgehead while the rest follow.
tactics.users: every army; Aldmark, Zanara, Tamar and the Horde most often.

tactics.name: Seizing the Bridge
tactics.desc: A fast party races ahead to take a bridge before it is broken, or the guards are bought or killed; both ends are then held.
tactics.users: Tessaria, Aldmark, Varenna, Ostra.

tactics.name: Road Clearing
tactics.desc: Clearing a forest road for a column: axemen cut 30–50 m back on each side while shield men cover them and scouts work the trees; 2–5 km a day.
tactics.users: Aldmark (on the Sylvaran border), Ranpur, the Amber Isles (highland march).

tactics.name: Mule-Train Resupply
tactics.desc: Mule trains carry about 100 kg a mule at 25–30 km a day over mountain paths carts cannot use; 500 mules carry 50 tonnes, food for 10,000 men for five days. Skyhold uses yaks the same way.
tactics.users: Highland, Stonehold, Qadir, Varenna (Crown passes), Skyhold.

tactics.name: Runner Relays
tactics.desc: Runners carry messages 15–20 km each and hand on; a relay covers 200–300 km a day, and a picked runner alone covers 100 km. It needs no horses and works in hill and forest.
tactics.users: Zanara (Runner Guard), the Horde (Longwind Runners), Sylvaran (Lightfoot Scouts).

tactics.name: Relay Horses
tactics.desc: Riders change to fresh horses at stations every 25–40 km, or each leads three to five horses: a courier does 150–250 km a day, a steppe army 60–100 km a day for a week.
tactics.users: the Nine Winds (yams since 873; Yam Riders), Morhaven, Aldmark, the Horde.

tactics.name: Night Supply Run
tactics.desc: Food is carried into a besieged place by night: sledges over lake ice, boats with muffled oars, mules on goat paths.
tactics.users: Drevna (Sled Riders), Kesh, Highland.

tactics.name: Sea Resupply
tactics.desc: Feeding a besieged port or a coastal army by sea: a 100-tonne cog carries bread for 10,000 men for eight to ten days, so a city fed by sea cannot be starved by land.
tactics.users: Morhaven, Lucerna, Greyhaven, Varenna, Tessaria (Livia's 12 galleys).

tactics.name: Scorched Earth
tactics.desc: Burning crops, granaries and villages, breaking mills and driving off herds in the enemy's path so his army starves. It ruins one's own people too.
tactics.users: Drevna, Northreach, Velgrad, the Tusk Clans.

tactics.name: Burning the Grass
tactics.desc: Firing the dry steppe behind you, or ahead of the enemy, so his horses have nothing to eat for 100 km. It works from July to October.
tactics.users: the Nine Winds, the Horde, the Tusk Clans.

tactics.name: Forest Burning
tactics.desc: Burning a forest edge to deny archers their cover; it takes a dry summer and an east wind, and it burns villages and hunting grounds with it.
tactics.users: Aldmark keeps it as a threat; the elves fear it above all.

tactics.name: Fouling the Water
tactics.desc: Carcasses, dung or salt thrown into wells, cisterns or the stream above an enemy camp; the flux follows within days.
tactics.users: Morhaven, the Sand Clans, Sabra, the Horde.

tactics.name: Well Denial
tactics.desc: Holding, filling or fouling the wells on a desert or steppe road so that an army must turn back or die of thirst.
tactics.users: the Sand Clans, the Nine Winds, Sabra, Qadir.

tactics.name: Dyke Cutting
tactics.desc: Breaking river dykes or canal banks so the flood drowns roads and camps; in Tamar the August flood turns the valley into a lake.
tactics.users: Tamar, Varenna (Palella), Drevna.

tactics.name: Caravan Screen
tactics.desc: Riders escort a caravan in a moving ring 1–3 km out: scouts ahead, horse archers on the flanks, a reserve behind. They chase raiders off rather than fight them.
tactics.users: the Tusk Clans (Toll Riders of Kraoth), the Sand Clans (Salt Road Escort), the Nine Winds, Qadir.

tactics.name: Pilgrim Road Escort
tactics.desc: Mailed knights and sergeants ride ahead of and behind pilgrim bands on the Sun Road and the roads to Solenne, using chapter houses as stations. The same drill guards the Well of Samar and the Bluespire circuit.
tactics.users: Solenne (Knights of the Sun), the Sand Clans (Riders of the Well), Skyhold (circuit wardens).

tactics.name: Smoke Screen
tactics.desc: Wet straw, green wood or tarred pots burned upwind to hide boats, a landing or a withdrawal; at sea, smoke rafts.
tactics.users: Blackreef, Kesh, Greyhaven.

tactics.name: Dragon Show
tactics.desc: Fire-oil burned on the water at night in long streams and shapes, with horns, gongs and a few burning hulls, so that crews believe a fire-dragon guards the isles.
tactics.users: Blackreef (the Forty, the only people who know the whole secret).

tactics.name: Drum Storm
tactics.desc: Hundreds of war-drums, a thousand at full muster, beat together as the relay waves charge: untrained horses shy and bolt, horn calls are drowned, and the Dravic royal line, whose ears cannot bear it, collapses.
tactics.users: the Tusk Clans (the Drum Band), the Horde (the Drum Lodge).

tactics.name: Far-Eye Signal
tactics.desc: Towers with flag and fire codes, read by the sharpest eyes: Falcone carriers read a banner at 3 km and spot sails at 30 km, and messages pass 10 km a step.
tactics.users: Morhaven (Tower Watch), Greyhaven (Beaconstone), Varenna (Tibata Strait Tower).

tactics.name: Sun at Back
tactics.desc: Choosing the field and the hour so the sun is behind your army and in the enemy's eyes: face west in the morning, east in the afternoon. Archers aim worse into the sun.
tactics.users: Solenne, the Sand Clans (Noon Lances).

tactics.name: Night Scouting
tactics.desc: Riders or rangers go out after dark, find the enemy's camp fires, count them and return before dawn; owl-eyed families do it best.
tactics.users: Aldmark (Ravenscar Night Riders), Eldergrove (Night Rangers), Sylvaran, the Horde.

tactics.name: Siege Lines
tactics.desc: A ditch and palisade facing the town, and often a second facing outward against relief; a town 1.5 km across needs lines 6–8 km long and 6,000–8,000 men to hold them.
tactics.users: Varenna, Ranpur, Aldmark, Tessaria (Andros), Zanara.

tactics.name: Starvation Siege
tactics.desc: Waiting for hunger. A town with six months' food falls in six months; a castle stocked for two years, like the Citadel of Vitia, laughs at it. The besiegers starve too unless they are supplied.
tactics.users: Tamar, Abara, Tessaria, Zanara, Varenna.

tactics.name: Escalade
tactics.desc: Assault with ladders 1–2 m longer than the wall is high, 10–20 for every 100 m of wall, each carried by six men; climbers go up with shields over their heads. Costly, and used where walls are low or the garrison thin.
tactics.users: the Horde, Aldmark, Varenna, Zanara.

tactics.name: Night Escalade
tactics.desc: Ladders by night against a weak stretch of wall, a silent approach, the guards killed, and a gate opened from inside.
tactics.users: the Horde (one of its clans trains ladder parties: the one siege skill the Horde has).

tactics.name: Siege Tower Assault
tactics.desc: A wheeled timber tower taller than the wall, faced with wet hides, is pushed across a filled ditch and drops a bridge onto the wall-walk. It takes weeks to build.
tactics.users: Tessaria (Andros), Varenna, Aldmark, Ranpur.

tactics.name: Stone-Thrower Bombardment
tactics.desc: Traction stone-throwers pulled by teams of 15–80 men throw stones of 3–40 kg at 80–150 m, two to four shots a minute with a good crew. They smash parapets, hoardings and roofs but rarely breach thick walls.
tactics.users: most realms, chiefly Varenna, Aldmark, Ranpur, Zanara, Qadir.

tactics.name: Counterweight Bombardment
tactics.desc: The counterweight trebuchet drops a box of 5–10 tonnes of earth and stone and throws 50–100 kg stones 150–300 m, one shot every five to ten minutes, always to the same spot. It breaks towers, walls and siege towers. It costs about 5,000 suns to build, and its aiming tables are a secret.
tactics.users: Tessaria (two engines on Tessar's walls; the Engine Yard), Aldmark (Crossmarch and the Imperial Engine Corps), Varenna (two, carried in pieces), and the few…

tactics.name: Mining Under Walls
tactics.desc: A gallery dug under a wall's footing and propped with timber; the props are burned and the wall falls. A mine takes 30–60 days.
tactics.users: Ranpur (Miners of Tirpur), Stonehold, Irondeep, Emberdeep.

tactics.name: Seizing the Gate
tactics.desc: A sudden rush takes a gate before it can be shut: the force arrives faster than the news (runners, a night march) or hides among carts and cattle.
tactics.users: Zanara, Tessaria, the Horde.

tactics.name: Night Gate Opening
tactics.desc: A traitor or a bought man opens a gate at night to a waiting force. It is cheaper than any siege and is how most strong towns fall; Andros's habit of paying unpaid garrisons is its daylight cousin.
tactics.users: Tessaria, Ostra, and anyone with money.

tactics.name: Counter-Mining
tactics.desc: Listening for enemy digging (bowls of water ripple, dry peas jump on a drumskin), then digging to meet the mine and fighting in the dark, or firing and smoking it.
tactics.users: Irondeep, Stonehold, Emberdeep, Morhaven (the Deep Walls' listening galleries).

tactics.name: Flooding the Tunnels
tactics.desc: Dwarves turn the water from their waterwheel pumps or open sluices into an enemy mine.
tactics.users: Stonehold (Kelfast Sappers), Irondeep.

tactics.name: Night Sally
tactics.desc: Defenders slip out at night to burn engines, kill sappers or break into the siege lines, and return before the besiegers can form.
tactics.users: Tessaria (Livia), Morhaven, Varenna, Solenne.

tactics.name: Scalding Water Pour
tactics.desc: Boiling water or hot sand poured from hoardings and murder holes onto men at the gate; sand gets inside mail. Emberdeep pipes water from its own hot springs to the Tharmund Gate.
tactics.users: Emberdeep, Stonehold, Irondeep, every walled town.

tactics.name: Wet Hide Screen
tactics.desc: Fresh wet ox hides hung over hoardings, towers and ship sides, or carried as shields, against fire arrows and fire-pots, with sand and vinegar kept ready. Fire-oil still burns through in time.
tactics.users: Qadir (Sea Keep Marines), Varenna, Morhaven, Tessaria.

tactics.name: Fort Chain
tactics.desc: A line of small forts within signal of each other and a day's march apart, each holding 50–300 men, to watch valleys, roads or coasts and starve out raiders.
tactics.users: Morhaven (towers every 10 km), Aldmark (Crown Wall forts), Varenna (Albora Watch), Ranpur (Nagora road forts), Qadir.

tactics.name: Harbor Chain
tactics.desc: An iron chain on timber floats is raised across a harbor mouth between two towers by windlass; it stops galleys and cogs.
tactics.users: Greyhaven, Morhaven, Ostra, Kesh, the Amber Isles, Eldergrove (Nimthil), Velgrad (Sevany), Tamar (Marira), Blackreef.

tactics.name: Lagoon Chain
tactics.desc: Lucerna's chain across the lagoon mouth between the Lagoon Chain Towers (built under Doge Renato Salvi, 866–883), with sunken stakes in the side channels that only Lucernan pilots can pass.
tactics.users: Lucerna.

tactics.name: Harbor Blockade
tactics.desc: Galleys and armed cogs patrol outside a port to stop all ships. Galleys must water and beach every two or three days, so blockades leak and break up in winter storms.
tactics.users: Lucerna (the grain blockade), Varenna, Greyhaven, the Amber Isles, Qadir.

tactics.name: River Blockade
tactics.desc: Chained boats, war canoes or galleys across a river or harbor mouth.
tactics.users: Tamar, Qadir, Zanara (war canoes on the Mosawa and Tedana), Drevna, Varenna.

tactics.name: Galley Ramming
tactics.desc: The rowers sprint for the last 200 m at 12–15 km an hour and drive the iron-shod beak into the enemy's side or across his oar bank, breaking oars and men.
tactics.users: Varenna, Lucerna, Greyhaven, Velgrad, Qadir, Ostra, Kesh, the Amber Isles.

tactics.name: Boarding Action
tactics.desc: Grapnels thrown, a crossbow volley across the gap, then marines over the bow; most sea battles end in boarding.
tactics.users: every navy; Lucerna (Lagoon Marines), Qadir, Velgrad (Sevany Hooks), Kesh (Monuro Marines), the Amber Isles (Sultan's Marines), Greyhaven (Chain Guard).

tactics.name: Fire Ship
tactics.desc: An old hull filled with pitch, straw and oil is sailed or drifted downwind into an anchored fleet at night; the crew leaves by boat at 100–200 m.
tactics.users: Kesh, the Amber Isles, Greyhaven, Sabra, Blackreef.

tactics.name: Fire Raft
tactics.desc: Log rafts heaped with pitch and brush, with fire-oil where it can be had, set adrift on the tide or the current into ships at anchor. Cheaper than a fire ship.
tactics.users: Blackreef (dozens hidden on Gull Isle), Velgrad, Sabra.

tactics.name: Fire-Oil Pots
tactics.desc: Clay pots of fire-oil with a burning rag, thrown by hand to 20–30 m or by engine to about 150 m; the fire sticks, floats and burns on water.
tactics.users: the Nine Winds (Keepers of the Seeps), Sabra (Fire-Boat Crews), and in secret Lucerna, Blackreef and Queen Livia of Tessaria.

tactics.name: Beach Landing
tactics.desc: Galleys and longships run bow-first onto a beach; marines and archers jump into knee-deep water and form on the sand. Horses are slow and dangerous to land.
tactics.users: Northreach, Varenna, the Amber Isles, Lucerna.

tactics.name: Mist Landing
tactics.desc: Longships come in under morning sea mist, steering by the sound of the surf, and land archers first.
tactics.users: Eldergrove.

tactics.name: Night Tide Attack
tactics.desc: Boats ride the ebb or the flood at night, oars muffled with rags, silently into or out of a harbor.
tactics.users: Blackreef, Greyhaven, Eldergrove, Northreach.

tactics.name: Seizing the Ships
tactics.desc: At a signal, an enemy's merchant ships are seized in one's own ports, or cut out at anchor by night.
tactics.users: Ostra, Lucerna, Blackreef, Varenna.

tactics.name: Shoal Luring
tactics.desc: Light ships flee into reefs and shoals they know by heart; heavier pursuers run aground.
tactics.users: Blackreef (Shoal Pilots), the Amber Isles.

tactics.name: Landing behind Enemy Lines
tactics.desc: Troops are carried by sea past the enemy's front and landed behind it.
tactics.users: Varenna, Greyhaven, Lucerna.

tactics.name: Pinning against the Coast
tactics.desc: An enemy army is driven against a coast or a river with no ships behind it, until it must surrender or drown.
tactics.users: Tessaria, Morhaven, Varenna.

tactics.name: Lodestone Night Run
tactics.desc: A pilot who holds the lodestone needle can keep a course on a starless night or in fog, so his ships run a blockade or strike at dawn from where nobody looked.
tactics.users: Lucerna (Night Pilots), Greyhaven, the Amber Isles.

tactics.name: Relay Charge
tactics.desc: Orc waves of 100–300 riders or foot strike for about two minutes and pull back 100–200 m to recover for about 30 seconds while the next wave strikes; drums time the waves. Six to ten waves keep up the pressure for 15–20 minutes, and then the whole band is spent.
tactics.users: the Horde, the Tusk Clans.

tactics.name: Blood Fury Charge
tactics.desc: The first relay wave is led by carriers of the blood fury of the Line of Gorath: for three to five minutes they feel no fear and strike faster and harder, then faint grey-lipped.
tactics.users: the Horde (Gorath's Hearth Guard under Grask Firstwave).

tactics.name: Hide Wall Charge
tactics.desc: The thick-skinned riders of Clan Ironhide form the front of the first wave behind the drums; cuts are shallow on them, though bolts still kill.
tactics.users: the Tusk Clans (Ironhide Hearth Band).

tactics.name: Laughing Charge
tactics.desc: Varenna's Laughing Company charges first. Its Montaro cousins feel little pain or fear and laugh as they go in; the men around them take heart. Many die later of wounds they never noticed.
tactics.users: Varenna.

tactics.name: Back-to-Back Pairs
tactics.desc: Giants fight in pairs, back to back, because a giant needs about three seconds to turn; each covers the other's back while they break gates, boats and shield walls. Human harpooners guard their knees.
tactics.users: Frostholm, Hrimfell.

tactics.name: Thin-Air Retreat
tactics.desc: Falling back uphill above 3,000 m, where lowlanders sicken within a day or two (headache, vomiting, breathlessness), while the defenders cut the supply road and wait.
tactics.users: Skyhold, Stonehold (Crown Shelf Guard).

chronicle: Traders see the mammoths
Northreach tin traders at Haugberg see giants driving small mammoths hauling timber.
House Corso raised to nobility
After a dry summer, Adela Corso's cogs bring Qadiri grain to Morhaven at the old price. At Harvest Home King Aurelio II raises House Corso to the nobility.
Nagora pepper reaches the north
Ranpur finishes its cart road over the Nagora Pass and sends its own pepper north overland.
The Great Blizzard of the Northern Steppe
A three-day blizzard sweeps the Northern Steppe and the caravan road. The Gorak clans lose about a third of their sheep, and a silk caravan of 60 people loses…
Death of Emperor Conrad the Stubborn
Emperor Conrad Ironside dies at 68 after reigning 49 years.
Coronation of Emperor Aldwin
Aldwin Ironside, 32, swears on the iron ring in the Oath Hall and is crowned Emperor of Aldmark on Return Day 1081, four months after his father's death.
The Kyzai fire
The old jar store of fire-oil at Kyzai catches fire in summer heat and burns for two days.
The Dwarf's Gate is built
About 400 dwarves of Stonehold raise a stone gatehouse across the new Nagora road in five weeks and turn back Ranpur's caravans. The Nagora War begins.
Urza takes the rule
At the Great Ride at Grakmar, Urza Ironhide, 16, takes the War-Mother's spear back from Mother Krasha, and the council of clan-mothers ends its rule for her.
Battle of Tiravi
In 1082 Stonehold built a gatehouse across the Nagora road and began the Nagora War.
The flogging of the forty drivers
After the defeat at Tiravi, Prince Indrajit has 40 elephant drivers flogged at Tirpur and dismissed for the panic that broke his charge.
Crash of the Leontine
Queen Livia's mint cuts the silver in the Leontine to two parts in five. Marches merchants refuse the coin.
Death of Queen Gwenith
Queen Gwenith of Swanburg, wife of King Edric for 15 years, dies at Ashmere. Princess Rowena, their only living child, is 13.
The first great loans to Queen Livia
Treasurer Crispin Dorn lends Queen Livia 250,000 suns of Temple money through House Lunetti after her Leontine crashed.
Coronation of King Osric IV Tidewell
King Osric III Tidewell dies. His son Osric IV, 26, deaf from years of deep diving, is crowned at Greyhaven.
The Sabena Citadel begun
After the riots of 1083, the Twelve build a citadel over the Sabena docks, paid for mostly by House Pell and House Lunetti. It is finished in 1086.
The fall of the Dwarf's Gate
Ranpuri miners win the third race under the dwarven gatehouse on the Nagora road and bring down a tower. The dwarves withdraw in order to Mormund.
The Seep Stockade and the death oath
Khan Ozbek makes Duran Master of the Seeps and builds the Seep Stockade near Kyzai, with earth walls and a ditch around the jar stores.
Killing winter on the Goroth grass
Ice seals the grass of the Goroth and Salt Edge grazing for six weeks. The eastern clans lose about a third of their horses; some families lose everything.
Treaty of Tirpur
The Nagora War ends after Ranpuri miners brought down a tower of the dwarven gatehouse in 1084. The pass stays Ranpur's.
Eirik weds Sigrid Winterborn
Prince Eirik Winterborn, 25, marries his cousin Sigrid Winterborn of the Stagflow branch at the Sea King's stones.
The spinning wheel comes to the Palella
House Calvane buys the first twenty spinning wheels from the Camia wheelwright Jacopo Brisa, who built one in 1084 from a Ranpuri trader's account of the…
Coronation of Queen Milena Dravic
King Yaromir Dravic dies at 71. His daughter Milena, 29, is crowned by the Patriarch of Dawn at Drevna.
Blackreef burns Tibata harbor
Blackreef raiders come into Tibata harbor at night, burn the fishing fleet and the harbor sheds, and carry off cargo.
The Cloud Ridge chief killed
Highland Spears from Aming ambush the chief of the Cloud Ridge clan on a raid against a tapping camp and kill him with eleven of his men.
Death of old Toghrul
Toghrul Kharsan, the khan forced out in 1079, dies at his daughters' camp at Ersgol, aged 74.
Settlers for the Whale Coast
Queen Milena sends settlers and whalers north to the Whale Coast and makes Stepan Kolin Lord of Dobin. Whaling stations are built along Whale Sound.
Blood-price of the Krugak wells
At the Great Ride, Ushkar the Grey and the Grey Mothers end the four-year feud between the Redhand clans and the Goroth clans over the wells of the Krugak.
Karim Sabrani becomes Emir of Sabra
Emir Nasir Sabrani dies. His son Karim, 32, takes the emirate. Nasir's father Farid had died in 1060.
Renewal of the rye at Thardush
Queen Milena's envoys meet the War-Mother at the Thardush cairns and renew the Treaty of Thardush for the new reign.
Tariq Bahar chosen Speaker of the Sand Clans
After Speaker Malik Bahar dies, the clan council at Zarak chooses Tariq Bahar, 38, as Speaker.
Truce of the Cedars
Livia and Andros agree a truce at Feleria after plague and the coin crash empty both treasuries. It lasts nine years.
Morhaven's neutral trade compact
Two weeks after the Truce of the Cedars, King Aurelio II signs separate letters with Queen Livia and Prince Andros.
The hungry winter of Irondeep
With barley short, Queen Brynja sells iron to Aldmark at half price for grain to keep the hold fed.
The crown prince marries Nefret
In the Hungry Year Crown Prince Amenhar marries his cousin Nefret, daughter of Princess Tiye.
Gurz made Master of the Silk Tolls
Mother Hulda Tallyhand, who kept the Kraoth count for 21 years, dies. War-Mother Urza names her son Gurz, 27, Master of the Silk Tolls.
Old Ironjaw sinks the Golden Gull
A scarred Grey Leviathan bull rams and sinks the Lucernan cog Golden Gull, 180 tonnes, west of the Strait of Hael. 34 drown.
Coronation of King Roderic III Valdane
Queen Lucilla dies in April at 68. Her son Roderic III, 26, is crowned by the Temple at Varenna on Return Day.
Riot at the tin fair
Drunk Northreach sailors riot at the Skarfell fair and try to break into Skarfell Hall.
Election of High Luminary Severin III
High Luminary Clement IV the Stern dies at 82 after 38 years. The Luminaries elect Severin III, 57.
Tamar's Hungry Year
The Monuti flood fails in 1087 and again in 1088. About 80,000 people die in Tamar.
The Edict of the Halls
On Oathfather's Day 1089 Emperor Aldwin, as head of the Seven Halls, proclaims that every hall-priest in Northreach and the Highland League must be confirmed…
Coronation of King Amenhar V
King Amenhar IV dies in March after two failed floods. His son Amenhar V, 23, is crowned as the Flood Mother's divine son.
The October gale of 1089
A gale off Ithira breaks up the longship Sea Hawk; one man, Faron Stormrail, comes ashore in her boat.
Flood of 1089 declared fair
The flood-priests read the Flood Stairs and declare the flood of 1089 'fair'. Amenhar V keeps his throne.
The grain contract renewed
Tamar renews the grain contract of 645 with Lucerna's factors on harder terms: the crown repays the Hungry Years' debt of about 300,000 suns in wheat below the…
The old Steward's confession
Lobsang Snowborn, Steward until he fell sick in 1089, dies at the White Stair in January 1090.
Death of Mother Yazra
Mother Yazra, Elder of the Grey Mothers since 1044, dies at Urgol at 87. The Grey Mothers name Ugra, 48, Elder.
Coronation of the twin kings Yared and Yonas
King Kaleb died in March 1089 and King Kiros in November 1089. Kaleb's twin sons Yared and Yonas, 20, are crowned to share the throne in alternate years.
Death of King Bjorn Winterborn
On New Year's Day 1089 Emperor Aldwin claimed the right to confirm every hall-priest in Northreach and the Highland League.
Coronation of King Eirik III Winterborn
Bjorn's son Eirik III, 30, is crowned at Wolfhaven on Lantern Night. He swears on the Oathfather's ring to keep the Free Halls.
The Falcone marriage pact
King Roderic III marries Bianca Falcone, daughter of King Aurelio II of Morhaven, at Varenna. Each kingdom promises the other 2,000 men in war.
Exile of Prince Tekle Asfari
Tekle Asfari, 28, son of King Kiros, is banished from Abara after he calls the new twin kings usurpers. He goes to Tessar.
Prince Tristan's ring dive
On Return Day Prince Tristan, seven, dives for the silver ring before the whole harbor and comes up holding it. The crowd cheers him as a true Tidewell.
Coronation of Raja Indrajit Ranavir
Raja Devraj Ranavir dies. His son Indrajit, 32, victor of the Nagora War, is crowned at Ranpur.
The Rag Compact
At Marira Rasha the Ragwoman of Qadira, Nofret the Weaver and Yunus Marari seal the Rag Compact: Qadiri rag-buyers get first pick of Tamari linen rags at a…
The Silver of the Halls
The Council of Valleys lends King Eirik III of Northreach 40,000 highland silver for the Rising, to be repaid by 1111, and lets 400 volunteers march north.
Bolts for the hird
During the Northreach Rising, Captain Torsten Grimhelm of the Iron Road guard meets Kettil Frost's men in the hills.
Battle of the Stagflow
An Aldmark army of 12,000 marching on Saltbridge is ambushed by Eirik III's 5,000 at the Stagflow fords in fog. Aldmark loses 2,500 and retreats.
Cosimo Lunetti heads the Council of Twelve
First Banker Lorenzo Lunetti dies. The Council of Twelve of Ostra chooses his son Cosimo, 38, to lead it.
Fight at the Brightwash ford
A Varennan patrol led by Dario Montaro clashes with Ashmere bowmen at a Brightwash ford over a stolen barge. An arrowhead lodges near Dario's spine.
Banking compact with House Lunetti renewed
High Luminary Severin III renews the banking compact: House Lunetti holds the Temple's coin and lends it at 8 in 100 to kings the Temple names.
The Winter Crossing
King Eirik III leads 800 men on skis and foot over the frozen mouth of the Glenwash by night and burns Aldmark's winter grain stores at Brightmoor.
Fire in the Kabale galleries
Fire in the timbers of the south gallery at Kabale kills 60 slaves. The lamp-carrier Sadiki leads Lady Amara's surveyors out through the smoke and is freed for…
Coronation of Sultan Zahir IV
Sultan Zahir III of Qadir dies. His son Zahir IV, 35, becomes Sultan and Guardian of the Water at Qadira.
The Thing of 1092
Bergthor of Haugberg speaks against Chieftain Skarvi for four hours and loses by two halls. Vermund Farcast throws 31 m.
The blockade of Wolfhaven
In the Northreach Rising a Greyhaven squadron blockades Wolfhaven for Aldmark. It loses two galleys to Northreach longships in a night raid, and Tide Divers…
The blockade of Wolfhaven broken
Twenty Greyhaven and Aldmark ships have blockaded Wolfhaven since June. On an August night ebb Kettil Frost leads eight longships out and burns two Greyhaven…
The first keels at Miruma
Grand Admiral Jalal Zahiri lays the keels of four war galleys at Miruma. By 1104 there are 34, built at Miruma and the Sea Keep for about 680,000 suns.
Death of Nuru Keshari the Boneless
Nuru Keshari, 57, falls from the roof of the Pepper Hall at Kesh during the Harvest Home climb. His son Amani, 32, becomes Prince.
Birth of Prince Vikram
Rani Sita, Raja Indrajit's queen and cousin, bears a son who lives. He is named Vikram for his great-grandfather, and the palace cook's daughter Tara Moti…
The night raid off Madamo
Tekook rowers under the stroke oar Fikri Laut row two galleys into the Madamo roads by night and take three Keshi smugglers' boats carrying cloves out of the…
Eirik's letter
On the night before the Accord of Coldhaven, King Eirik III signs a private letter to Emperor Aldwin promising not to raise his father's death for ten years.
Accord of Coldhaven
The Northreach Rising ends at Coldhaven. Aldmark drops its claim. The Free Halls of Northreach and the Highland League keep choosing their own priests.
Albano retaken
General Vittor Montaro takes Albano back from rebel tenants who had seized its granary after two hungry years in the Ashland March.
Skulls of the Long Rift clay
Bone-diggers of Abara find very old skulls with heavy brows and small braincases in the Long Rift clay beds.
Coronation of Emperor Mosi III Kanemba
Emperor Mosi II dies after 48 years on the throne. His son Mosi III, 31, is crowned on the Ancestor Hill at Zanara.
The queen's new Leontine
On Livia's Crowning Day the Tessar mint under Lady Cassia Mentis strikes a new Leontine with half again the silver of the old.
The Mirona road massacre
A column of 31 pilgrims is robbed and killed on the Mirona road. The See blames Ashen heretics and hangs two shepherds of Mirona.
Rook Brine lost at sea
Captain-General Rook Brine's galley founders in an October storm off Wreck Isle, with all 90 aboard.
The Ashen riot at the royal chapel
On Ash Night 1094 about 200 men of the Ashen cult storm the royal chapel of Ashmere, crying that Mount Cinder will bury a court that worships the sun.
Death of Ulzag Redhand
Ulzag Redhand, chief of the Magak clans for 32 years, dies of a stroke at 53. By Redhand custom the staff goes to his sister's son, Skarn, 28.
Jamila becomes Pearl-Master
Jamila Sabrani, who bought the boats of three ruined pearl masters in 1093, is chosen Pearl-Master of Azara.
Hrimfell Raids begin
Giants of Hrimfell burn the Drevnan whaling station at Yarov after its whalers kill two Frost Leviathans.
Ulric Greycloak named Captain-General
The Council of Valleys names Ulric Greycloak, 40, Captain-General of the League, the first Greycloak to hold the office in 60 years.
The Harrak guest-killing
In a feud over winter grass, a guest of Clan Harrak is stabbed to death at the Burnak camp.
The Redley galley loan
Lord Godric Redley lends the crown 60,000 tides to rebuild the galley fleet.
King Yonas's court borrows from the Gold Houses
King Yonas's court, short of silver in the odd years, borrows against its even years from the Gold Houses of Zanara.
Election of Doge Tiberio Doravelli
Doge Pietro Salvi of Lucerna dies. The council elects Tiberio Doravelli, 56, and the High Luminary crowns him.
The Well Riders voted down
At the Horse Feast kurultai Idris of the Sea Wind asks for a Well-Keeper to sit beside the chief shaman. The chiefs vote him down six to three.
Fight at the Torholm shore
300 Drevnan spearmen and crossbowmen catch a giant raiding party near the Torholm shore on a warm day and kill two giants.
Redsail galleys turned back at Felano
Dame Serena Falcone, 21, spots five Blackreef galleys 28 km off Felano at dawn. The harbor chain rises before they arrive, and the galleys burn two fishing…
Fight at the Shagnak wells
About 900 Nine Winds raiders drive off Salt Edge herds near Shagnak. Ushkar sends 600 of the Hearth Guard, who catch them at the wells and break them in four…
Battle of Felina
Queen Livia breaks the Truce of the Cedars. Her 6,000 attack Andros's 5,000 at Felina, and Andros holds the town.
Death of Rani Sita
Rani Sita Ranavir dies bearing a stillborn son, her fifth dead child. Raja Indrajit does not marry again.
Stanislav weds Zora Koren
Prince Stanislav of Velgrad marries Zora Koren, 20, daughter of the Lord Marshal Zoran Koren, in the Dawn Cathedral.
Yrsa Windbellows walled out
Eldest Carver Bolli Ashgrave reads the exile of the bellows-wright Yrsa Windbellows for selling drawings of a water-driven bellows to the Chanari smith Ravi…
Samir named heir; Nadira made Keeper of the Purse
On Well Day 1097 Sultan Zahir IV names his son Samir, 16, as heir before the Well-Keepers, and makes Nadira Hassani Keeper of the Purse.
Giants break Dobin's harbor gate
30 giants fighting in pairs break Dobin's harbor gate and burn 14 whaling boats. One giant dies of crossbow wounds.
Ambush at Tower Nine
Dame Oriana Sabine chases Horde raiders off the steppe edge beyond Santora and rides into an ambush. 120 Santora Riders die.
Red Widow destroys the third gold expedition
The Company of the Golden Stream, 300 men with 40 hired dwarf crossbowmen, paid for by Lucerna and Ostra, reaches the gold streams. The Red Widow kills 190.
The Quiet Doubters
Abbess Dechen of Moonstair and abbots tired of the split form the Quiet Doubters on the Council of Abbots.
The heir faints at Sevmir
At a meeting with Tusk envoys at Sevmir, the envoys' escort beats the greeting on their drums and Princess Ludmila, 18, collapses.
Three Greywave cogs lost
Three cogs of House Greywave are lost on the southern run near the Strait of Hael, where the leviathan Old Ironjaw has sunk ships since 1088.
Zayd Blackveil exiled
Zayd of Clan Sayf kills a Marir man who had killed his cousin, at the well of Marir and within sight of the water.
The Loati channel
Dawit Mekonen has his engineer Fikru dig a channel to carry part of a Loati headwater stream to the Mekonen terraces.
Truce of Dobin
After giants break Dobin's harbor gate in 1097, Queen Milena and King Hraldr agree a truce at Dobin. Drevna forbids its whalers to kill Frost Leviathans.
The survivor's map sold
Jory Flint, one of eleven survivors of the third gold expedition, sells Cosimo Lunetti a map of the upper Tirana gold streams and the Red Widow's dawn patrol…
Earthquake on the Rift Coast
An earthquake cracks the wall of Falconhaven Pass and throws down houses along the channel shore.
The Thing refuses the hunters
At the Thing of 1098 Arvo Sealbane, newly chosen Headman of the Hunters, asks for a human seat at the Thing and the right for hunter families to leave their…
Vrag chosen War-Chief of the Horde
Ushkar the Grey dies in the spring. At the Great Ride at the Drum Stones the Grey Mothers choose Vrag, 26, grandson of Gorath, as war-chief.
Coronation of King Stanislav Sevrin
King Dobrin Sevrin of Velgrad dies. His son Stanislav, 27 and a head taller than other men, is crowned by the Patriarch of Dawn.
The carrion roll found
Sorting the chancery rolls, Lord Chancellor Emilio Castor finds the garrison pay roll of 897, which pays 'carrion carriers' in the last weeks of the siege.
The Striped Death is killed
Raja Indrajit shoots the man-eating tiger of Chanari from an elephant's back. It had killed about 200 people since 1090.
The Master's loan
House Goldvein's ruby seam at Dramhall fails.
A taster for Queen Livia
At Queen Livia's request, Doge Tiberio Doravelli sends his son Nerio to Tessar as her food-taster.
Baptism of Prince Radoslav
King Stanislav's son Radoslav, named for Radoslav the Bear, is baptized by Patriarch Kirill on Dawn Feast.
Hael Hounds kill Varennan surveyors
A pack of feral Hael Hounds tears apart two Varennan surveyors mapping the Ashlands for new farms.
Isaria Vale refused
The sun-sisters elect the half-elf Isaria Vale their Mother. High Luminary Severin III refuses to confirm her because she is half-elf.
A toll-hand at the Drowning Post
A Ratrock toll-boat hand is tied to the Drowning Post at low tide for a short count of the dragon toll. The tide takes him.
The Thing of 1099
Skarvi beats Bergthor by three halls. Bergthor swears before all the halls that he will challenge again in 1106. Sva counts 3,160 giants on the island.
Helga Stonefoot elected First Speaker
First Speaker Hugo Redford dies. The League's council elects Helga Stonefoot, 48, the girl who saved the child from the eagle's ledge in 1063.
Founding of the Miners' Moot
After a Northreach ship returns four runaway families under the Tin Compact, the tribute-folk's headman Colm Ashby calls the first Miners' Moot in a flooded…
Coronation of Sultan Iskandar Maruang
Sultan Harun II Maruang dies. His son Iskandar, 35, becomes Sultan of the Amber Isles.
The bargain at the waterfall
After a winter of hunger, Lintang Cloudwalker meets the Warden of the Highlands, Hamzah Batu, alone at Amtiuan Falls.
Tahir takes the fire-boats
Emir Karim gives his son Tahir, 22, command of the 30 fire-boats and their 600 crewmen, trained by Saad the Burnt at the Oil Yard of Zariya.
Silk toll raised at Lubany
Drevna raises the toll on silk caravans at Lubany. King Stanislav of Velgrad threatens to close the Tolek to Drevnan barges.
The new walls of Stagley
King Edric raises new stone walls at Stagley, facing Varenna, with 120,000 suns borrowed from House Lunetti of Ostra. Sir Godwin Ashdown oversees the work.
First toll rise at Kraoth
Gurz the Toll-Keeper raises the Kraoth toll from one part in twelve to one part in eleven. In 1103 he raises it again, to one part in ten.
Qadiri paper for the Temple
Hamid the Papermaker agrees to sell rag paper straight to the Temple scriptoria of Solenne through Ostran factors.
A roc egg in Amberport
Pearl divers sell a roc egg holding 10 litres at Amberport's market. It goes to the sultan's treasury.
The pale calf bought at Amberport
Ranpuri temple agents buy a young pale elephant cow at Amberport's market from hunters of the Amber highlands and ship her to a temple estate near Nagita.
The Merah cloves burned
After a rich harvest, the sultan's men burn about 2,000 bales of House Merah's cloves in Amberport harbor to hold the price.
The herring fails in the North Fjords
The herring shoals of the North Fjords fail. The Herring and Seal Hall of Ithira goes into debt to House Saltleaf for salt.
The night landing on the West Strand
Ilvara Mistwalker's Night Rangers land by night and burn a smugglers' camp cutting unmarked fir on the West Strand.
The first believing diver freed
A dying slave diver asks Chief Well-Keeper Mahmud the Just for the Book's blessing.
Death of the first prince
The eldest son of King Amenhar V and Queen Nefret dies of the blood sickness, aged 11. His brother Khaset, 5, is named heir.
Amani Keshari weds Laila Maruang
Prince Amani Keshari marries Laila Maruang, Sultan Iskandar's sister, at Kesh.
Crown Prince Hrodgar's practice climb
Crown Prince Hrodgar climbs Mount Bardun with one guide of the Crown Shelf Guard to prepare for the heir's climb.
New vents and the Lotus Loan
Emberdeep borrows 40,000 lotus from the temple banks of Ranpur at 12% a year against its gem output. Road-Warden Orm Coppertooth carries the terms.
Dragons nest above Kardeep
A pair of Great Ash Dragons comes to nest on new warm ground above the Kardeep gold mines. The upper galleries are abandoned.
Nia Tembo surveys the east road
The surveyor Nia Tembo walks and measures a route east from Tandi through the Eastern Uplands to Atani and the Abari border.
The Venina tithe strike
The tenant widow Agnese leads her village in refusing the Luminary of Varenna's rent collectors. By 1104 the strike has spread to 40 villages.
The Amber loan for 20 ships
The League borrows about 200,000 suns from Amber merchants to build 20 new fighting ships at Rehema's yards in Monuro.
The spring Thing of 1102
At the spring Thing Lawspeaker Einar Greyhand recites the whole law of Northreach, as he has every spring since 1072, and judges four cases between jarls.
Serik Kharsan marries Naran of the Morning Wind
The khan's heir Serik marries Naran, daughter of Altan, chief of the Morning Wind, at Ozlun.
Rowena's summer in the Stag Downs
Princess Rowena leads 600 King's Bowmen through the Stag Downs against Ashen rioters and the smugglers of the Hawkmarch road.
Drowning of Pio Ferro
Pio Ferro, a clerk of an Ostran trading house in Lucerna, disappears. His body is found in the lagoon.
Fight at the Coldbarrow Bridge
War-Chief Vrag leads 1,200 riders against Nine Winds horse raiders at the Coldbarrow Bridge on the Salt Edge and breaks them with a blood-fury charge.
The Tandi song stops
At the Night of Masks at Tandi, the Tedana Rememberers sing the thirteen Tedana kings and Sefu, and leave out the Kanemba line for the first time since 930.
Prince Vikram's arsenic test
At the Festival of Lamps the temple testers give the nine-year-old Prince Vikram his yearly arsenic cup. He is reported well.
First meeting at the Lunetti table
Lady Cassia Mentis for Queen Livia and the clerk Milos Ternak for Prince Andros meet in secret at Ostra in the house of First Banker Cosimo Lunetti.
Maren tells Tarn
Maren of Hazelhollow tells her son Tarn, 29, that his father was Durgash Blood-Fist, son of Gorath, and gives him Durgash's copper arm-ring.
The firebreak of Evenglade
Eldest Keeper Arannel marks 40 km of firebreak around Evenglade, the largest cutting in memory.
The trip-hammer at Saltbridge
A new water-driven trip-hammer begins working at a smithy of Saltbridge in the jarldom of Halvard Stagg.
The tally stones cut
No public record.
The Marad children taken
Riders of House Zarani of Sabra carry off about 30 children from the Clan Marad border camps and sell them at Zaran as Veld-born slaves.
Birth of the infant Nuru
Princess Laila bears Prince Amani a son, named Nuru for his grandfather. Sultan Iskandar sends a gold cradle.
The pit at Mirona
Shepherds of Lord Cato Brennus break into a pit outside Mirona's old wall and find 22 hanged men still wearing Solenne-made bronze belt buckles.
The horn cup sold and the road loan
Mosi III sells his father's unicorn horn cup to Sultan Zahir IV of Qadir, borrows 100,000 suns from House Sorondo and names Nia Tembo Road-Master.
The Ironjaw bounty
On Sea Opening the insurers of House Bassan post a bounty of 5,000 Lucernan crowns for the death of the leviathan Old Ironjaw.
Tarn Halfblood's Rising
Tarn Halfblood leads about 600 half-orcs in Aldmark's southern march. They burn House Harrow's tax barns at Hazelhollow and Copperham and flee across the…
The burning at Fenny Ford
A month after Tarn Halfblood's rising, Isa Ravenscar's Night Riders burn a half-orc farmstead at Fenny Ford near Hazelhollow and kill the family of seven…
The lamp-oil bargain
King Aurelio II agrees with Khan Ozbek to let 30 jars a year of steppe fire-oil pass through Morhaven to Queen Livia, marked as lamp oil, for about 60 suns a…
Fight at the Well of Buroth
In the spring three mares are stolen from the war-chief's hearth herd at Urgol. Blaming Salt Wind raiders, Vrag rides out in August and catches a Salt Wind…
Collapse of the deep south shaft
The deep south shaft at Kabale collapses. Lady Amara Kabale reports 40 dead to the emperor.
The Lavium salt strike
About 800 salt-workers and millers of the Lavium flats strike after House Bassan raises its milling toll.
Andros takes Doria
The civil war resumed in 1096 when Livia broke the Truce of the Cedars at Felina. In 1103, after a siege of ten weeks, Andros takes the southern town of Doria,…
Flood in the Deep Gallery
Water breaks into the Deep Gallery of the Brightwash copper mines at Mossreach and drowns nine men. The richest gallery in Ashmere fills to the roof.
Severin III falls ill
High Luminary Severin III falls ill in the winter of 1103 with a short breath and swollen ankles and does not leave Solenne again.
The Seekers of the Rider
At the Winter Count at Dushdush, Uzka Twoblood, 24, calls the half-orcs of the Tusk Clans to follow Tarn Halfblood as the rider born of two peoples.
Jotunhall goes short
In the winter of 1103 Jotunhall runs short of grain and seal fat and its humans go hungry, while Valdhall's grain pits stay full.
Meera Jalan dragged from the temple steps
Temple guards drag the One Face preacher Meera Jalan from the steps of the Great Temple. About 3,000 people follow her home through the streets of Ranpur.
Betrothal of Prince Harald and Princess Rowena
At Kingsmere, Aldmark's heir Prince Harald, 26, is betrothed to Ashmere's heir Princess Rowena, 33. The wedding is set for Return Day 1105.
Abbot Tashen falls ill
Abbot Tashen, 52, begins to cough blood in the spring of 1104. Steward Sonam doubles the guard on his rooms and stores two years of barley.
The Reef Crossbows hired to Queen Livia
Captain-General Nell Brine hires Captain Brann Hollow's 400 Reef Crossbows to Queen Livia for the rest of 1104 and all of 1105, half paid now and half by…
Shara's rhino trial
Shara Ironhide, 18, heir of the War-Mother, faces her rhino in the Tuknak valleys and is given her right to speak in council.
The Clean Ledger founded
Lady Flavia Morello and about a dozen council families form the Clean Ledger to open the Doge's strongroom and expose hidden payments.
Vrag's oath at the Drum Stones
At the Great Ride, Vrag refuses Aldmark's demand to hand over Tarn Halfblood. He calls Tarn a guest of the fire.
The War-Mother faints at Grakmar
At the Great Ride at Grakmar, War-Mother Urza Ironhide, 38, goes into her tent at noon and faints from the heat.
The omen of the cracked bone
At the Horse Feast the chief shaman burns a sheep's shoulder-blade for the khan's road. Ilga reads it aloud as a long road.
Three Salt Road wells fail
The wells of Najifa, Halis and Azar on the Salt Road between Zarak and Mirah give only mud by July. Southern herds must water at Bahar-held wells.
The missing jar
On Dragon Night, while the fire-rafts burn in the harbor, one sealed jar of Sabran fire-oil is taken from the Ratrock caves.
Tin loaded at Ragvik by night
A Kingsmere cog of the Amber Guild loads 200 bars of tin at Ragvik by night with Chieftain Skarvi's leave.
A robber killed above Starspire
On the circuit above Starspire the Bluewater warden captain Dorje Stonesling kills a Red Stair robber with a sling stone to the temple.
A new silver vein under Redford
Dwarf crews driving a drainage tunnel under the Redford valley find a rich new vein of silver.
Tusk riders ride west to Tarn
About 120 riders from three Tusk clans ride west to see Tarn Halfblood at Gashmar, paid with 400 suns of Horde silver that Uzka Twoblood took from Brak…
The two journeymen vanish
Two paper-mill journeymen, Adil and Hakim Warraqi, leave Qadira hidden in rag bales.
The Road Promise
In his even-year reign, King Yonas of Abara grants Zanara a road through Tamowa and Koyako to the Monuti for a toll of one part in twenty.
The drum at Harvest Home
At the Harvest Home feast a war-drum sounds under the feast-hall window and Princess Ludmila collapses in front of the lords. She suffers two days of ringing.
Two Clarente beams sold north
Sir Tobias Merel secretly sells two roof beams of the old Clarente granary to a buyer paying in Eldergrove silver.
Drevnan envoys at Greyhaven
Envoys of Queen Milena of Drevna come to Greyhaven to ask for Lady Linnet Tidewell's hand for Prince Yaromir.
The Channel-Master buys eight hulls
Channel-Master Radek Volan buys eight condemned hulls at Sevany, three of them old Greyhaven cogs, and sails them south to a creek that runs from the Dobava…
The drowned prospectors
A prospecting shaft sunk by Emeric Vane's Iron Road Company in the hills east of the Ore Shelf floods; three human miners drown.
Dead Frost Leviathan on the Torvik capes
Solvei of Torvik finds a dead Frost Leviathan stranded on the northern capes with three Drevnan iron harpoon heads in its back. She hides one head in her hall.
The Marshal's camp at Atani
Marshal Juma Kanemba camps at Atani with 6,000 spearmen and 800 horse to guard 11,000 laborers cutting the east road.
The lean flood of 1104
The flood-priests read the Flood Stairs and declare the flood of 1104 lean. The grain tax is set at a tenth.
Battle of Coreria
Livia's 7,000 men try to retake the road to Doria and meet Andros's 6,500 at Coreria. About 1,800 die. Neither side gives way, and Andros winters at Coreria.
The Gordush contract offered
Aldmark's envoys ask the Highland League for 2,000 crossbowmen on the Gordush by May Fair 1105, at double the usual pay.
The Nagora toll farm sold
Chief Minister Sanjay Dhar sells the right to collect the Nagora tolls for 1105 to 1107 to a ring of Amberport merchants for 60,000 lotus paid in advance.
The 1106 cloves pledged
Grand Vizier Rahim Sulong pledges the whole clove crop of 1106 to House Doravelli of Lucerna for a new loan of 150,000 suns to pay for the Isle of Pearls war.
Gold for Chanari blades
Steward Sonam sends 18 kg of gold dust from the lamp treasury south with the Keeper of the Salt's salt train to buy 40 Chanari blades from Ravi Lohar's smiths.
The physician's tablets copied
The scrivener Amadeo Rusk enters the Temple archive at night with the Lantern Guard captain's key and copies the Tessarian royal physician's wax tablets onto…
The Dunheim seam floods
The lower coal seam at Dunheim floods. Mine-Master Dain Coalbrow tells the Council it is a small leak.
The dragon above Kardeep
The Kardeep Dragon Watch shoots a young Great Ash Dragon out of the air above the gold mines, and it dies.
Brak Longwind in Aldwin's camp
Brak Longwind crosses the lower Gordush under a green branch and carries a private message from Vrag to Emperor Aldwin's camp.
The Gashmar ferry burned
An Aldmark rope ferry at the Gashmar fords is burned at night.
Whitehorn riders burn two farms
Whitehorn riders burn two Drevnan farms that had crept past the Thardush cairns west of Sevmir. A family of six dies in one of them.
Fire at Zariya
A boiling-shed at Zariya burns at night. Eleven slaves die, three escape in the smoke, and a Varennan ship off the coast sees the fire.
The well at Red Hollow
Surveying water points for Zanara's east road, the guide Khalid the Star finds a new well at Red Hollow.
The harbor dues pawned
Prince Amani pawns the harbor dues of Kesh for 1105 to an Amber merchant house for 40,000 suns to pay the interest on the League's loan.
The king falls in the Lion Hall yard
King Roderic III, 42, falls to his knees gasping with chest pain in the practice yard of the Lion Hall. Two knights carry him indoors.
The spinner crosses to Crowbrook
Sabina of Camia, a Palella spinner fleeing her husband, crosses into Ashmere at Crowbrook with the spindle and flyer of a spinning wheel and a drawing of its…
Andros's offer to the taster
Prince Andros's chancellor Basil Ordane secretly offers Queen Livia's food-taster, Nerio Doravelli, 5,000 crowns to let one dish pass.
The rye held at Sevmir
Lord Marshal Vadim Zorac holds the 2,000 bushels of winter rye owed to the Tusk Clans at Sevmir, saying the roads are unsafe.
Queen Brynja's letter to Aldwin
A sealed letter goes from the Deep Halls to Kingsmere.
Asta's letter to the First Hall
A sealed letter leaves the Breath Halls for Stonehold.
Rahotep's letter to Andros
General Rahotep Kadari sends Nakht the Oar up the Neck road with a secret letter to Prince Andros at Coreria: ten river galleys and a copy of the Kadah order…
Greyhaven's Midwinter Vigil of the Dragon
On Midwinter night the priests of Greyhaven hold the last rite before 1105, the year the Black Dragon is due to rise. Thousands keep watch on the harbor walls.
Thora's oath at the Kindling
At the Kindling of 1104, as every forge is relit from the First Hall's fire, Eldest Carver Thora Grimstone declares that the crucible steel of Chanari is too…
clock: The Lake Council of Drevna hears Dorn Twotongue argue for the 2,000 bushels of withheld rye; Pavel Brodar asks the council to set Ludmila aside
New Year's Day: rents and debts reckoned, tax rolls opened; the Hungry Year's dead counted at Tamar
King Yared's voiding of the Road Promise takes effect at dawn: Gebre Tsega holds Tamowa with 8,000 against Juma Kanemba's 12,000 at Atani
Lantern Night: the Ostran draft treaty (partition of the Neck) must be out of Cosimo Lunetti's study and on its way to Velgrad
Lantern Night: Return Day candle wax must be ordered; Ada Tallow's wax comes smuggled from Dawn Church Drevna
Tamar's 1105 river gift due to Abara in silver by King Yared's demand (wheat, linen and papyrus under the pact)
Queen Brynja's secret promise: 400 Aldmark soldiers may stay at the lower Iron Road fort from 1 March for 6,000 bushels of grain
The Founding at the First Hall of Stonehold: Thora Grimstone calls Emberdeep's Carvers to answer for the Chanari Compact; Korrin means to have the Law-Carvers declare his mother unfit
Well Day at the Well of Samar: Tariq Bahar threatens to read the sealed water-contract of Zahir aloud unless Qadir pays 20,000 suns;
Spring Equinox Moot at Ashmere: King Edric's new testament; Rowena demands to read her marriage contract with its hidden clause
Spring Equinox quarter day: rents due; Queen Livia's hired companies are owed about 90,000 suns a month and half paid
Sea Opening: open-sea sailing begins. Sultan Iskandar's fleet (about 6,200 men, with Keshi ships) sails for the Isle of Pearls
Sea Opening: Lark Shoalwise sells the stamped Sabran fire-oil jar to Qadir's Master of Doors
Sea Opening: Grand Admiral Jalal sails on Sabra with 34 galleys (12 rotting), waters at Mirad and runs the Bone Coast; Tahir Sabrani plans to burn the fleet at Miruma first
Sea Opening: the oath for Linnet Tidewell's marriage to Prince Yaromir Dravic is due; Yaromir secretly married Alena Birchwood on 22 September 1104
Sea Opening: Admiral Castellan asks Lucerna for 20 galleys against Blackreef and sails; Kamal the Eel carries the two paper journeymen to Marira
Sea Opening: galleys out on both shores of the Grey Channel; Velgrad's eight fire-raft hulls lie fitted below Mount Dobava

May Fair: armies may march. Prince Andros marches on Tessar with about 13,000 and his siege towers (up to 20,000 if Velgrad sends more); the Ostran partition must be signed before this day to stop him
May Fair: Orla of Hazelhollow means to burn the stakes and wagons in the Hartgate depot before this day; Oswin Gordale carries the half-orcs' petition to Kingsmere
May Fair: the Gordush crossbow contract. Aldmark needs the League's 4,000 crossbowmen on the line by now; the vote at Highcastle decides it
May Fair: Tekle Asfari must win his release from Queen Livia before she marches after this day; Mesfin Mandari raises the Horsemen of the Monundi with Zanari gold
Lord Garrick Harrow means to cross the Gordush with 4,000 lances and Prince Harald, seize Tarn Halfblood and present the Emperor with a war already won
Return Day: Prince Harald of Aldmark marries Princess Rowena of Ashmere at Kingsmere, sworn on the iron ring or by the Sun rite; afterwards Ashmere passes 1,000 elven yew staves a year to Aldmark
Return Day: the Great Ride at the Drum Stones. Harkun judges whether Tarn Halfblood is the rider of two peoples; Maren of Hazelhollow swears Tarn is Durgash's son;
Return Day: the Tusk Great Ride at Grakmar. Uzka Twoblood wants Tarn there; Bolg means to denounce her; Ashka Drumtongue carries a copy of the Grey Mothers' hide toward Grakmar
Midsummer: the Thing of Hrimfell chooses its next king. Mother Asta names Ulfar; Arvo Sealbane asks for a human seat; Solvei of Torvik carries a harpoon head of Drevnan iron
Return Day: the Horse Feast of the Nine Winds. Yesun of the Red Wind needs the Well tribes' votes to block Serik; the cords of the Forty Silent Days lie in Khatun Sorga's chest
Return Day quarter day: the Reef Crossbows' half-year pay; Lord Dmitar Kovar has offered double to bring them to Andros
From 1 July Brightwater keeps 30 galleys behind the Greyhaven chain with crews aboard every dusk and the Tide Divers at the harbor mouth
The Harvest of the Mother at Tamar: Faruq the Lamp is paid to preach any confession from the Flood Stairs
Sea Closing: ships laid up; open-sea contracts end. Jalal's fleet, Castellan's galleys and the Isle of Pearls fleet must be home or wintering abroad
Slaughter Feast: servants' and companies' yearly contracts end and renew; the Reef Crossbows' year with Queen Livia runs to the end of 1105
Midwinter Vigil: Greyhaven's Vigil of the Dragon; the Kindling at Stonehold, where Thora Grimstone's oath of 1104 falls due
songs: The Noon of the Return
Solenfolk and every Temple land; children sing it on Lantern Night.

Seven years the sky was grey,
seven years no golden day.
Corvan stood and raised his hand,
and noon came back to Solen land.
The Miracle of Morhaven
The Kingdom of Morhaven's hymn for 2 October.

The Hawk came down with a thousand wings,
the walls were thin and the wells ran dry.
Our king knelt down and the noon sun rose,
and the Hawk lay down to die.
The Lay of Hartgate
Hall-singers of the Empire of Aldmark.

Stand, said the Iron King, stand by the stake,
let the grey tide break as the grey tides break.
Eighteen thousand came at noon,
and few rode home by the light of the moon.
The Lay of the Winter Crossing
The Kingdom of Northreach.

Over the ice in the dark of the year,
eight hundred went and none knew fear.
The emperor's barns made a bonfire bright,
and the Sea King sang to us all that night.
The Diver and the Chain
The Kingdom of Greyhaven; a diving rhyme for harbor children.

Down, down, the Diver's crown,
under the chain where the riders drown.
Hold your breath and count to ten,
and up comes Greyhaven's king again.
Elsbeth's Night March
Ballads of the Kingdom of Ashmere.

The queen she never closed her eyes,
the bowmen never lay;
we walked the night to the Brightwash ford
and shot the lions at break of day.
Hild on Roktar
The Highland League; yodeled between valleys.

Hild went up where the eagles go,
up through the ice and over the snow.
She sat on the top of the world one day,
and came back down and would not say.
The Listener
The Kingdom of Drevna; "speak low, the queen is listening" is a saying.

Hush by the hearth and hush by the door,
the Listener hears through the wall and the floor.
Whisper your secret into the snow,
and the queen in Drevna will know.
The Forty Silent Days
A long song of the Khanate of the Nine Winds.

The Khan lay still and the wind lay still,
the snow lay white on the Kharsa hill.
Saran counted the stars by night,
and the morning rose with the Khan's own light.
The Thunder Horse
Drummers of the Horde of Gorath.

Thunder in the grass and thunder in the sky,
the black horse ran and the stones stood by.
Gorath rode where the lightning goes,
Storm's own son, as the whole grass knows.
Tukar's Run
Every orc clan; "run like Tukar" means do what cannot be done.

Three days, three nights, no fire, no bread,
Tukar ran and the camps were fed.
Ask the grass where the riders went:
they burned the wind and an empty tent.
Samar and the Rock
The Path of the Well, on Well Day.

He struck the stone in the burning land
with a dry staff in a dry hand.
The Giver heard and the rock gave way,
and we drink from his well to this day.
The Runner Who Never Tires
Praise-singers of the Empire of Zanara, as call and answer.

Who is the wind? Mosi is the wind.
Who is the dawn at Kisara's gate? Mosi is the dawn.
The night is long.
The Runner is longer.
The Unpoisoned
The Kingdom of Ranpur, at the Festival of Lamps.

Seven cups and seven lamps,
seven times the poison came.
Seven times the Raja drank,
and lit a lamp in the gods' name.
Durek's Road
All three holds; in the Kingdom of Emberdeep no child is named Durek.

Forty-one went up the road,
forty-one with the iron load.
Down came the fire with never a sign,
and Durek stood at the head of the line.
Sethril the Unwounded
The elves of the Kingdom of Sylvaran; the Sunlands tell it darker.

Leaf on the water, light on the blade,
four hundred years and never afraid.
He lay down under the oak to sleep,
and the oak keeps what it has to keep.
The Parting Song
The Kingdom of Eldergrove, on Leaf Fall; Sylvaran never sings it.

We left the oaks that never move
for the grey road and the sea we love.
Sing, sister, on the falling leaf,
a short farewell for a long grief.
Dragon Night
The Brotherhood of Blackreef, and every sailor who pays the toll.

Pay the dragon, pay the toll,
one in forty for your soul.
Mag Brine laughed and the sea caught flame,
and the dragon came when he called its name.
The Ferryman of the Tirana
The Marchfolk, over drink.

Ferryman, ferryman, what's your fee?
A copper for you and a copper for me.
Why won't you take the emperor's sun?
Because I know whose face is on it, son.
Grom's Whale
Giants of the Kingdom of Hrimfell and the Halls of Frostholm.

Slow, slow, the ice is wide.
Slow, slow, the whale is dead.
Grom pulls, and the halls are fed.
Slow, slow, by the Mother's side.
sayings: "Don't lie at noon."
Solenfolk of the Holy See of Solenne and the Kingdom of Varenna
Be honest when it counts. From the Temple's taboo on lying at noon, the holy hour.
"A hearth that dies at Midwinter is a house that dies in spring."
Solen farm families
Keep up the small duties or lose the big things. From the Midwinter Vigil taboo.
Lex scripta manet. "Written law stands."
Lawyers and clerks of the Sunlands
A written contract beats a spoken promise. From the Twelve Books.
"The Needle counts, and the Needle is never wrong."
Priests and schoolboys of the Holy See
Said to end a quarrel over dates. The few who know the six missing years say it without smiling.
"Bite the coin, not the banker."
Moneychangers of the Free City of Ostra
Test the goods, not the man's face. Coins are worth their metal, not their name (6.2).
"A black cap never forgets a penny."
Ostra's harbor folk
Debts to the bankers in black caps are never forgiven, only rolled over.
"Every lamp has its oil."
Harbor cant of the Republic of Lucerna
Every informer (a *lamp*) has a paymaster. Old sailors hear a second meaning: "lamp oil" is fire-oil.
"Iron does not lie."
Northfolk of the Empire of Aldmark
An oath sworn on the iron ring binds. Used of any solemn promise.
"Ask the Fairrush."
Kingsmere
A threat: oath-breakers are drowned in the Fairrush. Never said in front of an Ironside, because of the whispered prophecy of an Ironside in the water.
"Stand by the stake."
Aldmark soldiers
Hold your ground behind your defenses. From Hartgate, 1051.
"Seven years and the field is yours."
Ashwater yeomen of the Kingdom of Ashmere
Patience earns ownership. From the Ashwater Charter (17.3.2).
"Sleep is for Varennans."
Ashmere's bowmen
Keep going while the enemy rests. From Elsbeth's night march of 1014.
"Salt in the beard, silver in the hand."
Fishermen of the Kingdom of Northreach
Hard work at sea pays.
"Ask the Lawspeaker."
Northreach
Settle it by law, not by blows. The whole law lives in one man's head.
"A fixed sum can't be cheated."
Clansfolk of the Highland League
Prefer plain terms to fair-sounding shares. From Bran Greycloak's charter (17.3.1).
"Hire the cloak, not the crown."
Highland and Sunland captains
Pay for proven soldiers, not for a great name. The Greycloak crossbow companies are the best hired foot in the Known World.
"Hold your breath and count to ten."
Harbor children of the Kingdom of Greyhaven
Be patient under pressure. From the diving rhyme of Osric.
"The dragon comes every thirty-four years, the toll comes every day."
Greyhaven merchants
Fear the steady cost more than the rare terror.
"Speak low, the queen is listening."
The Kingdom of Drevna
Be careful what you say and where. From Ludmila the Listener.
Koliko za sobol? "How much for the sable?"
Traders of the Kingdom of Velgrad and Drevna
Let's talk price. Everything can be bought.
"The lamp is not the Light."
Dawn Church folk
Don't mistake the sign for the thing, or the office for the man.
