Kun kok, at semiz. "The sky is blue, the horse is fat."
Wind Riders of the Khanate of the Nine Winds
All is well.
"War and enemy are one word."
Wind Riders
*Jau* means both. Make an enemy and you have made a war.
"A tally cord forgets nothing."
Yam families of the Nine Winds
Records outlive the men who wish them gone. The cords of 912 still lie in the khan's chest.
Dush ka? Dush ha. "Is there water? There is water."
Every orc
The guest's greeting and the host's answer under the Law of the Fire. To answer *nakh* is the worst insult an orc can give.
"Run like Tukar."
Every orc clan
Do what cannot be done. From Tukar's run of 1046.
"A guest is not given."
The Horde of Gorath
Never hand over someone under your roof. Vrag said it of Tarn Halfblood in 1104.
"No chief is holy."
The League of the Tusk Clans
Distrust any leader who says the gods chose him. Aimed at the Line of Gorath.
"Count the rye before you thank the Drevnan."
Tusk clan-mothers
Check what you are given. Drevna calls its yearly rye a gift; both sides know it is tribute.
Vael, vael. "Slowly, slowly."
Elves to humans
What is right is not hurried. Humans hear it as "you are too quick to die".
"Ask the tree's pardon."
The Kingdom of Sylvaran
Be courteous to whatever you take from. Elves say it before felling a tree, and to a human about to make a deal.
"A human's promise lasts as long as a human."
Elves
Human promises are short. It is why elves want treaties sealed and kept for centuries.
"Even an oak floats once it's cut."
The Kingdom of Eldergrove
Things can change their nature. The Grovers' answer to Sylvaran purists.
Ristet er rett. "What is carved is law."
Dwarves of every hold
It is settled; stop arguing.
Hald fast. "Hold fast."
Dwarves
The greeting at a gate, answered *Fast hald*. Also: endure.
"Two names, one bar."
Dwarven smiths and traders
A partnership binds both. From the molten-metal oath of a dwarven contract.
"Slow, slow, the ice is wide."
Giants of the Halls of Frostholm and the Kingdom of Hrimfell
A long task is done by steady work. From the song of Grom's whale.
"Waste nothing of the whale."
Giants and their tribute-folk
Use everything you are given. Every whale is an ancestor coming home.
Al-bir la yakdhib. "The well does not lie."
Qadiri and every Well people
Facts speak.
"Give water to your enemy, and he drinks from your hand."
The Sultanate of Qadir
Generosity is a kind of power. From the law of water-alms.
"A Rider counts stars, a Well counts coins."
Sandfolk of the Confederacy of the Sand Clans
The desert clans mock the town folk of the Sultanate of Qadir and the Emirate of Sabra. From the split of 581.
"The diver comes up, or he doesn't."
Pearl divers of Sabra
Take the risk whole, knowing its price. No half measures.
Moy en Mut. "Water of the Mother."
Tamari of the Kingdom of Tamar
Said when the flood rises, and of anything left in the gods' hands.
"Three low floods, no king."
Tamari farmers, in whispers
Even a living god depends on the river. From the flood law; never said near a flood-priest since 1089.
"A name not spoken fades."
Zanari of the Empire of Zanara
Remember your dead; and a reputation must be told to live.
Uko? Niko. "Are you there? I am here."
Zanari
The greeting. Also: show up, be counted.
"Pepper pays where silver sleeps."
Merchants of the League of the Spice Coast
Goods are money where coin is short. A kilo of pepper is worth 30 suns.
Hulet zewd, and ager. "Two crowns, one land."
The Kingdom of Abara
Said at the New Year handover. Also said with a shrug of any bargain that holds only because both sides are tired.
"The cord knows."
Abari
The truth is knotted somewhere even if nobody shows it. Prince Tekle's people say it pointedly.
Svapna chale. "The dream goes on."
Ranpuri of the Kingdom of Ranpur
Life goes on after a disaster. Said at the Monsoon Welcome.
"Seven cups, and the Raja still drinks."
Ranpur
Luck holds until it doesn't. From Vikram the Unpoisoned.
Ribut datang. "The storm is coming."
Amberfolk of the Sultanate of the Amber Isles
Danger ahead. Said in earnest when a Maruang has a headache.
"The pilot's bowl is not for looking."
Amber Isles sailors
Some craft secrets are not asked about. The pilots guard their lodestone bowl.
"Three and one."
Skyfolk of the Abbey of Skyhold
Said instead of "four", which is also "death". Names a danger without naming it.
Ri la, chu la. "To the peak, to the water."
Pilgrims on the Bluespire circuit
Keep walking. Used for any long, hard road.
"One in forty for your soul."
Corsairs of the Brotherhood of Blackreef, and the sailors who pay them
Everything has a price, and the price is set by the strong. From the dragon toll.
"The tide judges."
Blackreef
Let the consequences decide. From the Drowning Post.
"No blade in sight of the saint."
Marchfolk of the Free Marches
Keep the peace at meetings. A saint's grave is neutral ground.
"A copper for the ferryman, never a sun."
Marchfolk
Don't trust a coin with a lord's face on it; stay free. From the song of the Tirana ferryman.
"Take one, not two."
Leaf People of the Deep Green
Never take more than you need. From their hunting song (17.1, REL-16).
